document_title: Investigation of Road Accidents of cases and Guidelines regarding Motor Accident Claim Tribunal
text: STANDING ORDER NO. L&O/72/2024 INVESTIGATION OF ROAD ACCIDENTS OF CASES AND GUIDELINES REGARDING MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIM TRIBUNAL INTRODUCTION In order to ensure quick response, proper and scientific investigation of road accident cases, following instructions are hereby laid down for strictly adherence by IOs and supervisory officers. SECTION- I 1. PRELIMINARY STAGE (i) INFORMATION ON ACCIDENTS As soon as information of a road accident is received in the Central Police Control Room (CPCR), the same should be communicated to the nearest MPV quickly for the removal of the injured to the nearest hospital for immediate medical attention. In case the information is received directly in the police station, the nearest MPV should be dispatched immediately. In all accident cases, the Central Police Control Room (CPCR) shall immediately inform the Traffic Control Room which shall, in turn, direct the area Traffic Inspector/Zonal Officer to reach the accident site immediately. Any person, who brings an accident victim to a hospital or a nursing home for medical aid shall not be subjected to any harassment. In special cases, they should be recommended for suitable rewards. The concerned Police official(s) shall allow the Good Samaritan to leave after having informed the Police person about the accident. No further questions shall be asked if the Good Samaritan does not desire to be a witness in the matter. In case a Good Samaritan so chooses to be a witness, he shall be examined with utmost care and respect and without any discrimination on the ground of gender, religion, nationality, caste or any other grounds. Concerned IO will follow the Central Government Guidelines for protection of the Good Samaritan published on 21st January, 2016 in the Gazette notification in India. In cases where the injured persons are trapped in the vehicle, Disaster Management Cell should be immediately informed for safe evacuation and any other contingency including fire. 1 (ii) INVESTIGATION OFFICER KIT The following equipment shall be carried by the IOs while proceeding to the scene of accident: -  First Aid Box.  Torch light (during night only).  Measuring tapes cotton 100 feet.  Steel measuring tapes.  Crime Investigation Box.  Sheets of Papers, pencils of various colors, carbon paper sand Fountain pen.  Blank Case diaries.  Camera fitted with flash light unit.  Audio-video recording device preferably mobile phone for recording at accident site. If the Crime Team is unavailable or delayed, the officers investigating accident cases may ‘avail the services of a professional private photographer and take photographs of the site of the accident from all angles. Expenditure for the same may be met from the Imprest Fund. (iii) INSPECTION OF THE SPOT In all accident cases, whether fatal or simple - the professional and scientific Inspection of the spot is crucial. The Skid-marks indicate the probable speed of vehicle(s) and can he of great help to investigating officers in arriving at some pertinent conclusions The direction(s) of the vehicles involved in the accident, condition of the road, whether one-way or two-way,

(iii) INSPECTION OF THE SPOT In all accident cases, whether fatal or simple - the professional and scientific Inspection of the spot is crucial. The Skid-marks indicate the probable speed of vehicle(s) and can he of great help to investigating officers in arriving at some pertinent conclusions The direction(s) of the vehicles involved in the accident, condition of the road, whether one-way or two-way, road-curve, visibility at the time of the accident, existence of speed-breakers or potholes on the road, Skid-marks etc. should invariably find mention in the Spot Inspection Note (Mauka-Mulahiza) of the case diary. The Investigating Officer shall also conduct spot enquiry by examining the eye- witnesses/by standers, if any. The Crime team along with forensic expert be called on the spot for lifting samples, skid marks and other exhibits. CCTV footage of the Camera installed at the location, if any be also collected. The MPVs fitted with cameras shall also preserve their footage from the place of incidence. Scene of crime should be visited by the SHO/ Inspr. Investigation to guide the IO on the spot. The IOs should also collect the traces of paint imprints, for linkage with offending vehicles. (iv) MECHANICAL INSPECTION The mechanical inspection officer shall prepare separate Mechanical Inspection Report for each vehicle involved in the accident as 2 per Form No. IX of Scheme for Motor Accident Claim. As far as possible the mechanical inspection of the vehicles should be done at the spot itself. If the vehicle(s) involved in the accident are causing hindrance in the smooth flow of traffic, it is advisable to remove them to one side. The IO should note down the details of damages to the vehicles(s) involved in an accident, such as area of damage, extent of damage, point of impact between the vehicles, and see if there are paint-marks or any other evidence transferred from one vehicle to another at the time of impact. He should bring it on record through his observations mentioned in the endorsement of the ruqqa, statements of witnesses, photographs, video etc. The Mechanical Inspection Report should include the status of tyre condition, brake and whether the vehicle is fit for Road or otherwise. If the Mechanical Inspector or any other expert is not readily available at the spot, it should be got done in the Police Station. The vehicles should be released only after their mechanical inspection has been completed. The Hon’ble High Court has directed the Transport Department, GNCT of Delhi to appoint Mechanical Inspectors for the inspection of the vehicle(s) involved in the accident. The process of their appointment is under consideration with GNCT of Delhi. Till their appointment, the present system of mechanical inspection will continue. There are professional private Mechanical Inspectors whose services can be availed and their fee may be got reimbursed from the investigation fund. (v) FORENSIC EXAMINATION In fatal accident cases, efforts should be made by the IOs to trace out and seize all relevant evidence in an appropriate manner. Where necessary, a forensic expert attached with the district or forensic expert from FSL, should be requisitioned at the spot to examine the scene of accident. The vehicle(s) and the exhibits should be collected carefully by the IO with the help of Crime Team and ‘sent to the FSL for an opinion. In accident cases particularly fatal accident, where there are no eye witnesses such evidence could be crucial. This task shall be closely supervised by the SDPO/concerned ACP (Sub Division). (vi) SITE PLAN The Investigation Officer of Police Station shall inspect ‘the site of accident and prepare a site plan, drawn to scale, as to indicate the lay- out and width, etc., of the road(s) or place, as the case may be, the position of vehicles (s), and person(s) involved, and such other facts as may be relevant so as to preserve the evidence in this regard. In the case of an accident, properly drawn site plan renders far more valuable evidence than the oral testimony of witnesses as the site plan speaks a lot of facts itself. A site plan shall be prepared according to scale which should indicate the positions and in which the vehicles were found, point 3 of impact, position of the deceased, skid marks (with dimensions}, width of the road, directions of vehicle(s) involved, central verge or road-divider, lamp-post, traffic lights/signals, CCTV camera, etc and position of CCTV camera, if any. The position of eye witness shall be specifically mentioned depending on the circumstances of the case in the site plan itself. The investigating officer may, if necessary, requisition the services of a qualified draftsman at the scene of accident. Different colour markings could also be used to describe any other circumstances/ evidence having. a bearing on the case. If the site plan has been prepared at the instance of an eye witness, their signature should be recorded on the site plan. (vii) PHOTOGRAPHY AND VIDEOGRAPHY An IO need to take photographs and video of the spot himself or he may take assistance of the official or a professional photographer. The relevant tyre marks/skid marks should be photographed & videographed after placing a chit near them bearing the details of the case and signatures of the witnesses present at spot for subsequent correlation. A scale bar to illustrate the length of the marks shall also be used while photographing. Damage caused by the vehicle’s on account of the accident should also

INVESTIGATION (i) RECORDING OF FIR If the condition of the injured person permits, his Statement should preferably form the basis of the FIR. The IO should keep in mind that the safety and life of the injured must receive precedence over any other task. The initial statement that forms the basis of the FIR and subsequent statements of witness(s)must mention the description of the accused, if identified including his name, mobile number, address and age. If accused is not found on the spot his approximate age, built, complexion, clothes worn be specifically mentioned. Description of the vehicles i.e make, registration number, colour etc. involved in the accident should be mentioned in the said information is known. The manner in which the driver of offending vehicle was rash and negligent be also specifically mentioned. No of passenger(s) in offending vehicles be also mentioned. (ii) FATAL CASES (a) Investigation by an Upper Subordinate of MACT Cell:- Fatal Accident Cases necessarily involve conducting inquest proceedings 4 and therefore, shall be investigated by an upper subordinate officer posted in MACT Cell of the district. The SHO shall ensure that the IO is well versed with the law and procedural requirements for conducting investigation of such cases. (b) Keeping dead bodies in body bags:- The IO while proceeding to the spot of a fatal accident shall also carry body bags and gloves supplied by the Makhanas to handle and carry the dead bodies. In no case, the body of the deceased shall be allowed to remain uncovered. Dead Body bags/Shrouds to be kept in MPV vans and the Police stations shall be procured centrally by the P&L Unit and supplied to all Districts/Units and stocks be replenished as per requirement. (c) Post-Mortem Examination:- Inquest papers i.e. brief facts, Form No. 25.35(B} PPR, identification statements, MLC, copies of FIR/DD entries, etc. should be filled in with due care and caution. The IO shall remain present at the time of the postmortem examination and after the same is over, the dead body be handed over to the relatives after re-identification under proper receipt. In all fatal hit and run cases where the offending vehicle is not known and also victim’s identity is not known till the time of Post mortem, the ACP/Sub-Division shall satisfy himself that the case is of road accident and

The Hon’ble Delhi High Court has mandated that the concerned hospital will issue the MLC and Post-mortem report within 15 days of the accident. (i) Possession of fake driving license etc:- If the driving license of the driver is found to be fake, the Investigating Officer shall prosecute the driver for holding a fake driving license and/or other persons involved in forging the fake driving license. Investigating officer will also check from RTO, if the driving license has been revoked or suspended by them. (j) Non-disclosure of information by driver(s), Owner(s), Insurance Company and/or Claimants:- In the event of failure of the driver(s), owner(s), Insurance Company and/or claimants to disclose the relevant information and documents required to complete the Detailed Accident Reports, the Investigating Officer shall seek necessary directions from the Claims Tribunal (Part X of the DAR format) whereupon the Claims Tribunal shall, in appropriate cases, direct the parties in default to disclose the relevant information on affidavit along with the original documents within 15 days. 3. PREPARATION OF CASE FILE The I.O should ensure that the memos or fards and statements of the witnesses are properly recorded. The investigation of all accident cases shall be completed at the earliest and chargesheet be submitted 8 thereafter without delay. All other directions concerning investigation contained in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, Bhartiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, MV Acts, Police Rules, Standing Orders, etc. shall be strictly complied with. It is advisable that in all fatal accidents, the Investigating Officer should visit the family of the victim(s) if they are located in Delhi, to inform them about the progress of the investigation of the case and the action taken by the police. If the victim resides out of Delhi, they may be informed telephonically about the progress of the investigation. They shall also arrange for equipment required to be carried by the IOs detailed on this duty. These articles should be kept ready/handy with the Duty Officer to avoid delay. In addition to the equipment indicated above stretchers shall also be taken to the spot, if necessary. These arrangements should be made by all the SHOs without fail. Fatal accidents or simple accidents involving physical injuries are to be necessarily dealt with u/s 281/106 of BNS 2023 or 281/125 of BNS 2023 as the case may be. After this, the vehicles are to be seized, the defaulting driver arrested, the mechanical inspection of vehicles done, Judicial TIP got conducted, if required. Finally, the charge sheet should be prepared and submitted in the Court. The following points are required to be taken note of while preparing charge sheet u/s 193 of BNSS 2023 in accident cases: (i) Permissible speed on the road where accident has taken place. (ii) Site plan indicating exact position of the vehicle and the victim involved in the accident. (iii) Condition of the street lights and whether sufficient light was there or otherwise. (iv) Number of vehicles and other road users on the road at the time of accident, viz. whether the road was crowded or otherwise. (v) Lane of the vehicle in which the accident took place (vi) Approximate speed of the erring vehicle. (vii) Whether the driver of erring vehicle was listening to mobile or he was talking to someone else sitting beside him. (viii) Width of the road and whether it had a central verge or otherwise. 9 (ix) Was there any speed breaker in close proximity. (x) Condition of the road including presence of potholes, dry or slippery due to rain etc. 4. The SHO shall ensure timely dispatch of the accident reports to the DCP/Traffic (HQ), Dev Prakash Shastri Marg, Pusa, New Delhi. All necessary information for analysis of cause of accident etc. will be provided by SHO to the Traffic Inspector. 5. MISCELLANEOUS INSTRUCTIONS: (i) Accident in which no injury is caused to any person but only vehicle(s) are damaged, can either be dealt with u/s 281 BNS 2023 or u/s 184/185 MV Act 1988 (as amended in 2019). These sections have almost the same thrust and effect. Though in cases where impact is quite severe causing heavy damages, the action should normally be taken u/s 281 BNS 2023. However, in simple accidents, prosecution u/s 184/185 MV Act 1988 (as amended in 2019) or other provisions of the MV Act should be preferred, so that unnecessary harassment is not caused to the concerned individuals. Such cases may not be many and can be easily identified by the supervisory officers. (ii) The police officer has no power to accept a compromise or ask the parties to enter into a compromise. The offence u/s 281 BNS 2023 10 and 184/185 MV Act 1988 (as amended in 2019) and other provisions of the MV Act, etc. is against the State and non- compoundable in Courts. (iii) Report / information of road accident, involving C.D. (diplomatic). cars, is to be sent to the Principal Secretary (Home), Govt. of N.C.T. of Delhi. DIRECTIONS OF HON’BLE HIGH COURT OF DELHI To ensure that police officers investigating accident cases conduct investigation in a professional manner, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, in a Revision Petition (Cri.) No. 114 of 2006 - Abdul Subhan Versus State (NCT of Delhi), has also issued certain directions for proper investigation of road accident cases. For the benefit of IOs, these guidelines are reiterated as under: (i) In most of the cases the site plans are not produced or the same are of a very unsatisfactory nature. It is imperative that the investigating officer should be provided with maps of the roads drawn to scale so that accurate site plans can be produced as 11 evidence before Courts. The exact point of impact as well as tyre skid marks and the point at which vehicles come to rest after the collision should be demarcated clearly. The length of the tyre skid marks of the vehicles involved in the impact indicate the speed at which the vehicles were travelling. This would enable the Courts to examine the evidence in a much more objective manner and the Courts would not have to face vague and subjective expressions, such as ‘high speed (ii) The case mechanical inspection reports that are prepared, in a majority of the cases are very superficial and of a cursory nature. The inspection ought to be conducted by qualified personnel who are able to indicate in their reports the exact physical condition of the vehicles. They should

text: This would enable the Courts to examine the evidence in a much more objective manner and the Courts would not have to face vague and subjective expressions, such as ‘high speed (ii) The case mechanical inspection reports that are prepared, in a majority of the cases are very superficial and of a cursory nature. The inspection ought to be conducted by qualified personnel who are able to indicate in their reports the exact physical condition of the vehicles. They should be able to point out exactly the damage suffered by the vehicles as a result of the impact during the accident. The mechanical inspection report should indicate all the tell-tale signs of the collision such as the paint of one vehicle rubbing off on the other. It should also indicate as to whether the vehicles were mechanically sound or not prior to the impact so as to enable the Court to arrive at a conclusion as to whether the collision took place due to human rashness or negligence or due to mechanical failure beyond human control. (iii) The photographs and video of the scene ought to be taken not only of the vehicles involved in the collision but also of the site and- surrounding areas so that the exact topography can be easily understood by the Courts. (iv) The prevalent weather conditions must be noted and mentioned by the investigating officer. This would establish situations like whether the road was slippery due to rain or otherwise, whether there was poor visibility due to fog or mist, etc. or otherwise. (v) The path of movement of the vehicles must be sought to be established during the course of investigation and should not be ambiguous and doubtful. (vi) The drivers of the vehicles involved must also be subjected to tests to reveal whether they had consumed any intoxicants. (vii) All elements of subjectivity need to be eliminated and the investigation should be such that, when a charge sheet is filed, the Court is presented with a case which when taken objectively should lead to the inescapable conclusion that a conviction is maintainable. 12 7. SUPERVISION OVER INVESTIGATION The concerned SHO and ACP shall be responsible for supervising the investigation and proper pairvi of such cases in Court. In fatal accidents, the scene of occurrence shall be visited by the concerned SHO/Inspector Investigation and concerned Traffic Inspector immediately or at the earliest. SECTION –II 1. RELEASE OF VEHICLES BELONGING TO ACCIDENTS VICTIMS: A. While disposing of Crl. WP No. 1476/2007, Arun Handa vs Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors., the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi has observed on 10.1.2008 that the petitioner was the victim of an accident while he was coming on his motorcycle and a bus overtaking the petitioner from the left, squeezed the petitioner between road divider and its body. text: Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors., the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi has observed on 10.1.2008 that the petitioner was the victim of an accident while he was coming on his motorcycle and a bus overtaking the petitioner from the left, squeezed the petitioner between road divider and its body. The petitioner was saved but his motorcycle suffered damages. Subsequently, a FIR was registered at PS Sarojini Nagar, the motorcycle of the petitioner was seized he was told to get it released form the court of Ld. MM. B. As the motorcycle of the petitioner was kept at Police Station for several days, he filed the aforesaid Criminal Writ Petition with the prayer that, where a victim of accident reports to the police about being hit by a bus and damage caused to his motorcycle, the same should be released to him after completing all formalities and furnishing a surety bond for producing the motorcycle before the trial Court as and when required. The Court observed that in all accident cases, the police should release the vehicle of the victim on executing a surety bond that he/she shall produce the same in the court as and when required and shall not dispose off the vehicle till the case is over. The police can give directions to the victim that he should execute a similar bond before the Court when the challan is filed. The Court has observed that if an accused in case u/s 281/125 or even 106 BNS 2023 can be released by the police on bail, then why cannot the vehicle of a complainant be released on the basis of surety given by him. The Court underscored that there has to be a different treatment given to the accused and the victim. A victim cannot be treated in the category of an accused. C. The issue of decongestion of Malkhanas of Police Stations and expeditious disposal of case properties has been deliberated upon by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India as well as Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in various judgments. OBLIGATIONS OF POLICE REGARDING MOTOR ACCIDENTS CLAIM TRIBUNAL & GUIDELINES REGARDING MOTOR ACCIDENTS CLAIM TRIBUNAL: (A) According to section 158(6) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), it is mandatory for the police (Investigating Officer) to send the Accident Information Report to the concerned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) within 30 days of registration of the FIR. Copies of the Accident Information Report are also required to be sent to the insurer and the owner of the offending vehicle with in the same time period. The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in their order dated 9.7.2007 in writ petition (C) No. 282 of 2007 “General Insurance Council & others Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh and others have specifically directed that the report should be sent within the shortest possible time but not later than 30 days of registration of FIR. The Hon’ble Supreme Court further observed that “the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019) is a beneficent/benevolent piece of legislation, seeking to provide quick monetary compensation to persons who sustain bodily injury/disablement, permanent or partial or to the legal heirs of the persons who die or sustain fatal injuries due to the use of motor vehicles in a public place.” Hit and Run cases’ details will be sent to concerned SDM within 30 days for compensation in view of GSR no. 163(E) issued by Ministry 14 of Road transport & Highways vide notification dated 25.02.2022 and judgement passed by Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in (W.P (C) No. 295 of 2012 titled as S. Rajaseekaran vs Union of India & Ors, judgement dated 12.01.2024). However, the Hon’ble Delhi High Courtin case No. FAO 842/2003 in the matter of Rajesh Tyagi & Or versus Jaibir Singh & Ors has laid down scheme for motor accident claims. In the said judgment dated 08.01.2021 duties have been cast upon police regarding preparation and submission of FAR and DAR before MACT and the following guidelines have been laid down by the Hon’ble Delhi High Court. The obligations cast upon police and guidelines laid down by the Hon’ble Court are given below: - (i) Investigation of Road Accidents by Police: On receipt of the information of a road accident, the Investigating Officer shall immediately inspect the site of accident; take photographs & Video of the scene of the accident and’ the vehicle(s) involved in the accident and prepare site plan, drawn to scale, as to indicate the layout and width, etc., of the road(s) or place(s), as the case may be; the position of vehicle(s) and person(s) involved; and such other facts as may be relevant. In injury cases, the Investigating Officer shall also take the photograph(s). of the injured in the hospital. The Investigating Officer shall conduct an on-the- spot enquiry by examining the eye witnesses/by standers. (ii) Form-I- First Accident Report (FAR) to be submitted by the Investigating Officer to the Claims Tribunal within 48 hours: The Investigating Officer shall intimate the accident to the Claims Tribunal by submitting First Accident Report (FAR)in Form-I within 48 hours of the receipt of intimation of the accident. If the particulars of insurance policy are available, the intimation of the accident in Form-I shall be given to the Nodal Officer of the concerned Insurance Company of the offending vehicle. The Investigating Officer shall furnish the copy of FAR to the victims. The Investigating Officer shall furnish the copy. of FAR. to Delhi State Legal Services Authority (DSLSA). The Investigating Officer shall upload FAR of the accident on the website www.dpacciclaim.in of Delhi Police. (iii) Form-II- Rights of Victim(s) of Road Accident and Flow Chart of this Scheme to be furnished by the Investigating Officer to the Victim(s) within 10 days: 15 The Investigating Officer shall furnish Form-II containing the description of Rights of Victim(s) of road accidents and flow chart of this Scheme to the victim(s) (injured/legal representatives of deceased) within 10 days of the accident against a written acknowledgement. Copy of Form-II containing the acknowledgement of the victim(s) shall be filed by the Investigating Officer before the Claims Tribunal along with Detailed Accident Report (DAR). (iv) Form-III- Driver’s Form to be submitted by the driver to the Investigating Officer within 30 days: The driver of the vehicle(s} involved in the accident shall furnish their relevant information namely his name, age, gender, income, driving license, period of validity of license, vehicle registration number, particulars of the owner and insurance of the vehicle, etc., to

text: DELHI POLICE SHANTI SEWA NYAYA Citizens' harter C Objective To prevent and detect crime; To pursue justice for all; To uphold the law fairly and firmly; To be seen to do all this with integrity To protect, help and reassure the people; To maintain peace in partnership with the community; To show compassion and patience. To act without fear, favour or prejudice; To accept suggestions with a willingness to change; To remain professional, calm and restrained in the face of violence; To apply only that force which is absolutely essential for our lawful duty. CITIZENS' CHARTER Police is an important part of the Criminal Justice System and broadly provide services which, interalia, are the Prevention and Detection of crime; and the Maintenance of Law and Order in civil society. The public has the right to complain to the police in case they are victims of any cognizable or non- cognizable offense. The public may also submit petitions to the police for redressal of their grievances. The Police Station, at the cutting edge of the Police Department, is the most important point of delivery of the services mentioned above. It has a defined jurisdictional territory as notified by the Government under the relevant law. The Police Station provides services to the public as defined in various laws and judgments of various courts delivered from time to time. Further details of services provided by police are asunder: 1. COGNIZABLE OFFENCE (a) If the complaint lodged falls under a Cognizable offense as per 154 Cr.P.C. then a case will be registered in the prescribed format "FIR" and a copy of the FIR will be given to the complainant free of cost after obtaining the signature of the complainant as acknowledgment (mandatory). FIR will be dispatched to the llaka Magistrate on the same day or on the next day depending on the time factor. A final report will be sent to court for disposal. (b) If the complaint pertains to the theft of a motor vehicle or property, the complainant will have the option to lodge an e-FIR by logging on to Delhi Police website https://delhipolice.gov.in. (c) The complainant has every right to enquire about the status of his complaint and its progress. The status of the investigation will be intimated by the investigating officer, if not otherwise engaged with any other urgent work. 2. NON-COGNIZABLEOFFENCE (a) If the complaint lodged falls under Non Cognizable offence as per section 155 Cr.P.C. suitable action will be taken as per law. (b) A non-cognizable report (NCR) can also be electronically lodged for lost articles/ documents/property by logging on to the Delhi Police website https://delhipolice.gov.in. 3. text: BEST PRACTICES IN DELHI POLICE Delhi Police has taken a number of digital initiatives in keeping with the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s directives regarding SMART policing. Technological upgradation has been given top priority in order to achieve the desired technological advancement to keep pace with the trends across the globe. A Chief Technology Officer inducted last year, kept his vigil on the ongoing projects besides rendering his valuable contribution in the process of implementation of various projects. Some of the important digital initiatives already launched by Delhi Police were continued and improved upon to render better services to the citizens of Delhi. e-MV Theft The process of reporting MV Theft for registering e-FIR and court approved final report for claiming insurance continued to function through the web-based application. It was the path breaking initiative by Delhi Police to empower citizens wherein one could file an e-FIR for motor vehicle thefts from home through computer or mobile phone. The entire investigation is carried out in a time bound manner through e-Police Station. The process of courts is also carried out electronically by the e- courts designated for this purpose. During the year, 46,064 MV Theft e- FIR have been lodged and so far more than 1.48 Lakh FIRs have been lodged since its launch in April, 2015. e-courts have accepted 1,22,255 untraced reports so far through this application enabling complainants to file their claims before concerned insurance companies. Property Theft App This App facilitates citizens to lodge online, first information report (FIR) for the property stolen in Delhi, through web, anytime, anywhere, without physically going to the Police Station. There is instant dispatch of a copy of digitally signed FIR to the e-mail of the complainant, area SHO, senior officers and designated Court etc. During the year, 1,33,920 property e-FIRs have been lodged and more than 3,11,548 e-FIRs have been lodged so far since its launching in February, 2016. 1 Lost Report App The purpose of this App is to issue a report to an individual in case of loss of important document like passport, I-Card, Ration Card, Driving License etc. By entering relevant details on this mobile/web based App, one can lodge a lost report instantly and obtain a printable digitally signed report of the same and use this document for getting a fresh document re- issued from the concerned authority. So far 86,71,163 lost reports have been issued online through this App. HimmatPlus App The HimmatPlus SOS App for women was re-launched on 6th Feb. 2018. The App has been made bilingual. The registration is simple and possible through the App only. Also the app has been transformed from an Emergency Safety App to a Utility App for all sections of the society. The Facebook page of Delhi Traffic Police and Twitter handle of Delhi Police has also been linked in the App to provide traffic updates as well other updates of Delhi Police for the benefit of the users. Prahari Scheme Prahari, a force multiplier for policing, is an initiative of Delhi Police for involving various stakeholders like guards and chowkidars in prevention of crime. It aims at promoting a feeling of ownership and camaraderie in the community to promote better police-public relations. Prahari aims at institutionalizing partnerships and cooperation between the police public and private sector security providers in community policing. The objectives of the scheme are i) to identify crime prone areas, ii) to reduce property crime, iii) to foster police-public relations, iv) to increase community spirit, v) to equip the chowkidars and security guards with security equipment, and vi) to enlist the support of these stakeholders in crime prevention and detection in the area. 19,812Parhari’s have been enrolled under this scheme so far. The staff of Investigation Wing is being selected after scrutiny of their service records and experience of conducting Investigation. The effectiveness and professionalism of delivery of police services depends upon developing a system based approach with adequate monitoring mechanism. The true impact or outcomes of results yielded by these initiatives can be analysed only by a holistic analysis of services rendered by the police, through public surveys conducted by professional and independent agencies. The Police force has a tremendous responsibility to serve the community and ensure its safety & security. The Public Perception Survey is a means to gather feedback from general community on the police force and its services in general and also assess the crimes which remain unreported. With the Public Perception Survey, it is intended to find the satisfaction level of the general public with the Police, their concerns and the reasons behind their satisfaction levels/concerns. Delhi Police has engaged the Quality Council of India (QCI), an autonomous body created to lead nationwide quality movement in India, to conduct a Public Perception Survey using globally tested statistical tools for assessing the quality of citizen services rendered by the Delhi Police. text: ,) DELHI POLICE 433/2014 STANDING ORDER, NO. Subject: BUSINESS AREA WATCH SCHEME: DELHI POLICE Spread over an area of 1483 sq. kms. with a population of over 1.8 crores, Delhi is amongst the most populous cities in the world with a density of approximately 6000 persons per sq. km. Its growth since independence has outpaced planned development and a major part of .city's population lives in slums and areas lacking civic amenities. Consequently, urban anonymity coupled with economic inequalities are among the major crimogenic factors. Policing in Delhi is an onerous and ever expanding responsibility. However, increase in police strength have not kept pace with this mega city's growth. Consequentially, the policemen cannot always be present at all places. This, however, can be compensated through enhancing community policing and by appropriate usageof technology. Delhi Policehas taken a number of community policing initiatives like the Neighbourhood Watch Scheme, Eyes and Ears Scheme, Parivartan, Pehchan,Yuva, Senior Citizens Scheme, tenant/servant verification etc. In all these schemes, the design'and format has been provided by the Police,in which the community members participate in policing with Delhi Policeacting as facilitator. In the field of technology, Delhi Policehas inter-alia been using CCTV coverage of important market placesand border checkposts for prevention and detection of crimes. So far CCTV system has been funded by the government and is being implemented and maintained by ECIL/Delhi Police. Since requirement of CCTV.cameras in the city is very large and police budgetary provisions may not enable coverage of all vulnerable places in one go, alternate financing models may become necessary. In this regard, installation of CCTVnetwork/s with public assistance is relevant and can be suitably implemented to meet Delhi's expanding needs. In order to further augment the CCTVcoverage in the city, it has been decided to initiate a Business Area Watch Scheme as community initiative with Delhi Policeacting as the facilitator of the scheme and public spirited members of the community funding the installation, maintenance and operation' of CCTV converqeJn an area; particularly markets and other' commercial/institutional locations. This BusinessArea Watch Scheme (BAWS) of Delhi Policewill be as follows:- 1. It will be implemented in all the districts in a phased manner. 2. All District Add!. CsP/DCsPwill immediately identify vulnerable areas from crime or terror point of view, where the market or business community is willing to participate by way of installation of CCTV.cameras and its maintenance under police guidance. 3'. The Local Monitoring Centre of these cameras will be set up at the respective BAWSareas and, if required, the cameras will be connected to Cyber Highway by linking them with concerned PoliceStation. The locations chosen should generally be such that linking upto the Police Station is not cost prohibitive. It may be noted .that the Cyber Highway connectivity is already provided to all the PoliceStations in Delhi. In addition, a'wide area network setup by ECILexists'at market places where the government funded CCTVsystem is already installed. 4. document_title: Standing Order No. 436 : Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace.
text: Standing Order Y36/2014 Subject: SEXUAL HARASSMENT OF WOMEN AT WORKPLACE. Sexual harassment at work place is a highly undesirable act and demeaning for the self respect of a woman. In order to provide a safe environment free from sexual harassment, the Government of India has passed "The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace· (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal), Act, 2013". Asper the Act"Sexual Harassment" includes anyone or more unwelcome acts or behavior (whether directly or by implication) (i) Physical contact and advances (Ii) A demand or request for sexual favours (ili) Making sexually coloured remarks (iv) Showing pornography (v) Any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct ofsexual nature. Followingcircumstances also amount to sexual harassment (i) Implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in service (il) Implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in her service and present or future postings (ili) Interference with her work or creating an intimidating or offensiveor hostile work environment for her (iv) Humiliating treatment likelyto affecther health or safety. CONSTITUTIONOF COMMITTEEAT POLICE HEADQUARTERSAS .J WELLAS ATRANGE/UNITLEVEL In order to curb the incident of sexual harassment and to conduct enquiry into the incident of alleged sexual harassment, a Committee at the PHQ level will be formed, which will be called as "Central Internal Complaints Committee". The Committee shall consist ofthe followingmembers:- (a) A Presiding Omcer who shall be a woman officer preferably of the rank ofAddl. Commissioner of Police but not below the rank of Deputy Commissioner of Police. Provided that in case an officer of the rank of DCPis not posted in PHQ,a lady officerofthe equivalent rank willbe nominated from any District/Unit. (b) Not less than two members of the rank not below the rank of Addl Deputy Commissioner ·of Police and at least one ofthem to be a women officer. (c) One member from amongst non-governmental organizations or associations committed to the cause of women or a person familiar with the issues relating to sexual harassment. 1 The members of the committee will be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi or an officer designated by the Commissioner of Police. The Central Internal Complaints Committee will monitor the functioning of District/Unit 'Internal Complaints Committee' and enquire into the complaints against the alleged officials of all ranks posted in Police Headquarters. An aggrieved woman may submit a written complaint to the Internal Complaints Committee within a period of three months from the date of incident. The Internal Committee may further extend three months time, if it is satisfied that there were circumstances that prevented the aggrieved women from filing a complaint. The Presiding Officer and other members of the committee will assist the aggrieved women in submitting a written complaint. In cases where the aggrieved women is unable to make a complaint on account of her physical or mental incapacity or death or otherwise her legal heir may make a complaint. ./ SPECIFIC STEPS TO BE TAKEN BY THE COMMITTEE. When a complaint of sexual harassment at work place is received the followingactions willbe taken:- ...-- (i) The enquiry into the complaint should be taken-up by the Central Internal Complaints Committee at PHQ level or by the Internal Complaints Committee at the Ranges/Units levelas the case may be, and the enquiry should be completed within a period ofninety days. The aggrieved women as well as the respondent should be given an opportunity ofbeing heard during the course ofenquiry and a copy of the findings should be made available to both, enabling them to make representation against the findings before the committee. (ii) The Presiding Officerofthe Committee should submit the findings to the Commissioner of Police or to the officer designated by the Commissioner of Police for this purpose in case of Central Internal Complaints Committee and to Addl.CP/DCP of the District/Unit in case of Internal Complaints Committee at Ranges/Units level within a period often days from the date ofcompletion of the enquiry. (iii) The Committee may before initiating an enquiry at the request of the complainant take steps to settle the matter through conciliation. However, no monetary settlement would be made as a basis of conciliation. (iv) During the pendency of the enquiry on a written request from"the complainant, the committee may recommend the transfer of the complainant or the respondent to any other District/Unit/Section, 4 grant leave to the complainant upto a period of three months or any other reliefto the complainant. (v) If the Committee arrives at the conclusion that the allegations have been proved, it would recommend action for sexual harassment as misconduct in accordance with the provisions of the service rules applicable to the respondent. Action will be taken on the recommendations within sixty days of its receipt. Where behavior of the alleged person falls under criminal law, the Committee shall forward the complaint to the

(v) If the Committee arrives at the conclusion that the allegations have been proved, it would recommend action for sexual harassment as misconduct in accordance with the provisions of the service rules applicable to the respondent. Action will be taken on the recommendations within sixty days of its receipt. Where behavior of the alleged person falls under criminal law, the Committee shall forward the complaint to the local police within a period of 07 days forregistration ofthe case. (vi) In cases where the committee arrives at the conclusion that the allegation has not been proved it shall recommend that no action is required to be taken in the matter. (vii) Where the committee arrives at a conclusion that the allegation against the respondent are malicious, false and forged/misleading documents have been produced by the complainant, it may recommend to take action against the complainant in accordance with the provisions ofthe service rules applicable to her. (viii) The contents of the complaint, the identity and addresses of the aggrieved women, respondent and witnesses, any information relating to conciliation and enquiry proceedings, recommendations of the Committee under the provisions of this Act shall not be published, communicated or made known to the public, press and. media in any manner. (ix) The record ofthe complaints ofsexual harassment willbe maintained in a separate register in the respective Ranges/Units and the proceeding ofthe complaint willbe kept "CONFIDENTIAL". OPERATION "NIRBHEEK" Introduction It has been seen that offenders in more than ninety percent· of the sexual assault cases ·are relatives, neighbours, friends and acquaintances of victims. And most of the cases take place within the four walls of private. spaces like homes and work places. Quite often victims hesitate to come foiWard to register their cases owing to family and social pressure, social stigma; and lack of trust in the administration of criminal justice system. The above is invariably the case of innocent young children who happen to be unaware of what constitutes a sexual offence or which touch is good or bad. Owing to their innocence, they fall prey to the lust of a pervert offender, and sometimes become victim of serious crime also. Through 'Operation Nirbheek' Delhi Police has taken an initiative to spread awareness in ·girls'/Co-ed schools to educate girl students aboutvarious aspects of sexual offences of which innocently or inadvertently they be.come victim, to instill confidence in. them to report to Police for legal action, and to involve parents and community to win their confidence .and . seek their participation in handling this sensitive issue. This operation will be launched in each girls'/co-ed school through a designated police officer. Objectives . Operation Nirbheek will have the following objectives: (i) To spread awareness among the girl students about various types of sexual offences ~hey may fall prey to, for example, about. a good touch and a bad touch, etc. (ii) To interact with the girl students in order to have friendly and participative interaction. · (iii) To instill confidence in them so. that they. could share their most personal trauma. (iv) To identify the victim of sexual offences amongst the girl students. (v) To convince them to report to police in case they have become victim of sexual offence. (vi) To engage parents and community to fight against such crimes. (vii) To make the parents and community aware that if they do not come forward to take action against sexual offenders owing to social stigma, their action would embolden these offenders to commit major crimes. W/SI or ASI of Police Station will be the coordinator, and W/ HC or Constable will be the 'Nirbheek Woman Poli~e Officer (NWPO). document_title: Standing Order No. 449 : Public Facilitation Desk & Public Facilitation Officers.
text: /:il- I Standing Order No L1 l1 '1 r:i r:;· J' IJllllJJ ISILlI<C IF~IClIILJiiA ilIO['j] l:JH;:Sn{ Police is the most visible arm of the Government. A person in distress uslilally approaches police by calling emergency response numbers like '100' or rushes to a police station for redressal of grievances. A visitor to a police station as a complainant or otherwise certainly deserves to be heard and all he/she expects is an honest and sincere effort on the part of police to solve his/her problems .. 2. At present, in every police station, there is a system wherein the complainants/visitors coming to the police stations are attended to by the Duty Offo::er, who listens/attends to them <'Jnd brings their grievances to the notice of the concerried officers of the police station. However, the Duty Officer already has numerous other duties to take care of. Therefore, due to his pre-occupation in. connection with his responsibilities as a "Duty i ' Officer", most of the time he .fails to appropriately attend to the complainants/visitors. Similarly, most of the time, SHO/IOs are not available in the police station due to their pre-occupation in other field/court duties and the complainants/visitors to the police stations find it~ very difficult to communicate with them. The ultimate result is loss of public faith in police functioning. With a view to fill the 'gap' and 'mis-trust' created due to lack of communication between the police and members of public, "Public Facilitation desk" in each police station is to be set-up which will. act as the first point of contact and s.hall make the visit to a police station a satisfying and pleasurable experience for one and all. (1) 3. OBJECTIVES Public Facilitation Desk in the police stations is aimed to achieve the following objectives:- 1. Act as first point of contact for all visitors to the Police Station. 2. Enhance the quality of interaction between the public and the police personnel. 3. Facilitate general public to get answers for their queries in a systematic manner. 4. Streamline the process of handling different categories of 'Walk-ins' into the police stations. · 5. Faster complaints redressal. 6. Elimination of harassment of complainants/visitors. 7. Making visit to the PS a pleasurable experience. 4. DUTIES OF PUBLIC FACILITATION DESK OFFICER It will be the duty of the 'Public Facilitation Desk' Officer to attend to all the visitors and complainants who visit the police station for any purpose and ensure that their purpose of coming to the police station is achieved without any un-due delay in the best possible manner. A record of the details of the visitors and purpose of visit shall be maintained in a specially designed register in case his/her grievance cannot be addressed at that moment due to absence of an officer or for any other reason. He shall then inform the concerned officer of the police station (through a slip) (2) ' and arrange redressal of grievances of complainant/visitor. The concerned officer shall sign the carbon copy of the

document_title: Standing Order No. 453 : Action against Sale and abuse of Narcotic Drugs.
text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER No.~53/2018 ACTION AGAINST SALE AND ABUSE OF NARCOTIC DRUGS INTRODUCTION The purpose of this Standing Order is to reiterate and emphasise on the need to put an effective control on sale and abuse of narcotic drugs in Delhi. The existing law and rules are sufficient and stringent to deal with the problem. However, there is an urgent need to make the most effective use of the legal provisions and supplement the same by adopting administrative steps effectively. It is well known that the problem of drug abuse is the result of various socio-economic factors particular to a metropolitan city like Delhi and, hence, it needs to be tackled on different fronts to gain effective control over it. This strategy will involve various long and short-term measures to reduce the demand on the one hand and taking effective legal action against the supply chain on the other hand. Being conscious and aware of the sale and abuse of narcotic drugs and its harmful effects, a road map has been prepared to tackle it by taking various short-term and long-term measures. 1. CONTROL ON ILLICIT SALE AND ACTION AGAINST THE SUPPLY CHAIN There is no doubt that the foremost task in this endeavour is to put a control over the sale and supply of drugs. Presently, there is a specialized unit for prevention of sale and trafficking of narcotic drugs viz. 'Narcotics & Crime Prevention Cell' headed by a DCP-rank officer, who works under the supervision ofJoint CP/Crime and Special CP/Crime. In addition, from time to time the District Police also make search and seizure of narcotic drugs and effect arrest of drug-peddlers. Even while the present arrangement will continue the action, for more effective co-ordinated action, the following steps willalso be taken by the districtsyunitsr- (i) Setting up a 'Narcotic Squad' in each district: A'Narcotics Squad' willbe constituted in each district, which shall be 1 supervised by an Inspector, who, in turn, shall work under the supervision of ACP/Operations. Each Narcotics Squad, to start with, shall have a manpower consisting of two Upper and eight LowerSubordinate Officers. In due course, the strength ofthese squads willbe increased appropriately. The Narcotics Squad and the local police shall undertake the following tasks:- a. Identification of hot spot of drugs sale in the district in which there are complaints of sale of drugs or where the drug addicts are mostly found flocking, and immediate necessary steps to bust/ apprehend such peddlers who are active in drugs- trafficking. b. Identification of potential suppliers and strict action as per law against them. (ii) Enhanced action vi] s 29 of NDPS Act shall be taken against the abettors and conspirators, aiding the sale ofdrugs. (iii) Identification be carried out ofpersons with previous involvements for taking substantive as well as preventive actions against them. (iv) Enhanced action be taken under Section 77 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, which prescribes punishment to offenders also for selling narcotics material tojuveniles. It is reiterated that the Juvenile

text: suppliers and strict action as per law against them. (ii) Enhanced action vi] s 29 of NDPS Act shall be taken against the abettors and conspirators, aiding the sale ofdrugs. (iii) Identification be carried out ofpersons with previous involvements for taking substantive as well as preventive actions against them. (iv) Enhanced action be taken under Section 77 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, which prescribes punishment to offenders also for selling narcotics material tojuveniles. It is reiterated that the Juvenile Justice Board has widely interpreted the expression "Intoxicating Liqour" to include substances such as whitener, thinners and vulcanizing solutions/ sulochans, which have the effect of intoxication and which may not be beverages per se and, hence, these substances should also be treated as intoxicating liquor within the meaning of Section 77 of the JJ Act. In compliance of Order dated 20.03.2017 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board-III, the Government of NCT of Delhi has also issued a Notification dated 28th July, 2017 which, inter-alia, directs that a "mandatory warning should be made on the application devise (pens or otherwise) of correcting fluids/thinners and vulcanized solutions/ sulochans regarding the effects of inhalation of vapour/consumption of the chemicals contained therein on health". Additional action under Section 188 may IPC also be taken if any violation comes to notice. (v) Regular visits to vulnerable schools identified by State Project Director-SSA, Department of Education, GNCTof Delhi to identify the drug- peddlers. District DCsP shall ensure that officers posted in the Narcotics Squad and police stations concerned visit such identified schools at least once in a week and ensure Zero Tolerance on this issue. All-out efforts shall be made to identify such elements and in case any drug-peddler is identified, immediate action must be taken against him. 2 (vi) Efforts are being made to get help from Drugs Control Department of the Govt. of NCTof Delhi by getting Nodal Officers appointed at the district level. Use of Pharmaceutical drugs, especially the Habit Forming drugs and Schedule-H 1 drugs, are a real menace. Liaison with the Drugs Control Department is required to be made for initiating action under the Drugs & Cosmetics Act and the NDPS Act against the unscrupulous elements, who are involved in sale of Pharmaceutical products to be used as a narcotics substance. Local police shall promptly provide all necessary help to the Drugs Control Department (GNCTD),as and when a demand is made for any raid of this nature. (vii) Training session for police officers for capacity building and improving the investigation skills: Regular training is required to be conducted for capacity building and improving the investigating as well as intelligence collection skills of the investigating officers with regard to detection and investigation of NDPS Act related cases. Sustained action by trained investigators will only have a deterrent impact on the supply chain. Dy. Commissioner of Police/Narcotics & Crime Prevention Cell will hold regular training sessions in this regard. District DCsP shall ensure that officers of the rank of Sub-Inspector, Inspector, ACP and

Commissioner of Police/CRO shall collate information on drug- dealers to prepare a booklet, which shall be circulated among all concerned for taking preventive as well as substantive action. The updating of the data will be on a monthly basis. Inter-District Coordination Committee shall also be formed for this purpose and it shall hold a meeting at least once In a quarter, which willbe attended by the officer(s)of Narcotics Squad. 2. REDUCTION OF DEMAND This is another effective step to tackle the problem and needs to be taken simultaneously along with the above steps directed towards reduction in supply. In this direction the followingsteps need to be taken:- (i) Regular visits to vulnerable schools identified by the GNCTDAgency to identify potential users: State Project Director-SSA, Department of Education, GNCT of Delhi provides the list of vulnerable schools for monitoring and curbing availability and peddling the drugs and narcotics substances among school going children. Delhi Police will make necessary efforts to coordinate with the government agencies and NGOs to educate and make aware the potential users of the dangers and harmful consequences of using such products. Also, all possible support shall be extended by district DCsP for holding of Nukkad Natak, Camp(s) against drug abuse etc. (ii) Involvement of Health Services/NGOs to ensure more effective publicity to harmful effects of drug consumption: This involves steps like holding of sessions by Health Services/NGOs to give assurance to drug 3 users that return to normal life, by giving up drugs, is possible and that they would be accepted back by the society. District DCsP shall ensure that maximum co-operation and support in such programmes is provided. text: . , :;: '0 ~.: D·ELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER No.4 5LJ /2018 'P R A H A R I' S C HEM E 1. INTRODUCTION Prahari -a Force MUltiplierforPolicing- is an initiativeofDelhiPolicefor eliciting active 'partiCipation of various' stakeholders like 'Private Security Guards and .Chowkidarsin prevention of crime. It aims at promoting a feeling of ownership andcamaraderie in the community to fcsterbetterpolice-publlc relations; With more and more people turning to private 'security for personal safety" that of their families and property, as also that of their residential, , colonies and business establishments, it is in the Interest of Delhi Police to sensitize'and involve such private'security personnel with a viewto maximizing .'their performance in the overall interest of the safety and security of 'the community. ' " , , With, the above' purpose in mind, the geed' for institutionalized partnerships- andcooperation between the public ana private sector security in community policing, can hardly be over-emphasized. The level of cooperation can be enhanced through joint training, regular joint security briefingmeetings " and crime mappmg,physical and information resource sharing as well as reduced suspicion between the two entities. This can sigriificantly and qlialitatlvely,enhance the participation of the private' security providers in community policing. 2. AllISAIm OBJBCTIyE8 . . '. : . The Prahari Scheme is a veritably potent community policing initiative . r inasmuch ,as it emphasizes on proactive enforcement that works on the proposition that street"crime can be'reduced to a great extent through greater community involvement and integration between citizens and police, In this initiative, all the 'stakeholders and ofticersaim to devotequality time to develop 1 a "partnership" to:- (a) Prevent and counter crime; (b)Maintain order; and (c) Reducethe fear ofcrime. The Prahari Scheme runs on the basic principle that law can be better enforced and crime can be better prevented. with the cooperation of the Praharis (Private Security Guards and Chowkidars). Under this Scheme, the Delhi Police identifies and involves various stakeholders like Guards and Chowkidars primarily for prevention of the various types of property crimes such as robberies and burglaries, snatchings, motorcycles and vehicle thefts and miscellaneous types ofthefts. Afterenrolment, the Praharis are trained by the DelhiPoliceto help and coordinate in overseeingthe safety and security of public and property in the residential and market .areaa. Theobjectivesofthe Schemeare broadlyas follows: a) Toidentifycrime-prone areas. b) Toreduce property crime. c) Tofoster police-publicrelations. d) Toincrease community participation in pre:ventionand detection of crime. 3. ROLE OF PRAHARlS In many cases, chowkidars, guards and villagewatchmen haveplayed a .vitalrolenot onlyin preventing crimes liketheft, burglary, robberyetc. but also in providing vital clues in heinous cases as also about criminal/anti-social elements visitingthe area. Toestablish a mutual relationship with the Praharis on the basis of a common objectiveof promoting sec!m.tyand safety ofpeople is in the interests ofDelhiPolice. . Specifically, the Praharis will be required to discharge the following functions: a) Makethe residents aware about the identity/photographs, addresses and modus operandi ofthe criminals/burglars residing in their area, so that. any suspicious movement of such bad elements could be reported promptlyto the police.

document_title: Standing Order No. 414 : Grant of Swimming Pool Licences.
text: STA NDING ORDER FOR THE GRANT OF SWIMMING POOL LICENCES >, ,'· - I ... \ STANDING ORDER NO. 4/(1µ0/~ POWERS AND PROCEDURES WITH REGARD TO GRANT OF LICENCE FOR SWIMMING POOLS UNDER THE REGULATION "UNION TERRITORY OF DELHI SWIMMING POOLS (LICENSING AND CONTROLLING> REGULATION. 1980". 1. DERIVATION OF POWERS : As per Clause 'X' of Sub-Section (1) of Section 28 read with sub-section (2) & (3) of Section 28 of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police has promulgated the Regulation titled "Union Territory of Delhi Swimming Pools (Licensing and Controlling) Regulation, 1980", which -~f extends to the Union Territory of Delhi. This Regulation applies to all swimming pools to which members of public are admitted either on payment of money or with the intention that money may be collected from those admitted. It is provided that no person shall maintain any swimming ·pool to which these regulations apply except under a licence. As per the order issued by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi vide No.83-182/Spl. Cell/PHQ dated 01.02.2008, the power to license swimming pools vests with the Addi. Commissioner of Police (Licensing), Delhi. 2. POWERS: Under the "Union Territory of Delhi Swimming Pools (Licensing and Controlling) Regulation, 1980", the Commissioner of Police, Union Territory of Delhi i.e. Addi. Commissioner of Police (Licensing) has been empowered with:- i) Grant of Swimming Pool Licence Swimming Pool Licence is issued under Regulation 4(2) of "Union Territory of Delhi Swimming Pools (Licensing and Controlling) Regulation, 1980". Commissioner of Police (Licensing), _may, if he is satisfied after such enquiry as he thinks fit, that the licensee is not a suitable person for continuing to hold the licence, or if the swimming pool is not in a suitable condition, after giving the licensee an opportunity to render an explanation and after recording his reasons, refuse to renew the licence. · iii) Suspension/revocation of Licence a) A licence granted or renewed shall be for the use by only the person, firm or company to whom or on whose behalf it is granted, or in whose favour it is renewed, and on the death of such person or the dissolution of the firm or the winding up or the liquidation of the company, the licence shall be deemed to be revoked. b) Where a licence is issued to a firm, the retirement of a partner from or the admission of \, a new partner into the firm shall be notified to the

The Licensee shall not keep Swimming Pool open after 12 O' clock mid-night or open it before 5 O' clock in the morning, except with the special permission in writing from the Commissioner of Police. 9. The Licensee shall not allow more than 40 persons (beginners) in the shallow and s persons in each lane of 2.5 mts width in a full sized pool i.e. 50 mts X 21 mts. And shall only allow 20 persons in the shallow and 3 persons in each lane of the smaller pool. 10. The Licensee shall provide qualified instructor I coach who has adequate knowledge of the first aid and artificial respiration. j 11. The Licensee shall also provide necessary fire fighting equipments in the premises, which must be maintained in proper condition. 13. The Licensee shall keep the water of the Pool clean and change it atleast once a month and at the short intervals if directed. document_title: Standing Order No. 416 : Subsidiary Central Police Canteen (SCPC), New Police Lines, Delhi Police
text: - ; DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO, 41612014 SUBSIDIARY CENTRAL POLICE CANTEEN (SCPC), "Subsidiary Central Police Canteens" have been established in different Battalions of DAP for providing consumer goods/durables at cheaper rates to Delhi Police personnel. The goods shall be sold to Police personnel and their family members. 1. OBJECTIVE The objective of Central Police Canteen is to r,un a welfare oriented, self-sustained store with specific objective of providing good quality consumer, goods to Delhi Police personnel at prices cheaper than those prevailing in the market. 2. CANTEEN ESTABLISHMENT "-- A Canteen Committee comprising of the following officers and men has been constituted to operate the canteen:- 1)President DCP/Concerned Battalion of DAP 2)VicePresident ACP/ HQ/ Concerned Battalion of DAP 3) Secretary ACP/ADJ/ Concerned Battalion of DAP 4) Audit Board Audit team of PHQunder FA 5) Manager/Canteen One Inspector/One S.l. 6) Account Clerk One ..HC (Min.) or any other competent HC having knowledge of accounts related work. 7) Billing /Cash Clerk 1 HC and 1Ct. having knowledge of computers. 8).Store Keeper 1 HC with 2 constable for proper upkeep of item in store room. 9)RecordKeeper 1 constable having knowledge of computers for the proper maintenance of. correspondence file & documents. 10)Salesmen 2 HC& 3 Ct. in each shift. 3. PROCUREMENT The Committee shall procure items from the Master Central Police Canteen run under aegis of the Ministry of Home Affairs or from the dealers/suppliers approved by the Central PoliceCanteen Organization, as per the directions and provisions in this regard. 4. STORE The canteen willmaintain a reasonable stock ofsaleable items as per the strength and monthly requirement of the unit. There shall never be excessive inventory ofsuperfluous items. Items in the store willbe categorized as follows:- a) Toiletriesand Cosmetics. b} Kitchenwares & Plastic wares. c) Stationery items. d) Grocery,Food & Beverages. e) Watches & Time Devices. f) Electrical & Electronic Devices. g) Consumer Durables such as T.V.,Refrigerator,Washing machine etc. h) Sports Goods, Hosiery items & Luggageitems. i) Cycles,Motorcycles& Cars. j) Miscellaneous items (as :perthe decision ofthe Committee). k) Items made at Delhi PoliceWelfareCenter. 1) Items made at Tihar Jail. 2. 5.SALE Allcommodities will be sold on cash/cheque/D.O. payment. In case of cheque payment, items willbe deliveredon encashment ofthe cheque. Allcash transactions will be through computer generated bills. The principle of first come, first served basis willbe followedfor sale. Whereverapplicable, rationing may be imposed on the quantity ofsaleable items and a rationing quota system willbe developed in due course after analyzing the monthly quantum of sale. Further, for this purpose, a framework shall be developed in the daily sale software to have details like date, name & PIS No. of the purchaser, items purchased in a month and price. In case of high value items like automobiles etc., the police personnel .may be required to pay in advance the sale price to enable the Canteen to procure the item. The Police personnel must ensure that the items are purchased for her/his own consumption and not for re-sale. Anyone found· indulging in malpractice can

The Police personnel must ensure that the items are purchased for her/his own consumption and not for re-sale. This monthly stock taking will be conducted by the Canteen Managerunder the supervision ofthe VicePresident. The stocktaking day will be observed as a holiday. This closing day will be utilized for the purchase of provisions and checking of accounts/stocks by the Canteen Manager. A certificatewillbe recorded in the cash register in token ofhaving done so. Further, half yearly physical verification of stock shall be conducted by an officer not below the rank of an ACP, not directly connected with the maintenance of account of canteen and also not being an officebearer of the Canteen Committee. 7. PRICING The canteen willfunction at no profit no loss basis. However,a margin of 1% over the purchase price will be levied to meet the administrative requirement. Everysaleable item willdisplay a price tag. As and when deemed necessary, the canteen may charge a reasonable amount forprovidingcarry bags or packing material forthe sold items. 3 8. TIMING The canteens will function from 9.30 AMto 7:00 PM in two shifts on all the 07 days as per schedule given below:- Morning shift: 9.30 AMto 2.00 PM Evening shift: 02.00 PM to 07.00 PM The Canteen Committee, however, may decide about any change in the working hours for the canteen in their monthly meeting as per the requirement of the unit. 9. NECESSARY INFRASTRUCTURE/LOGISTICS Apart from the basic requirement of hall/rooms having sufficient space for the canteen and separate room for storing items, additional provisions of some basic infrastructural requirement imperative for the smooth running and management of the canteen are hereby made as under: - 1) C.C.T.V. CAMERAS The whole canteen and its store room will be covered by C.C.T.V. surveillance to keep a vigilant eye on the activities of staff as well as customers to avoid any untoward incident like theft of articles etc. In case any incident comes to notice, enquiry shall be conducted on the basis of C.C.T.V footage. 2) ACs & FRIDGE The canteen will have split ACs and Fridge in required numbers so that the purchased edible, cosmetic and health related other perishable items could be kept at suitable temperatures. 3) INVERTER In order to ensure continuous power supply for uninterrupted running of the canteen during working hours, an Inverter of suitable power sufficient to run the computer, printer, billing machine and lightings will be installed in the canteen. 4) COMPUTER, PRINTER, SCANNER, BAR CODE READER, BUSINESS .

UNIFORM OF CANTEEN STAFF There would be separate summer & winter uniform for the staff responsible for running the canteen. The pattern shall be decided by the President. The Canteen staff shall wear neat and clean uniform and shall be well groomed. The canteen uniform shall not be used for personal use. 12. CASH MANAGEMENT The Canteen Manager assisted by one HC will be responsible for ensuing maintenance of day-to-day cash transaction record. He will ensure legible entries in a Cash- Book of the receipts and expenditure. The daily sale cash (after closing of canteen) shall remain in the custody of the Canteen Manager/officer. 13. CUSTODY OF CASH All money received on account of the canteen shall be deposited in an account maintained with the nearest scheduled bank or the AXISBANKin the name of the Vice President of Canteen or Secretary of Canteen. 6 The Canteen cash receipt shall be deposited in the Bank on the next working-day except for a sum of Rs. 10,000/- which may be kept by the Manager as imprest money for meeting emergent daily expenditure. The imprest amount and all other cash shall be kept in the cash chest. 14. POWERS OF EXPENDITURE The President, SCPC,concerned Battalion of DAPshall have the powers to incur expenditure in connection with the upkeep of and additions to the Canteen property, provided that no single item ofexpenditure shall exceed Rs. 50,000/ -. For amounts in excess of this sum, the sanction of the CommissionerofPolice,Delhimay be obtained in advance who has fullpowers to utilize the funds. The President is empoweredto incur day to day ordinary expenditure including consumables in connection with the running of the Canteen and also to pay tradesmen's bills. 15. ,, DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. 422/2013 RECRUITMENT OF SUB-INSPECTOR(DRAFTSMAN) IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY Iii This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment against the posts of Sub-Inspector(Draftsman) in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 18 [ii] of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. Intimation regarding number of vacancies and details of the recruitment process shall be communicated to the Central Employment Exchange and Sub- Employment Exchanges in Delhi. In addition, the vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base of recruitment and make Delhi Police a metropolitan force. A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi Police website. Resident Commissioners of all the states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility requirements apply on the prescribed application form alongwith Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque of <100/-. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board of the Delhi Police located at New Police Lines, Kingsway Camp, Delhi. The candidates belonging to SC/ST category and Ex-servicemen category are not required to send Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque alongwith the application form. [ii] DCP/Establishment, Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. Un-reserved, SC, ST, OBC and Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi in the month of January and July each year. C.P. Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/Establishment, Delhi to DCP/Reeruitment Cell, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. Page 1of 11 2. MODE OF RECRUITMENT Vacancies in the rank of Sub-Inspect.or(Draftsman) shall be filled up by direct recruitment by holding prescribed competitive examinations. 3. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATION (i) AGE: 18 to 25 years. The upper age limit as prescribed above will be rclaxable only in the followingcases:- (a) Upto a maximum of 5 years if a candidate bclongs to a Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe category or other government servants. (b) Upto a maximum of3 years if a candidate belongs to an OBC category. This relaxation is admissible for those castes notified in the Central List and the List issued by the Govt. of NCTofDelhi. (c) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible upto 35 years (38 years for OBC, 40 years for SCs/STs) for widows/divorced women and women judicially separated from their husbands and who are not re-married. (d) Age concession to Ex-Servicemen will be allowed in accordance with the orders issued by the government from time to lime. They will be permitted to

is admissible for those castes notified in the Central List and the List issued by the Govt. of NCTofDelhi. (c) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible upto 35 years (38 years for OBC, 40 years for SCs/STs) for widows/divorced women and women judicially separated from their husbands and who are not re-married. (d) Age concession to Ex-Servicemen will be allowed in accordance with the orders issued by the government from time to lime. They will be permitted to deduct the period served in the armed forces from their actual age and the resultant age, so derived, should not exceed the prescribed age limit by more than three years. It is further clarified that an "Ex-Serviceman" means a person, who has served in any rank whether as a combatant or non-combatant inArmy, Navy orAir Forceof the Indian Union and who retired/rom such service after earning his pension. (e) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible upto 30 years (33. years for OBC, 35 years for SCs/STs) for departmental candidates of Delhi Police. A "departmental candidate" means who has rendered a minimum three years regular and continuous service in Delhi Police. Note Candidates claiming benefits under OBC category shall be in accordance with castes notified in the Central List. This relaxation will also be admissible for candidates who are issued OBC certificate by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi. The certificate should be in the prescribed form issued by the competent authority empowered for the purpose. No other certificate wi:1lbe accepted as sufficient proof. (iii) MEDICAL FITNESS I STANDARDS The candidate should be of sound health, free from disease/ defect/ debility and colour blindness. Better eye 6/6 without glasses. Worse eye 6/36 corrected with glasses to 6/9 or 6/12 without glasses (both eyes). No relaxation is allowed to any category of candidates on this count. 4. INTRODUCTORYnmlkjihgfedcbaZYXWVUTSRQPONMLKJIHGFEDCBA [i] This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Head Constable (Telephone ExchangeOperator) in Delhi Policein accordance with Rule 17-B (XIV) of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) (Amendment) Rules,2013. ./ [ii] Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. Intimation regarding number of vacancies and details of recruitment processshall be communicated to the Central Employment Exchange and Sub-Employment Exchangesin Delhi. In addition, the vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base of recruitment and make Delhi Police a metropolitan force. A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi Police website. Resident Commissioners of all states will also be requested to publicize the recruitment in their respective' states. Delhiwill take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/Establishment,Delhi to DCP/Recruitment Cell, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. 2.
