document_title: Standing Order No. 426 : Grant of Licence/No Objetion Certificate for Ammonium Nitrate Store House.
text: J =.0 STANDING ORDER No. 4 ~6 J 3 r 4 GRANT OF LICENCE/NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE FOR AMMONIUM NITRATE STORE HOUSE This Standing Order aims to lay down rules and procedures related to grant of Ammonium Nitrate Licence to regulate and control manufacture, conversion, stevedoring and bagging, import, export, transport, possession for sale or use, of Ammonium Nitrate and No Objection Certificate where licence is to be granted by the Controller of Explosives, Nagpur or Joint Chief Controller of Explosives, North Circle, Faridabad, Haryana. As per Rule 2 (b) of the Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012, Ammonium Nitrate means the compound having the chemical formula NH4N03 and includes any mixture or compound having more than 4S percent Ammonium Nitrate by weight including emulsions, suspensions, melts or gels (with or without inorganic nitrates) but excluding emulsion or slurry explosives and non-explosives emulsion matrix and fertilizers from which Ammonium Nitrate can not be extracted by any physical. or chemical process. 1. Derivation of powers: As per section 146 (i) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, the Commissioner of Police is empowered to exercise all powers which may be exercised by District Magistrate under the Acts mentioned in Schedule I, and the rules made thereunder, which include the Explosive Act, 1884 and the Ammonium Nitrate Rules 2012. Therefore, all the powers vested in the 'District Authority' as mentioned in the Explosives Act, 1884 and the Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012 are to be exercised by the Commissioner of Pollee, Delhi, which in case of Ammonium Nitrate licences/No Objection Certificates, have been delegated to the Additional Commissioner of Police, Licensing, Delhi vide order No. 83-182/Spl. Cell/PHQ dated 01.02.2008. Therefore, the Ammonium Nitrate licences are to be granted by Additional Commissioner of Police, Licensing, Delhi upto a quantity of maximum of 30 MT to (1) possess for sale or use of Ammonium Nitrate from a storehouse, (2) to possess for use of Ammonium Nitrate for agricultural purposes from a storehouse and (3) to transport Ammonium Nitrate for licences granted by Additional Commissioner of Police, Licensing, Delhi for possession for sale or possession for use (as per Schedule I of Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012). The licences for quantity exceeding 30 MT of Ammonium Nitrate are granted by the Controller of Explosives/Nagpur or Joint Chief Controller of Explosive, Faridabad Haryana after receipt of No objection certificate issued by the Addl. Commissioner of Police, Licensing Delhi. 2. NO LICENCE REQUIRED FOR POSSESSION OF AMMONIUM NITRATE QF QUANTITY LESS THAN SKG BY CERTAIIQ ESTABLISHMENTS: No licence shall be required for possession and use of ammonium nitrate of quantity not exceeding five kilogram (Skgs) by established laboratories, educational institutions, medical institutions, hospitals and clinics for scientific and educational purposes. However, they must inform local police,about the quantity under possession for the foresaid purposes. 3. CONDITIONS: Grant of Ammonium Nitrate licences/No Objection Certificate shall be so regulated that no pilferage, fire accidents/incidents resulting in injury and loss of human life takes place. This should be done in accordance with the provisions of The

This should be done in accordance with the provisions of The Explosives Act, 1884, The Explosives Substances Act, 1908, The Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012 and other conditions as given below:- i. Licences shall be granted only for a storehouse located on a commercial street or area as per the Master Plan Delhi- 2021 in accordance with Section 15.5 & 15.6.2 and 15.6.3. The premises used for, manufacture of the Ammonium Nitrate or conversion of the melt into solid form of Ammonium Nitrate or vice versa and the storehouse shall be surrounded by a wall of at least two metres height of such strength and construction as to effectively prevent entry of unauthorised persons. 2 vii. Safety distance of 9 metres from store houseto the compound wall and 90 meters from any protected works shall be maintained for storage house of Ammonium Nitrate exceeding 30 MT. (Note:- Safety distance shall be measured from the edge of the . storehouse) ix. text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. 430/2014 MOBILE APP INTEGRATED WITH WEB BASED APPLICATION TO LODGE POLICE REPORT REGARDING ARTICLE/DOCUMENT LOST IN DELHI Delhi Police has consistently been adopting new methodologies and technologies to enhance its service delivery capabilities. Towards this endeavour, it has been decided to launch a mobile and web based service for recording of information with police about article/document lost in Delhi. This service will enable a person to lodge a report at his convenience on his Mobile Phone using the Delhi Police Mobile Application on Google play store/Windows phone store/Apple App store. Alternately, the service may be accessed through the Delhi Police Website i.e. www.delhipolice.nic.in. Once a report is lodged through mobile or on web, a digitally- si.gned lost report would be instantaneously sent back to the complainant on mobile phone and at the given e-mail address for taking a print out in the format enclosed as Annexure-A. This application will also enable its verification online. The report so generated can be used for record or re-issue of duplicate lost document/article after obtaining identity proof for any authority. No enquiry or investigation is required to be conducted on the information received about the lost articles. This facility is not available for any loss due to theft or any crime and complainant shall contact police station in such cases. This information should be prominently displayed on the application as well as mentioned in the 'Lost Report' being issued through the system. Duties & Responsibilities The LT. Centre, PHQ and SCRBshall undertake the following jobs for Mobile App & web maintained, respectively :- 1. Development, maintenance, troubleshooting, upgradation/modification. 2. Security audit from any CERT.IN empanelled firm. 3. Uploading/hosting of App/web on respective App stores/web servers, 4. Payment of periodical charges to keep the application working. 5. text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. '13/ /2014 PROVIDING OF COPY OF FIR TO THE INFORMANT IVICTIM THROUGH SPEED POST -. DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO.if3"tL /2014 RECRUITMENT OF DRAFTSMAN (HEAD CONSTABLE) (TRACER) IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY [i] This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Draftsman (Head Constable) (Tracer) in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 17-B (xii)of the Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment)(Amendment) Rules, 2013. [ii] Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule-8 of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980.' Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply, Intimation regarding number of vacancies and details of recruitment process shall' be communicated to the Central Employment Exchange and. Sub-Employment Exchanges in Delhi. The vacancies shall be advertised in Employment News and leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi,Police website. Residerit Commissioners of all states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states. In the advertisements, full particulars' of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility requirements apply on the prescribed application form alongwith Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque of Rs. 100/-. The candidates belonging to SC/ST category and Ex-servicemen category are not required to send Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque alongwith the. application form. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board of the Delhi Police located at NewPolice Lines, Kingsway Camp, Delhi. [iii] The DCP/Establishment, Delhi will put up the vacancy position to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi about availability of vacancy. C.P. Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment. The decision regarding recruitment will be .communicated by DCP/Establishment, Delhi to DCP/Recruitment Cell, Delhi who willinitiate the process of recruitment. '2. MODE OF RECRUITMENT Vacancies in the rank of Draftsman (Head Constable) (Tracer) shall be filled through direct recruitment by holding 'various prescribed competitive examinations /tests. 1 3. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONANDOTHER STANDARDS (i) ~: 18<to 27 years. The upper age limit as prescribed above will be relaxable only in the followingcases:- - (a) Upto a maximum offiveyears ifa candidate belongs to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe category (b) Upto a maximum of 3 years ifa candidate belongs to an OBC category.. This relaxation is admissible to those castes notified in the Central List and the List issued by the Govt. of NCTof Delhi. (c) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible upto 35 years (38 years for OBC, 40 years for SCs/STs) for widows/divorced women and women judicially separated from their husbands and who are not re-married. (d) Upto a maximum of 5 years for sportsmen/sportswomen of distinction who have represented a state at the national level and the country at the international level in sports. The discipline of sports for which relaxation is available is mentioned in the Annexure - 'A'. document_title: Standing Order No. 389 : Anti Stalking Cell and Units in Delhi Police.
text: STANDING ORDER No. 389/2010 ANTI-STALKING CELL AND UNITS IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTION Prevention of crime against women has all along been a priority area for Delhi Police, and several measures have already been taken in this regard. One area where complaints have been voiced from time to time concerns women/ girls being followed/ stalked by undesirable elements thereby causing great mental harassment and a kind offear psychosis in the minds ofthe victims. In order to ensure redressal in complaints ofyoung women and girls about being stalked and harassed by known/unknown persons, it is proposed to set up an "Anti-Stalking Cell" for the redressal of such complaints. This will be another important step taken by Delhi Police in the efforts to prevent crimes against women in the city. 2. FUNCTIONING OF THE ANTI-STALKING CELL _____T_h~-2roROSed~'Anti-Stalking Cell,,_willhave~~hub-and_-~12oke" kind of arrangement with a central hub in the Crime Branch and the Districts setting up their own District Anti-Stalking Units. Involvement ofthe district police will be critical in as much as a substantial amount offollow-up work will be necessary in order to ensure prompt and effective redressal of complaints of this nature. f 3. CELL IN THE CRIME BRANCH 'The Anti-Stalking Cell in the Crime Branch which will be the nodal agency to centrally monitor all complaints ofstalking, will have the following modalities of functioning: (i) The "Anti-Obscene Call Cell" functioning at the Special Investigation Team (SIT)office in Sector 18, Rohini, will also function as the Central Anti-Stalking Cell. The toll-free number 1096 and the landline number ·2.7894455 which have been widely publicised as the contact numbers for the Anti-Obscene Call Cell will be utilized and publicised as the contact numbers for the central Anti-Stalking Cell. (ii) Once information regarding stalking is received by the central Anti- Stalking Cell, it willbe entered in a register which will contain columns for name, address and telephone number of the victim, the nature of complaint and details of the stalker. This register will be maintained as per the format given- at Annexure-"A". Action should be taken expeditiously and a woman police officer should be associated as and when required. 407 (iii) This information will then be conveyed simultaneously both to the concerned District Anti-Stalking Unit and to the police station concerned. The victim willalso be informed about the district unit's contact number and the police station to which her complaint has been forwarded. (iv) In some complaints, however, if it is felt that the matter should be straightway referred to the police station forprompt follow-upaction, the Central Cell will do the same under intimation to the District Anti-Stalking Unit. text: STANDING ORDER NO. 390 OF 2016 INCENTIVE FOR ARRESTING PROCLAIMED OFFENDERS. It has been noticed that a number of subordinate officers have taken keen interest in arresting Proclaimed Offenders. In order to recognize their hard work and commitment to duty it was decided to consider them for the grant of followingincentives, in addition to the rewards prescribed under Delhi Police (General Condition of Service) Rules, 1980. However, the followingnorms have been set up in order to have a uniform policy:- I. document_title: Standing Order No. 403 : "Jan Sanpark" An efforts to promote police-public partnership.
text: STANDINGORDER NO.403/2012. "JAN SAMPARK" - AN'EFFORT TO PROMOTE POLICE-PUBLIC PARTNERSHIP. Weshould engagethe community in our crime prevention activities, as much as we can, by organizing regular interactions with them. The common perception of the public is that the local level officers are not available to hear their grievances and do not respond to them satisfactorily. Weall hear members ofpublic in our officesand do our best to ensure that their complaints are properly looked into. However,it is felt that instead of members ofpublic comingto us, it is better that we reach out to them and meet them in their areas at, preferably a neutral venue like a'community center, public auditorium, college/school building etc., if they' are found available and suitable. Adequate notice should be given to the members of public in the area stating that Addl. CP/DCP or the Joint CP/Range would be available at a particular time and date where members of public can come and meet them without any prior appointment and air their grievances and submit their complaints and petitions. We can call this initiative 'JAN SAM PARK' and do it systematically so that every area gets covered. Localissue based 'Jan Sampark Sabhas' orpublic meetings to dispose ofpending complaints can be thought of. Complainants can be informed wellin advance about the date, time and venue ofsuch sabhas. It is left to the discretion ofDistrictDCsP/Addl.CsPto giveatheme to such interactions. Proper followup ofsuch complaints and grievances should be done and appropriate record should be maintained in the District officeregarding redressal ofthese grievances. Progress achievedin organizing these meetings may be communicated to the undersigned through proper channels. Goodwork done in disposing ofpending complaints, resolving local issues etc. will get due recognition. ~ (Neeraj Kumar) Commissioner of Police, Delhi. O.B. NO.12/2012 No.1260-1420/HAR/PHQ, dated Delhi the 16.7.2012. 451

document_title: Standing Order No. 404 : "YUVA" Police Initiative to engage young adults and street children in constructive activities to wean them away from crime.
text: STANDINGORDER NO. 404/2012. ~'YuvA"- POLICE INITIATIVE TO ENGAGE YOUNG ADULTS AND STREET CHILDREN IN CONSTRUCTIVE ACTIVITIES TO WEAN THEM AWAY FROM CRIME. Oflate, in some districts an effort has been made to involve street children and young adults in sports activities, vocational studies, painting workshops etc. Theideabehind this initiative has been towean awayyoung adults and under-privileged children, who for want ofproper educational and sports facilitiesmaytake to crime. This initiative needs tobe put 'on an -even keel by involvingNGOswho are working in the resettlement colonies, slums,jhuggi-jhopri clusters etc.,whichmay have becomebreedinggrounds for juvenile delinquency and potential criminals. Engaging young-adults and under-privileged children will enable them to encourage them to stay away from crime and may become a source ofcriminal intelligence as well. This initiative shall, henceforth, be called 'YUVA' and should involve -NGOs,corporate houses, social volunteers etc. It should be explained to the local officers that far from being a gimmick, such initiatives are taken by police forces acrossthe world and have proved to beverysuccessful in bringing the community and the police closerand in curbing street crime. Ifcarried out with sincerityona sustained basis, it would show our humane face and also keep petty crimes under -control. Such 'members of staff, who show keen interest in the initiative should be suitably rewarded. Concerned beat officersand division officers should be a part ofthis scheme. ThePoliceStations where such initiatives are necessary and possible should be identified in everydistrict and the scheme implemented. Progress achieved in this regard may be communicated to the undersigned through proper channels. ~ (Neeraj Kumar) Commissioner of Police, Delhi. document_title: Standing Order No. 408 : Duties of JWs especially deputed to visit child welfare committees for the services of summons, processes, orders etc.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. 408/2012 .DUTIES OF JWOs ESPECIALLY DEPUTED TO VISIT CHILD WELFARE COMMITTEES FOR THE SERVICES OF SUMMON~, PROCESSES, ORDERS ETC. INTRODUCTION: TheJuvenile Justice Committee ofthe Hon'ble High Court ofDelhi, in its meeting held with Principal Magistrates, Juvenile Justice Board, Chairpersons, Child Welfare Committee, police and other agencies, has observed that service of summons, processes, orders, etc. issued by the Child WelfareCommittees are invariable delayed. FUNCTIONING OF CHILD wELFARE COMMITTEES. The Committeefurther' observed that the Child WelfareCommittees' discharge important functions relating to care and protection of children and policeassistance in such matters is much needed to ensure presence ofpersons/officialsconcerned,verificationofantecedents and policereports in the matter of restoration/ adoption of children. It is, therefore, desired that policepersonnel shallbedeputed toassist the ChildWelfareCommittees in service ofsummons, processes, orders etc. COORDINATION BETWEEN POLICE AND CHILD WELFARE COMMITTEES. For the purpose of smooth functioning and better coordination between police and ·ChildW. elfareCommittee, it is hereby directed that all Districts/Units Addl.CsP/DCsP shall ensure strict compliance of the followingpoints approved by the Juvenile Justice Committee of Hon'ble High Court ofDelhi.- 1. Thepolicepersonnel from SJPU/District shall visit the ChildWelfare ,Committee concerned on every working day to collect summons, processes and orders. 2. SJPUs shallmakea record ofsummons /processes/orders socollected and ensure their timely service and respect to the Child Welfare Committees. 3. SHOs/JWOsshould be suitably directed to attend/visit ChildWelfare Committees in the matters related to their police stations when informed or directed by the Child WelfareCommittee. 4. Asstt. Commissioners of Police (l/C SJPUs) and InsprjSJPUs will hold regular meetings (once a month) with concerned Principal Magistrates ofJJB and Chairpersons of Child WelfareCommittee to resolvethe issues in the best interest ofchild. 467 These instructions should be brought to the notice ofall concerned fOfimmed~ate and meticulous compliance for establishing better raport 4th the Juvenile :yustice Boards and Child WelfareCommittees. . document_title: Standing Order No. 410 : Guidelines for initiating action against false complaints
text: STANDING ORDER No. 410/2012 Subject: - Guidelines for initiating action against false -complaints, Introduction:- Sometimes false complaints are made with a motive to use the police '" " to wreak vengeance an their opponents or settle personal scores. False complaints are also made to claim insurance money by cooking up false stories oftheft, robberies, fires or for grabbing properties. There are many other reasons forfilingfalse complaints and FIRswith police.In such cases, it is the duty ofpoliceto probe carefully, find out the truth and ensure that no innocent person gets unnecessarily harassed. Action by Police in such cases - (1) When a false FIRis registered: After concluding the investigation in such cases, the final report should be submitted ii]« 173 Cr.P.C. to the court and in the final report itself, the court may be requested to institute proceedings ix]« 182/211 IPCagainst the complainant who had got a false case registered by givingmisleading facts. (2) When a hoax call is made: When it becomes clear on enquiry that a hoax call has been made deliberately and maliciously, an enquiry r.eport, along with relevant evidence, should be submitted to the concerned court forinstitution ofproceedings u/s 182/211 IPCagainst "the offender. On being satisfied with the police report and available evidence, the court may issue notice to the offender or order the police to register a case against the offender and investigate the sarne. In serious matters in which hoax calls lead to delays offlights, trains, hamper court proceedings or cause heavy strain on resources ofpolice and other agencies causing inconvenience to public, the concerned police station should proceed against the offender u/s 66 Aofthe LT.(Amendment)Act- 2008, which is a cognizableoffenceand carries punishment 'upto 3 years. Allinvestigating officersand supervisory officersshould meticulously ensure compliance ofthese guidelineswhileinitiating action against falsecomplaints or hoax calls. ~ (NEERAJKUMAR) COMMISSIONEROF POLICE DELHI O.B. document_title: Standing Order No. 411 : Modalities to keep complainants posted of developments in cases/complaints lodged by them under the scheme "AAPKA UPDATE".
text: • 4 STANDING ORDER NO. I I OF 2012 MODALITIES TO KEEP COMPLAINANTS POSTED OF DEVELOPMENTS IN CASES/COMPLAINTS LODGED BY THEM UNDER THE SCHEME "AAPKA UPDATE" It is imperative that police officers keep complainants abreast of the developments in the enquiry/investigation underway in their complaints/cases registered in the police stations/units during enquiries/investigations. This grievance has been heard at various forums, including the recently held Jan Sampark Sabhas chaired by senior officers that the complainants are not informed of further progress in their matters. This creates unnecessary anxiety in the minds of complainants and generates a lot of ill-will for the police, in general. It has been, therefore, decided that complainants should be kept informed of the progress of their case/complaint at regular intervals through an institutional mechanism so that complainants' involvement in the status of their complaints/cases can help in fast tracking and in course correction of enquiry/investigation. This institutional mechanism will be called "AAPKA UPDATE". The following steps shall be taken for proper implementation of this scheme on receipt of a complaint/ registration of a case: 1. On receipt ?f a complaint/registration of an FIR, complainant should be asked whether he/she would like to be kept informed of the developments in his/her enquiry/investigation from time to time and his/her preferred mode of communication i.e. through SMS/mobile phone call/ post /personal visit etc. This information about the consent/willingness of the complainant along with relevant information will be recorded in the D.D. entry of the complaint/case registered, without fail. After this, the complainant shall be informed of the latest developments by concerned police officer every 15 days as per the means committed to the complainant. A proforma for providing information both in English and Hindi, is placed at Annexure "A' and "B'. 2. In case a complainant does not have a phone or does not live in the jurisdiction of the police station/unit so as to enable a personal visit, then the complainant shall be informed that he/she can visit the police station/unit for getting an "UPDATE" on the status of his/her enquiry/investigation from the concerned enquiry/investigating officer every Saturday between 4 to 6 p.m. in the police station/unit premises. It shall be the responsibility of the concerned ACP of the Sub Division/Unit to ensure that all the enquiry/investigating officers are present in the police station/unit premises at the - ' appointed time. In case an officer is on leave or on outstation duty, the Inspec!br (Investigation) of police station/other senior officer of the unit should have the information readily available for sharing with the complainant. 3. Under no circumstances, a complainant will be asked to visit again to find out the status of his/her complaint/FIR on a later date. In case of inability to provide information as per the schedule given above, concerned enquiry/investigating officer will ensure a personal visit at the residence of complainant to . . · .~ provide the required information on the date and time promised by him. 4. Any information which could hamper the er.iquiry/investigation

To ensure that the spirit behind this Standing Order is adequately conveyed to every enquiry/investigating officer in the Delhi Police, Joint CP and DCP concerned shall hold Sampark Sabhas at regular intervals with their officers and men so as to sensitize them and ensure proper implementation of the "AAPKA UPDATE" scheme. document_title: Standing Order No. 412 : Procedure for prosecution of Hookah Bars and smoking in public places, Hotels, Restaurants etc. in Delhi under COTPA-2003 and prohibition of smoking in public rules-2008.
text: .• 4/:Q STANDING ORDER NO. /2012 PROCEPURE FOR PROSECUTION OF HOOKAH BARS AND SMOKING IN PUBLIC PLACES. HOTELS. RESTAURANTS ETC. IN DELHI UNDER COTPA-2003 AND PROHIBITION OF SMOKING IN PUBLIC PLACE RULES-2008. This Standing Order aims to lay down rules and procedures related to prosecution of Hookah Bars and Smoking in Public Places, Hotels, Restaurants etc. in Delhi under the Cigarettes and other Tobacco products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (COTPA- 2003) and Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008, which has been enacted by the Central Govt. wherein; (i) Smoking has been prohibited in a public place; (a) Public Place means "any place to which the public have access, whether as of right or not, and includes auditoriums, hospital buildings, railway waiting rooms, amusement centres, restaurants, public offices, court buildings, educational institutions, libraries, public conveyances and the like which are visited by general public but does not include any open space" -Rule 3(L) of COTPA - 2003. (b) Smoking means, "smoking of tobacco in any form whether in the form of cigarette, cigar, beedis or otherwise with the aid of a pipe, wrapper or any other instruments;" - Rule 3(n) of COTPA -- 2003. (c) Tobacco means, "Cigarettes, Cigars, Cheroots, Beedis, Cigarette tobacco, pipe tobacco and hookah tobacco, Chewing tobacco, Snuff, Pan masala or any chewing material having tobacco as one of its ingredients (by whatever name called), Gutka, Tooth powder containing tobacco" - Rule 3(p) of COTPA - 2003 and as specified in the Schedule. -/~ (ii) The owner, proprietor, manager, supervisor or in charge of the affairs Of a hotel having thirty or more rooms or restaurant having a seating capacity of thirty persons or more and the manager of the airport may provide for a 'smoking area' - Rule 4 of Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008. (iii) The smoking area or space shall be a separately ventilated smoking room that - a) is physically separated and surrounded by full height walls on all four sides; b) has an entrance with an automatically closing door normally kept in closed position; c) has an air flow system i.e. exhausted directly to the. outside and not mixed back into the supply air for the other parts of the building; ·1 d) has negative air pressure in comparison with the remainder of the building; (iv) The smoking area or space shall not be established at the entrance or exit of the hotel, restaurant and the airport and shall be distinctively marked as "Smoking Area" in English and one Indian language, as applicable. (v) The smoking space shall be used only for the purpose of smoking and no other service(s) shall be allowed. (vi) The smoking rooms (in hotels having 30 or more rooms) so designated, shall form a separate section in the same floor or wing. In case of more than one floor / wings, the room shall be in one floor, as the case may

text: and shall be distinctively marked as "Smoking Area" in English and one Indian language, as applicable. (v) The smoking space shall be used only for the purpose of smoking and no other service(s) shall be allowed. (vi) The smoking rooms (in hotels having 30 or more rooms) so designated, shall form a separate section in the same floor or wing. In case of more than one floor / wings, the room shall be in one floor, as the case may be. -,;'(- L • (vii) The smoke from such room shall be ventilated outside and must not infiltrate I permeate into the non-smoking areas of the hotel / eating house. 1, (viii) "No Smoking Board" (as per Schedule II of the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008) should be displayed at the entrance of the public place. In case there are more than one entrance, at each such entrance and conspicuous place(s) inside. In case, if there are more than one floor, at each floor including the staircase and entrance of the lift(s) at each floor. (ix) The owner, proprietor, manager, supervisor or in-charge of the public place shall ensure that no ash-trays, matches, lighters or other things designed to facilitate smoking are provided in the public place. (x) The owner, proprietor, manager, supervisor or in-charge of a public place shall notify and cause to be displayed prominently the name of the person(s) to whom a complaint may be made by a person(s) who observes any person violating the provisions of these Rules. [As per the clarification sought from Directorate of Health Services, Govt. of NCT of Delhi, the Hookah / Sisha Bars/ Restaurants come under the purview of public places. Hookah Bars are violating the sections of Cigarette and Other . Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003 and Delhi Prohibition of Smoking and Non Smokers Health Protection Act 1996. Smoking is completely banned in public places as per Cigarette and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003 and Delhi Prohibition of Smoking and Non Smokers Health Protection Act 1996. Hookah is covered under the schedule of tobacco products mentioned under section 3{p) of COTPA 2003. Therefore, Ban on Hookah bars can be imposed]. I I PENALITY Any violation of the above mentioned provisions are compoundable and punishable with fine, which may extend to two hundred rupees as per Rule 21(1) of COTPA -2003. If the owner, proprietor, manager, supervisor or the authorized officer of a public place fails to act on a report of such violation, the owner, proprietor, manager, supervisor or the authorized officer shall be liable to pay fine equivalent to the number of individual offences - (Rule 3(3) of Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008). text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. '-//3 /2012 RECRUITMENT OF ASSTT.SUB-INSPECTORS(FINGER PRINT) IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Assistant Sub-Inspectors(Finger Print) in Delhi Police in accordance with Ruic 20-A-(l) of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. Recruitments for the said posts shall be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 of the Delhi Police !Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. Intimation regarding number of vacancies and details of recruitment process shall be communicated to the Central Employment Exchange and Sub-Employment Exchanges in Delhi. In addition, · the vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other l States. Vacancies shall also be published in the Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base I of the recruitment as the Delhi Police is a metropolitan police force. A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi Police website. Resident Commissioners of all the states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states. In the advertisements, full particulars of essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility requirements apply on the prescribed application forms alongwith Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque of°{ 100/-. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board of the Delhi Police located at New Police Lines , Kingsway Camp, Delhi. The candidates belonging to SC/ST category and Ex-servicemen category are not required to send Demand/Bank Drafts/Banker's Cheques alongwith their application forms. 2. MODE OF RECRUITMENT Vacancies in the rank of ASI(Finger Print) shall be filled by direct recruitment by holding presc;ribed competitive examinations. Page 1of13 ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATION (i) Age: 18 to 25 years. The upper age limit as prescribed above will be relaxablc only in the following cases:- (a) Upto a maximum of five years if a candidate belongs to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe category (b) Upto a maximum of 3 years if a candidate belongs to an OBC category. This relaxation is admissible for those castes notified in the Central List and the List issued by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi. (c) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible upto 35 years (38 years for OBC, 40 years for SCs/STs) for widows/ divorced women and women judicially separated from their husbands and who arc not re-married. (d) Upto a maximum of 5 years for sportsmen of distinction who have represented a state at the national level and the country at the international level in sports. The discipline of sports for which relaxation is available is mentioned in the Annexure - 'A'. If a candidate belongs to SC/ ST category and fulfills the above cri tcria, he is eligible for 5 years relaxation in upper age limit over and above the relaxation prescribed at Clause 3 (i)(a). In effect, he qualifies for

If a candidate belongs to SC/ ST category and fulfills the above cri tcria, he is eligible for 5 years relaxation in upper age limit over and above the relaxation prescribed at Clause 3 (i)(a). In effect, he qualifies for relaxation in the upper age limit to a maximum of 10 years. (e) Age concession to Ex-Servicemen will be allowed in accordance with the orders issued by the government from time to time. They will be permitted to deduct the period served in the armed forces from their actual age and the resultant age, so derived, should not exceed the prescribed age limit by more than three years. It is further clarified that an "Ex-Serviceman" means a person, who has served in any rank whether as a combatant or a non-combatant in the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Indian Union and who retiredfrom such service after earning his pension. (f) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible upto 40 years (43 years for OBC, 45 years for SCs/STs) for departmental candidates of Delhi Police. A "departmental candidate" means a person who has rendered a minimum of three years of regular and continuous service in the Delhi Police. Page 2of13 Candidates claiming benefits under OBC category shall be in accordance with castes notified in the Central List. This relaxation will also be admissible for candidates who are issued OBC certificates by the Govt. of NCT of Delhi. The certificates should be in the prescribed form issued by the competent authority empowered for the purpose. No other certificate will be accepted as sufficient proof. (ii) Educational Qualification:- Graduate in Science with Physics or Chemistry or Maths or Zoology or Anthropology Or Higher Secondary (10+2) with Science/Maths and having served for 3 years in any Finger Print Bureau. Or C.F.S.L. or F.S.L. personnel dealing with the science of Finger Prints or Single Digit Section of C.R.0. Or Serving Head Constables of Single Digit Section of Finger Print Bureau with at least 5 years service in the grade & 2 years experience of the trade. (iii) MEDICAL FITNESS/ STANDARDS The candidates should be of sound health, free from defect, deformity or disease. Both eyes should have a vision 6/ 12 with or without glasses. No relaxation is allowed to any category of candidates on this count. 4. The PE&MT test sheets and all legitimate corrections made would be personally attested by the DCP / ACP concerned with his name in capital letters in brackets and his office stamp with date. 11. APPELLATE BOARD FOR PHYSICAL MEASUREMENT One Addl.C.P & one A.C.P shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to constitute the appellate Board. The Board will consider the cases of such candidates who files an appeal against the Physical Measurement on the same day. There will be no appeal against the results in race, long jump and high jump events. 12. WRITTEN TEST AND EVALUATION OF ANSWER SHEETS (i) Those candidates who qualify the physical endurance & measurement tests shall be eligible to appear in the written test to be conducted by the recruitment board constituted in para 7. If required, additional number of DCsP / ACsP shall be provided for the conduct of the written examination. Page 7of 13 (ii) The paper shall be of 1 Y2 (one and half hour) duration and shall carry 100 marks. The paper shall be of an objective 1 type and include questions on General Knowledge/Awareness (25 marks), Arithmetic (25 marks), English (25 marks) and General Science (25 marks). (iii) The question paper shall be set by an officer of the rank of ,Joint C.P. nominated by the C.P. Delhi. It is the responsibility of the ,Joint C.P, so nominated to get the required number of copies of question booklets after ensuring confidentiality of the printing press, designing and printing of answer sheets in the form of OMR, packing of question booklets as per a seating plan and sealing of question papers in boxes and handing over the same to the Secrecy Officer. The DCP /Recruitment Cell, NPL will make the seating and other arrangements for the tests and for invigilation by G.Os/Inspectors/ Sis etc. ,Joint CP/Recruitment/Board shall supervise the whole examination to prevent copying or use of other dishonest practices. Any candidate found indulging in any unfair practice will be summarily removed from the written test and I debarred from further recruitments. 1, (iv) Alternatively, the Commissioner of Police, Delhi may entrust the task of conducting written test and evaluation of answer sheets to an independent agency. 13. INTERVIEW Successful candidates (depending upon the number of vacancies) shall be called to appear before the Selection Board for Interview on a date fixed by the Chairman of the Board. The Interview will be of 10 marks. The interview board will consist of one Joint C.P/Addl.C.P as Chairman, two DCsP as members and one Finger I Print Expert of the status of DCP shall be co-opted as ex-officio I member from any of the State Finger Print Bureau or from C.F.S.L. 14. FINAL RESULT /DISPLAY OF FINAL RESULT The final result will be prepared on the basis of marks obtained in the written test (100 marks) and Interview (10 marks). The list of successful candidates fas per the number of vacancies advertised (category-wise)] strictly as per merit shall be declared. Where equal marks have been obtained by candidates their merit will be Page 8of13 • fixed as per their dates of birth. The older candidate will be given preference and in case the date of birth is also the same, marks in the written test would decide the preference. Cases of selected candidates against whom any criminal case is registered/pending investigation/pending trial in the court, will be kept pending till the finalization of the same and their cases will be decided on merit after finalization of cases. The cases of departmental selected candidates, against whom any DE/PE/Cd.Case/Vigilance Enquiry etc. is pending, will also be kept pending till the finalization of the same and their cases will be decided on merits after finalization of ca_ses. The declaration of the result will be by displaying the lists of successful candidates for a week in the various Distt./Unit Hdqrs. on 4 / 5 notice boards, according to roll numbers, to avoid rush at any single notice board. It will also be displayed on the Delhi Police websites which is www.delhipolice.nic.in. 15. MEDICAL EXAMINATION The candidates so selected shall be medically examined by doctors in selected government hospitals in Delhi as per the prescribed standards. 16. VERIFICATION OF CHARACTER & ANTECEDENTS The verification of character & antecedents of the candidates as above will be done through concerned authorities expeditiously. If need be, special teams shall be sent to liaise with district authorities to expedite the police verification. 17. VERIFICATION OF GENUINENESS OF CASTE CERTIFICATE The verification of the genuineness of caste certificate m respect of each candidate selected against reserved vacancy of SC/ST/OBC will be got done from the concerned authority. MAINTENANCE OF RECRUITMENT RECORDS (i ) After evaluation and preparation of result sheets, the answer sheets will be scaled and handed over to the DCP / Incharge of recruitment for safe custody. Application forms/dossiers of candidates who fail in the examination and application forms/dossiers of candidates who are included in the merit list will be retained till the declaration of results of the next recruitment, (ii) Application forms/ dossiers of such candidates, whose appointment has not been done for one reason or the other, should be retained for a period of 3 years or till such time that the matter is finally disposed ofL The master sheets will also be retained for a period of three years. (iii) Representations received against the result announced should be retained in a separate file for a period of five years from the date of announcement of the final result_ The period can be extended beyond five years till the matter is finally disposed off in specific cases by the Sp!. CP/ Admn" Delhi. Application forms/ dossiers of selected/ appointed candidates may be sent to their respective places of posting for preparing their service record, Page 10of13 • J 20. TRAINING OF CANDIDATES (i ) On appointment, the candidates shall be required to undergo and successfully complete a 04 (four) months training course or as prescribed from time to time by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi and pass out of the Police Training College. (ii) The recruit ASI(Finger Print) should be specifically directed in the appointment letter to report at the PTC/PTS for training. They may be attached to any Distt./Unit for pay purposes, but their lien with the Distt./Unit starts and ends there. They should be under the disciplinary control of the Principal/PTS/PTC and they should not join any Distt./Unit unless they have passed out. In case any person is medically unfit then he/ she proceed on leave without pay and should re-join with the next batch. (iii) No recruit ASI(Finger Print) shall enter the ranks of Distts./Units to which he/she is allocated for the drawal of pay for any purpose whatsoever, unless he/she has successfully completed

text: the Distt./Unit starts and ends there. They should be under the disciplinary control of the Principal/PTS/PTC and they should not join any Distt./Unit unless they have passed out. In case any person is medically unfit then he/ she proceed on leave without pay and should re-join with the next batch. (iii) No recruit ASI(Finger Print) shall enter the ranks of Distts./Units to which he/she is allocated for the drawal of pay for any purpose whatsoever, unless he/she has successfully completed the training and has passed out of the PTC. (iv) Ordinarily, the services of those recruit ASI(Fingcr Print) who fail to qualify in the final examination will be terminated under Rule 5 of Central Civil Services Temporary Services Rules, 1965 by the Principal/PTC. However, one additional chance will be given to the failed trainees, and if he/she does not pass in all the papers even after availing the additional chance, his/her services will be terminated by the Principal/PTC. (v) The Principal/PTC shall be the competent authority for initiating/ finalizing (if the recruit is still in the PTC) disciplinary action against the recruitment AS!( Finger Print). He shall also be the competent authority to pass an order regarding termination of the services of a recruit ASI(Finger Print). In order to eliminate an unsuitable trainee from the force at the stage of his/her training itself, any one of the following grounds shall be sufficient for termination of services:- (a) Frequent absence of the trainee from outdoor/indoor programme leading to a conclusion that he/ she is an un dcvoted trainee and a habitual absentee, not likely to become a good police officer. Page 11of13 • (b) Submission of false Medical Certificates from any doctor for availing leave or light duty or rest. (c) Gross misconduct with the Indoor/Outdoor Instructors or with other trainees/staff. (d) If the performance of a trainee in the monthly tests and mid term examination is found to be very poor i.e. if he/ she is continuously obtaining less than 40% marks in monthly test. (e) If he/ she commits any mischief or any crime involving moral turpitude during his/her training. (0 If any information submitted by the trainee in his/her job application is found to be false, fabricated or manipulated to gain employment. (g) Any other ground which adversely reflects his/her behaviour and the officer is otherwise found unsuitable for Police services. text: STANDINGORDER NO. 383/2014 TACKLING THE PROBLEMS FACED BY STUDENTS AND OTHERS FROM NORTH EASTERN STATES IN DELHI. 1. Indian citizens hailing from the North Eastern States are residing in metropolitan cities and major urban areas across the country forthe pUr:P0seof education and employment. It has been reported time and again .that they are addressed with derogatory adjectives or face discrimination in the form of targeted attacks, assault, molestation and other atrocities. This has caused considerable anguish and. distress in the minds ofpersons from the North-Eastern States and isadverselyaffectingthe process ofnational integration. Itis therefore ofutmost importance that this feelingofinsecurity and negativity in the minds offellowcountrymen should be assuaged by an adequate and pro-active response. 2. text: STANDINGORDER NO. 385/09 GUIDELINES FOR PERMITTING COMMERCIAL USE OF FARM HOUSES FOR HOLDING SOCIAL FUNCTIONS 1. INTRODUCTION Farm Houses that fulfill requisite guidelines are permitted to hold social functions such as weddings, parties etc. The following guidelines were framed for holding social functions at Farm Houses by the GNCT of Delhi and approved by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in WP (C) No. 14261/04 - Bharastachar Virodhi Sangathan Vs. L.G., Delhi and Ors.:- 1. Farm Houses constructed as per sanctioned building plan and having sufficient parking space "(minimum 1acre for each 2.5 acre Farm area) inside their boundary wall may apply to the office ofthe Zonal Deputy Commissioner, MCD for holding social functions on their premises. The parking area within the Farm houses should be properly demarcated with separate Entry and Exit gates. Farm Houses owners shall depl~Y.J:heir ~wn securLtr-guards_ to.manage.the.parking-within- . - --the preIT;.ises. 2. Noparking shall be permitted outside the Farm Houses on the roadside and in the event of violations, the violators will be prosecuted in accordance with the law. ( '- 3. Only such Farm Houses should be selected which have proper access road .from main road to the Farm House. The minimum width of the access road to such Farm -House from the main road should be 60 feet. Farm Houses should not be located at a road which ends in a dead end. 4. For each social function, an amount ofRs.20, 000 / -per event for Farm House ofS acres and above, and Rs. 10,000/- per event for Farm House below 5 acres but not less than 2.05 acre would be levied by the DDA or the MCD as the case may be. Booking of Farm House (s) by MCD,may done through Citizen Services Bureau (CSB)/Internet. 5. . Acommittee under the Chairmanship ofthe Zonal Deputy Commissioner, with the Asstt. Commissioner of Traffic Police, ACP(Sub- Division), .Divisional Fire Officer, the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, and a representative of DDA in case of DDA Area Land, would scrutinize such applications. 6. Permission should be given on rotational basis with in the munici pal zone so that each Farm House is not used for more than 120 days in a year. Permission should be based on factors such as number ofguests, approximate number ofvehicles, nature of function etc. 403 7. Farm Houses shall take special precautions regarding use ofnoiseless generators, use of loudspeakers, musical instruments etc., so that noise pollution levelremains within the permissible limitin conformity with the guidelines j norms issued by CPCBj DPCC. Similarly,use of fire-crackers within and outside the Farm Houses should be within the permissible limit and the air pollution levelshould not exceed the prescribed limits stipulated by the CPCBjDPCC. 8. Noloudspeakers and bands should be permitted beyond 10 PM. 9. Processions and horse-drawn carriage should not be permitted on the roads outside the Farm Houses. 10. text: 3St/Jo Standing Order No. STANDING ORDER ON THE GRANT OF CINEMA LICENCE AND THE FUNCTIONING OF THE CINEMA SECTION OF LICENSING UNIT 1. DERIVATION OF POWER As per Section 146 (1) of the Delhi PoliceAct, 1978, the Commissioner of Police is empowered to exercise all powers and discharge all functions which may be exercised or discharged by a District Magistrate under the Acts mentioned in ScheduleI (and the rules made thereunder) which includes the Cinematograph Act, 1952. As per Rule2(r) of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 "Licensing Authority" means the authority defined in section 11 of the Cinematograph Act, 1952 which saysthat the "Authority having power to grant licenses under this part shall be the District Magistrate". The 'District Magistrate' in Delhi, as per the aforesaid section of the Delhi PoliceAct, 1978' means the Commissioner of Police. Therefore, all the powers vested in the 'District Magistrate' as mentioned in the Cinematograph Act, 1952 and the Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 are to be exercised by the ~ Commissionerof Police, Delhi, who hasfurther delegated the same to Addl, Commissioner of Pollee, Licensing vide order No.83- 182/SpI.Cell/PHQdated 01.02.2008. 2. POWERS 2.1 Under the Delhi Cinematograph Act, 1952 and the Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008, the District Magistrate i.e. Add!. Commissionerof Police,Licensinghasbeenempoweredto grant:- i) Proyisional Certificate ProvisionalCertificate is issuedunder Rule-4 of the Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008 for erecting a Cinema building or converting an existing building wholly or partly into a placeof exhibition of Cinematograph. ii) Cinematograph License Cinematograph License is granted for a period of ten years under Rule3 of DelhiCinematograph Rules,2008 read with Section 10of TheCinematographAct, 1952. iii) Renewal of Cinematograph License The license initially shall be granted for a period of ter years and thereafter it will be renewed after every ten years for which application shall be made six months in advance, as per Rule-7 read with Rule-3 of Delhi Cinematograph Rules,2008. Iv) Casual performance License A casuallicensefor a period not exceedingsevendays is granted in respect of any place for exhibition of films under Rule-3 (2) of the Delhi Cinematograph. Rules, 2008. v) Temporarv Permit A Temporary Permit for two months at a time and not more than six months in all, can be granted in casethe license is not renewed before the expiry of the license due to reasons beyond the control of the Licensing Authority and not directly attributable to the licensee under Rule-8of the DelhiCinematograph Rules,2008. vi) Sanction for alteration/repairs No alteration In any portion of the licensed place can be made without the sanction of the Licensing Authority, under Rule-22 of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008. Similarly no repairs or re-decorations necessitating the use of scaffolding, cradlesetc. can be done without the sanction of the licensingauthority, if it is Intended that the public shall be admitted while such scaffolding, cradles etc. are in position, as per rule 23 of DCR,2008. vii) Reyision of Admission Rate of Cinema Tickets 8t Classification of seats Revision of Admission Rate of Cinema Tickets and Classificationof Seats is dealt with under Rule-13 DCR-200S. 2.2

For this purpose, the licensing authority shall include the Local Police andTraffic Policeaspart of the inspectingteam. 2 ii) Inspection on receipt of application for grant of Cinematograph licenceor its renewal On receipt of an application for grant or renewal of a Cinematograph licence, along with the prescribed licence fee and inspection fee, the place shall be inspected by the inspecting team (Rule 12 DCR- 2008). iii) Annual Inspection of a licensed place A joint inspection of the Cinema Halls shall be carried out by the inspecting team, at least once in a year as per Rule 17 of Delhi Cinematograph Rules, 2008. iv) Bi-Annual Inspection of a licensed place As per directions of Hon'ble Lt. Governor, Delhi received vide GNCfO's letter No.F18/0S/1999/HP- II/69 dated 07.01.2009, Bi-Annual (six monthly) inspection of the Cinema Halls shall be carried out. v) Surprise Inspection Surprise inspection can be carried out at any time by the licensing authority. Location of building The building shall be located on a street or other public ways or open space and shall fulfill the requirements of byelaws for such types of buildings from which there are at all time free means of exit and not more than seventy per cent of space of the building shall be allowed for use other than exhibition of cinematograph. 2. External Walls (1) Materials used in the construction of external walls and party walls shall conform to the provisions of the National Building Code of India 2005, 'Building Materials". (2) In case, the building is in close proximity to another building, it shall be separated therefrom by walls and structures of fire resisting material in a manner to be approved by the building authority/Chief Fire Officer and no opening in the walls or in any part of the building such as may be liable to communicate fire shall overlook the neighbouring building. 3. Structural requirements (1) The building shall fulfill the requirements of fire resistance of different structural elements composing it, in accordance with the National Building Code of India 2005, Part 4, 'Fire and Life Safety'. (2) The building shall be enclosed within proper external or party walls of bricks, stone concrete (plain, hollow or reinforced) and the floors, tiers and roofs of the auditorium and all parts used by the public shall be constructed of fire-resisting material conforming to class 1 rating as per IS 12777: 1989: PROVIDEDthat the following materials may be used for the ceiling, namely:-- (a) Accoustic Celotex, (b) Asbestos Spray, (c) Canoc, (d) Seletex, (e) Heraklith, (f) Insulite Building Board (Termitex), and Insulite Hard Board and Tyuzne Wexna, Insulation Board, (g) Insulwood, Treatax, (h)Acoste Sound Insulation Board, (i) Light Crete Unika Sound Insulating, (j) Boards and Unitene, (k) Accoustic Tiles, (I) Gypsum Panel Board, (m) Thermocaustic, (n) Thermofriez. (3) No wooden posts shall be allowed for the support of galleries and tiers. No soft wood or other inflammable wall linings, partitions, screens or barriers shall be used in any part of the auditorium, and no cavities shall be left behind any linings. (4) The fronts or private boxes and each tier shall be formed of fireproof material, except at capping of boxes, which may be of wood. (5) The structural design of foundations, elements of masonry, timber plain concrete, reinforced concrete, pre-stressed concrete and structural steel shall be carried out in accordance with Part 6, 'Structural Design', Section 1 to 7 of National Building Code of India 2005. Height of tiers In case, the first tier or gallery extends over the stalls, the height between the floor of the stalls and such tier or gallery shall not in any part be less than three thousand millimeter, the height between the floor of the highest part of the gallery and the lowest part of the ceiling over the same shall not in any part be less than three thousand six hundred millimeter, the height between tier and the tier of ceiling above it shall in no case be less than twenty four hundred millimeter. 7. SEATING (1) The seating in the building shall be so arranged that there is free access to exits. (2) The distance between back of one row of seats to the back of another row of seats immediately behind it shall not be less than nine hundred millimeter where push back seats are used, or nine hundred eight millimeter in case of fixed seats. The width of the seat shall not be less than five hundred millimeter in case arms are provided and four hundred fifty millimeter in case of without arms. (3) The rows of seats shall be so arranged that there is a clear space of not less than three hundred eighty millimeter between the back of the seat and the foremost portion of the seat arm of frame just behind, measured between perpendiculars. (4) All seats, except in private boxes up to fourteen seats, shall be securely fixed to the floor, and if battened together or made in links, the complete links shall be firmly attached to the floor. GANGWAYS (1) Clear passages or longitudinal gangways shall be formed at the sides and down the center of the seating (seating between sides) in every part of the auditorium in such manner that no seat shall be more than seven seats, including the seat occupied i.e. not more than fourteen seats in a row between two gangways, away from any of the gangways:- (a) The width of the main longitudinal gangway shall not be less than twelve hundred millimeter and the width of the side longitudinal gangway shall not be less than one thousand millimeter. (b) At least two longitudinal gangways shall directly be connected to the exit door. For this purpose, if the side longitudinal gangways are connected to the exit door, the width of the same shall not be less than twelve hundred millimeter. (2) Cross gangways of not less than one thousand millimeter wide shall be provided parallel to the line of seating so as to provide direct access to the exit. At least one cross gangway shall be required for every ten rows. (3) All gangways exits and the treads of steps and stairways shall be maintained with non-slippery surfaces. (4) Druggests, matting and floor covering, if provided, in gangways shall be securely fastened on the floor. Lighting arrangement shall be provided along or on the sidewalls or step lights to facilitate the public in finding the way to their seats or to go outside during the show. In case of step lights, their supply voltage should not be more than twenty-four volts. (5) The exit of the gangways, and passage leading to exit, shall be kept clear of any obstruction. (6) If steps have to be inserted in a gangway or passage there shall be not less than three steps at anyone place. The treads shall not be less than three hundred millimeters wide and shall be of uniform riser and tread. (7) The height of parapet in galleries shall not be less than nine hundred millimeters. 9. (3) The treads and risers of steps on each flight shall be uniform; Provided that in case of elliptical and other curved forms of stairs the tread on inner side shall not be less than two hundred fifty millimeter. (4) No staircases shall have more than two flights of fifteen steps without a turn and the width of the landing between such flights shall be at least the same as the width of the staircase. (5) Stairs turning at an angle shall have a proper landing without winders being introduced at the turn. (6) All staircases shall have, on both sides, strong handrails firmly secured to the wall by strong metal brackets about seventy five millimeter clear there form and about nine hundred millimeter above the stairs and shall be continuous and extend not less than three hundred millimeter beyond the top and bottom steps. (7) There shall be no recesses of projections in the walls of such staircases within fifteen hundred millimeter of the floor and any fittings for lighting shall be at least two thousand millimeter above the steps or landing. (8) The minimum headroom in a passage under the landing of a staircase shall not be less than twenty two hundred millimeter. The minimum clear headroom in any part of staircase shall be less than twenty two hundred millimeter. (9) No stairways shall discharge into the passage or corridor against or across the direction of exit. (10) In case ramps are provided, slope shall not be greater than 1:12 for short distance up to nine hundred millimeter and the ramps shall be surfaced with non-slipping material. The width of the ramp shall not be less than fifteen hundred millimeter. (11) The ramp shall have handrails on both sides at a height of nine hundred millimeter measured from the surface of the ramp and shall extend three hundred millimeter beyond the top and bottom of the ramp. ENTRANCE (1) There shall be at least one entrance for each class in the auditorium. (2) At least one entrance usable by a person with disabilities in wheel chair shall be on a level that would make the elevator accessible. 11. EXITS (1) Every 'public portion of the building shall be provided with adequate number of clearly indicated exits placed in such position and so maintained as to afford the audience ample means of safe and speedy egress upon public thoroughfare. (2) In the auditorium there shall be at least one exit from every tier, floor or gallery for every one hundred fifty persons accommodated or part thereof; Provided that an exit on or by way of stage or platform shall not be reckoned as one of the exits required by this rule. (3) Every exit from the auditorium shall provide a clear opening space of not less than two meter high and not less than two meter wide. (4) Exits from the auditorium shall be suitably placed and spaced along both sides and along the back thereof and shall deliver into two or more different thoroughfares or open space from which there shall be at all times free means of rapid dispersal. (5) Every passage or corridor leading from an exit in the auditorium to a destined place of exit from the building shall be of such width as in the opinion of the licensing Authority enable the persons in an emergency, to leave the building without danger or crowding or congestion. At no point shall any passage or corridor be less than two meters wide and it shall not diminish in width in the direction of the final place of exit. (6) The combined width of the final place of exit from the building shall be such the there are at least five hundred millimeter of exit width for every 60 persons. (7) All exit doors shall open outwards and shall be so fitted that when opened they do not obstruct any gangway, passage, corridor, stairway or landing. (8) All the exit doors and doors through which the public have to pass on the way to open air shall be available for exit during the whole time when the public is inside the building and during such time these doors shall not be locked or bolted. Enclosure for Cinematograph and lighting. Subject to regulation 19 an independent permanent enclosure of sufficient size to allow the operator to work freely shall be provided in each auditorium in the building. 19. If a permanent enclosure as required by regulation 18, is not available, the cinematograph machine shall be contained in an enclosure formed of a smoke proof cabin constructed of sheet iron on suitable framework and fastened together securely. The cabin floor shall, if provided with boards, be covered with asbestos or other fire resisting material having half-an-hour fire rating and capable of supporting weight of two men. 20. The necessary pipes and cables shall enter the enclosure through efficient bushed openings. 21. No unnecessary combustible material shall be allowed within the enclosure, and all combustible materials necessary for exhibition of cinematograph shall be kept in fireproof receptacles suitable for the purpose. 22. No unauthorized person shall be allowed to enter or be in the enclosure while an exhibition is in progress. 23. The enclosure, generator room, air conditioning plant room, sub-station and ail switch rooms shall be out of bound to the public. 24. Projector apparatus and film Cinematograph projectors shall be placed on firm supports constructed of fire resisting materials and shall be provided with a metal shutter, so that it can be readily inserted between the source of light and film gate. This shutter shall immediately be dropped in the event of an accident to the cinematograph apparatus or stoppage of the film and shall only be raised when the film is in motion for the purpose of projection. 25. A separate room of fire resisting construction shall be constructed for film rewinding and the room shall not be used for any other purpose except for storing the films not in use. It shall not however, be necessary to have a separate room for rewinding films with acetate base or other safety film. 26. Lighting and electrical installation. (1) All lighting shall be provided by electricity. No gas, acetylene, oil or other lamps shall be used for lighting the licenced place. (2) Every portion of the licenced place, devoted to the use or accommodation of the public and also all outlets leading outside the licenced place including the corridors, shall be well and properly lighted during every exhibition and the same shall be lighted until the entire public have left the licenced place after the exhibition is over. (3) Sufficient emergency lighting shall be provided for use in case of failure of the electric lighting in the auditorium, gangways, passage, staircases and exits ways and these lights should be supplied required electrical power from an inverter or similar other power device and this should switch on automatically on failure of main electric supply. 27. Sanction of electrical Inspector to be obtained to be obtained for all electrical works. Before the installation of electric light or any electrical apparatus and before any alterations or additions to the electric installation are commenced, the sanction of the electrical inspector shall be obtained through the licensing authority and for this purpose plans showing the approximate position of lights, fans and such other fittings and specifications giving full particulars of the proposed work shall be forwarded to the electrical inspector to whom complete drawings shall also be sent on completion of the work. -1"7 28. MAIN CIRCUITS. (1) An auditorium when illuminated by electric light, it shall have preferably three separate and distinct main circuits and these circuits shall be :- (A) For the stage; (8) For auditorium; and (C) For corridors, exits and other parts of the premises open to the public (2) The circuits (B) and (C) shall be arranged that the lights in the auditorium, corridors, exits and other parts of the premises open to the public shall be as far as possible equally distributed on these two circuits. The circuits (8) and (C) shall neither be combined in one fitting nor shall the wires or leads of one circuit be placed in the casino or conduits of other circuit. 29. SUB-CIRCUITS. (1) The main circuits shall be sub-divided so that no sub-circuit shall be allow to carry more than six Amperes electric current in the case of Auditorium, corridors, exits and other parts of the premises, open to the public. And an electric current of 20 amperes with 230 volts in the case of the stage. Each sub- circuit shall start from a distributing board. (2) The main electric line for Circuit "A" shall, where possible be kept entirely on the stage side of the proscenium wall and those for circuit "8" and "C" entirely on the auditorium side of that wall. (3) The light inside and outside the premises shall be on separate circuits. Circuits for fans, power and cooling purposes shall be kept distinct and separate from lights circuits. 30. Emergency Lights Circuit. (1) The emergency lights circuit shall be so arranged that one emergency lighting circuit shall supply not less than three lamps arranged so as to avoid, as

text: side of the proscenium wall and those for circuit "8" and "C" entirely on the auditorium side of that wall. (3) The light inside and outside the premises shall be on separate circuits. Circuits for fans, power and cooling purposes shall be kept distinct and separate from lights circuits. 30. Emergency Lights Circuit. (1) The emergency lights circuit shall be so arranged that one emergency lighting circuit shall supply not less than three lamps arranged so as to avoid, as far as possible, a single fault extinguishing all the lamps. (2) Two way control from both inside and outside the enclosure may be adopted for the emergency lighting circuit and the control from outside the enclosure should be suitably indicated, it shall not be mounted on the same board as any of the general circuits and should be placed in such a position as to be readily handled by an employee of the licencee but inaccessible to the public. 31. Control of Auditorium lights from stage. If so required to control a portion of the lights in the auditorium from the stage switchboard (Circuit A) this will be permitted if a sufficient number of lights for safety purposes be maintained on circuit Band C for each portion of the auditorium entirely independent of the stage. The number and position of such lights shall be subject to the approval of the electrical inspector. 32. Control of auditorium lights from enclosure. In the case of cinemas, it may be permitted to control a portion of the lights in the auditorium by switches placed in the enclosure, provided these switches are of totally closed metal clad type and associated with Earth Leakage Circuit Breakers and/or Miniature Circuit Breakers of not more than 16 Amperes capacity at a pressure not exceeding 230 volts. The number and position of such switches shall be subject to the approval of the electrical inspector or any other officer authorize by him. 33. Three phase alternating current system. In case the electric supply is available on three phases alternating current system, the circuits A, Band C shall be supplied from three different phases and the electrical load shall be equally distributed on all the three phases. Special precautions shall be taken to prevent accidental connection of different circuits. 34. Source of supply. Changeover switches shall be used in case the electric supply is to be drawn from two different sources. 35. Auxiliary supply of exit sign. All exits signs shall be fitted with an auxiliary bulb capable of properly illuminating the sign and these bulbs shall be fed and from battery/batteries or inverters or similar emergency power sources capable of giving emergency supply for thirty minutes and the same shall be in fully charged condition before the first admission of the public on any day. 36. Torches. At least six electric torches (with four cells of 1.5 volts each) shall be kept in the each auditorium in proper working condition and these shall be distributed in the auditorium so

Torches. At least six electric torches (with four cells of 1.5 volts each) shall be kept in the each auditorium in proper working condition and these shall be distributed in the auditorium so as to be easily accessible to gatekeepers. 37. Electric supply to other premises. No other building shall be supplied with electric current from the mains/Miniature Circuit Breakers/Diesel generators used for such building. 38. Gas or water piDes. Gas or water pipes shall never be a part of "any electrical circuit. 39. Electric conductors. All electric conductors used within the building shall be tinned copper or electrolytic copper or Stranded Aluminum as per relevant Bureau of Indian Standards Code. 40. Insulation. All electric conductors shall be properly insulated and the insulation resistance shall not be less than as prescribed under the relevant provisions of the Electricity Rules, 2005: 41. Special precautions for electric conductors, etc. No metal work in connection with the electric circuits shall be exposed or so fixed or constructed as to be liable to cause a short circuit. In all cases electric conductors conveying current at high pressure inside the building shall be specially insulated. These conductors shall be enclosed in screw-jointed and earthed iron or steel tubing. Armored cable may be used for the Electricity Supply service. 42. Joints. Joints in electric conductors shall be avoided as far as possible but in exceptional cases the joint shall be electrically and mechanically perfect and shall be made by using requisite cable jointing kit. Soldering fluids shall not be used in making such joints, and no joints shall be made in metal conduit. No joint under any circumstances shall be allowed in flexible and/or portable wires/cables. 43. Electric Conductors fixing and protection. (1) The conductor including lead covered cable, accessible to the public, shall be efficiently protected from mechanical injury by external armour of iron or steel. (2) In case the conductor passes through or within the wall, fire proof floors or ceilings, the conductor shall be protected by iron pipes or by glazed stone-ware or porcelain tubes and precautions shall be taken to prevent the possibility of fire or water passing along the course of the conductor. (3) The conductor shall not be installed near the place liable to be heated by jets stem pipes or other appliances. (4) In special cases, or where necessary for protection from the depredations of rats, mice or other vermin, the wiring shall be enclosed in heavy gauge steel conduit. 44. Petrol engines No petrol driven engine shall be allowed in the building or premises for generating electric current. 45. Metallic tubing and mechanical protection In case iron or tube is used as a mechanical protection, bushing shall be provided wherever necessary

(4) In special cases, or where necessary for protection from the depredations of rats, mice or other vermin, the wiring shall be enclosed in heavy gauge steel conduit. 44. Petrol engines No petrol driven engine shall be allowed in the building or premises for generating electric current. 45. Metallic tubing and mechanical protection In case iron or tube is used as a mechanical protection, bushing shall be provided wherever necessary and properly bushing inspection boxes shall be used. All metallic tubing shall be efficiently earthed and shall be providing screw joints or other means of ensuring a good and permanent electrical connection, which shall be continuous with boxes and other fittings. 46. Stage Lights. In case auditorium or stage is used for a dramatic performance, special care shall be taken that all works in connection with the electric lighting of the stage are carried out in a substantial manner best possible, preferably in heavy gauge screwed metal conduit. 47. Stage switchboard. (1) In case auditorium or stage is used for dramatic performance, a switchboard fitted with the necessary switches, Earth Leakage Circuit Breakers, Miniature Circuit Breakers and other fittings for the control and regulation of the stage lighting shall be fixed in some convenient positions overlooking the stage. (2) Electric connections shall be made as far as possible at the back of the board and there shall be space of not less than 900mm between the wall and the back of the board or such larger space as many be necessary to ensure the thimbles and connection being at all times easily accessible, or, as an alternative in the case of wires not larger that 7/18 S.W.G. provisions may be made by hinging the board for rendering the back of the board accessible. 48. Footlights, etc. The footlights shall be properly protected from anything liable to cause a short circuit and shall be protected by a stuff guard so arranged that no flammable material such as posters, interior decoration material etc. can come in contact with lamps. 49. Enclosure (1) Within the enclosure no readily combustible material shall be used in connection with any lamp in such a manner that it may come in contact with the lamps or conductors. The insulating material of an electric cable including unprotected leads to lamps in the enclosure shall be covered with fire resisting material. (2) There shall be no coil of slack electric cable within the enclosure. The leads to the cinematography lamp shall, unless conveyed within a metal pipe or other suitable casing, be kept well apart both within and without the enclosure so that course of each may be readily traced. All live parts in the enclosure shall at all times, be totally covered by insulating and the fireproof material. 50. The electric cable for the cinematograph apparatus shall be taken as separate circuit from the source of supply and there shall be an efficient link iron clad switch and
