Resistanee (1) Resistance frame shall be made entirely of fire resisting material and shall be so constructed and maintained that no outside part shall at any time become unduly heated. The resistance shall not be permitted to become so over-heated that a piece of dry newspaper placed in contact with any part would readily burn. (2) All resistance with the exception of their resistance for regulating purposes shall be placed outside the enclosure and preferably outside the auditorium. They shall be adequately protected by wire guards or other efficient means of preventing accident contact. 52. Plug sockets for stage The plug sockets for the stage shall be of Bakelite or similar fireproof material and of especially substantial construction. 53. leads to battens, etc. The leads to battens and moveable lengths shall be specially guarded particularly at the pints where they join on to the battens and moveable lengths and a sufficient length shall be allowed to prevent the leads receiving any injury through any movement of the battens. This part of the leads shall be protected by stout canvas hose properly fixed and the battens shall be suspended by at least three ropes. 54. Arc lamps (1) The arc lamps shall not be used in the auditorium or in any part open to the public without permission of the electrical inspector. In case arc Lamps are used in any part of such building, special precautions shall be taken to guard against danger from falling glass and incandescent particles of carbon. All parts of the lamps, lanterns and fittings that are liable to be handled (except by the persons employed to handle them) shall be insulated from the framework. (2) Any exposed portion of metal work of an arc lamp liable to become heated to a temperature sufficient to cause a conflagration by contact with scenery or other inflammable material shall be protected by a wire guard. In no case, arc lamps shall be hanged by the conductors. 55. Cut-outs (1) All circuits shall be efficiently protected by Moulded Case Circuit Breakers/Miniature Circuit Breakers/Earth Leakage Circuit Breakers as required and placed in positions easily accessible to the staff but inaccessible to the public. (2) All switches, Moulded Case Circuit Breakers, Miniature Circuit Breakers etc. shall be so marked as so to identify

Cut-outs (1) All circuits shall be efficiently protected by Moulded Case Circuit Breakers/Miniature Circuit Breakers/Earth Leakage Circuit Breakers as required and placed in positions easily accessible to the staff but inaccessible to the public. (2) All switches, Moulded Case Circuit Breakers, Miniature Circuit Breakers etc. shall be so marked as so to identify clearly which circuit or lamp or fan or apparatus thy control. (3) All switches, Moulded Case Circuit Breakers, Miniature Circuit Breakers, Ceiling roses and wall sockets, shall have non- flammable bases and covers. (4) All switches shall be of ample size to carry the current for which they are intended without heating and shall be so constructed that they shall not remain in any position intermediate between the "on" and the "off" position so as to permit of an arc or shot circuit. 56. fittings (1) All fittings shall be fixed in an approved manner and special care be taken to avoid risk of the failing from any cause. (2) Combined gas and electric fittings shall not be used. (3) Any electric light pendants or brackets, in the auditorium and front of the house generally shall be a least 2500 mm above the floor to the lowest projecting part of the fittings. No electric fittings or apparatus of any description shall be so fixed or arranged as to interfere any time with the proper work of the safety curtain. 57. Switch and fuse boards (1) All switch and switch board, not fitted with front connections, shall be so mounted as to give instant and easy access to the connection at the back to the board and shall be provided with dividing strips between poles both at the back and in front and proper look up case with glass or metal fronts.' The glass, unless of adequate thickness, shall be protected with a wire guard or alternatively boxes with lids and sides rendered fireproof by asbestos sheeting may be used. (2) Switch and switchboards shall be fixed inaccessible place where they will not obstruct any passage or exit. 58. Generating plant In case the supply of electric current is derived from special plant in the building or the premises, such plant must in'all cases be approved by the electrical inspector. The main storage diesel tank (1000/990 liters in case of diesel generating plants/sets shall be installed outside the licensed premises. Only day/short time fuel tank of capacity around 500 liters may be allowed inside near to diesel generation plant/set. The flow of diesel from main diesel tank installed outside the building or premises to the day/short time fuel tank should be through pipes either with gravitation flow or through motor pump. In case of any fire the flow of diesel from main tank to short tank will be shut off through an automatic shut off valve/damper. 59. Diesel Generation Sets In

The flow of diesel from main diesel tank installed outside the building or premises to the day/short time fuel tank should be through pipes either with gravitation flow or through motor pump. In case of any fire the flow of diesel from main tank to short tank will be shut off through an automatic shut off valve/damper. 59. Diesel Generation Sets In case the diesel generating sets used for supply of electricity to said building necessary provisions shall be made for keeping the temperature of diesel engine rooms (couple to the alternator of the diesel generating set/s) within proper limits. 60. Accumulators Electrical Accumulators, unless installed in rooms or compartments specially reserved therefore, shall be completely enclosed together with the terminals in substantial castings constructed of or lines with insulating and fire resistinq material. Accumulators in cells or containers of celluloid shall not be installed, stored or used. 61. Transforming and converting machinery (1) Transforming and converting machinery with the controlling switches and circuit breakers shall be placed in a fire proof and water proof structure, adequately ventilated to the outside air, properly lighted and accessible to the management and shall be used for no other purpose. (2) The dry type of transformer only, shall be installed inside the building premises on ground floor or in the first basement at eh periphery of the basement with winding temperature, over current, earth fault and other protections as required/provided in the Electricity Rules. (3) The high-tension /high voltage (1100 volts) circuits breaks provided on the primary side of the transformer shall be dry type only viz. vacuum or SF6 circuit breaker or any other dry type circuit breaker. (4) The high voltage/medium voltage cables used in the electric installation of the building shall be of fire retardant low smoke (FRLS) cables or the cables shall be coated with fire retardant composition/paint/chemical. (5) No transformer of electric supply company shall be slowed in the building or premises, which is not supplying electricity to the said building. (6) A clear space of 1000 mm for a transformer up to a rating of 500 KVA and D.G. Set up to a rating of 200 KVA, a clear space of 1250 mm for transformer above 500KVA and D.G. set above 200 KVA shall be provided for easy operation maintenance without any hazard to the operation and maintenance personnel working near the equipment and also for ensuring adequate ventilation. (7) A clear space of 2000mm shall be kept in between the generators, if two generators are installed side by side. (8) The distribution transformer and Diesel Generating Set shall not be located on any floor other than a ground floor or first basement of the building. 62. High Voltage In case the primary current is of high voltage no part of such apparatus or the control thereof shall be accessible to any person except the person-in-charge of its maintenance.

Earthing of covers All metal work supporting or protecting electric supply lines shall be efficiently earthed by two separate and distinct connections with the earth. The resistance of the connections with the earth shall not exceed on ohm, and all earthing leads shall run in such a manner that the sources of each may be readily traced. In case earthing lead pass through walls or are laid in floors they shall be SUitable protected. 64. Motors, etc. All motors and electrical apparatus of power more than 300 Watts shall not be used inside the building without prior permission of the Electric Inspector, however electric fans and similar motors not taking more than 300 watts may by used, if separately wired, from switches/Miniature Circuit Breakers on a proper distribution board. 65. Plan of wiring A framed diagram indicating clearly the arrangement of all circuits and sub-circuits of the electrical installation, the position of distribution boards, and the size of cables shall be displayed at the auspicious place in the building and shall be kept to up to date. 66. Temporary lighting (1) In all cases of installing temporary lights, a notice of not less than seven days, shall be given to the electrical inspector in writing before it is desired to commence the work. (2) The wires and cables shall be adequately and firmly fixed and shall be similar to the wires already specified in these regulations and in cases where the wires are within reach of the public they shall be efficiently protected from mechanical injury by an armour of iron or steel. (3) All temporary works shall be immediately removed if no longer required for the purpose for which it was installed. In the case of temporary work on the stage, all connections to the permanent installation shall be removed immediately after the performance in which they are used, unless permission is obtained. Such special conditions as may be requisite each case may be attached by the electrical inspector for using temporary electric work. 67. Shock treatment instructions and insulated glove Instructions both in Hindi and English for the restoration of persons suffering from electric shock shall be affixed in a conspicuous place and one pair of insulated rubber gloves of requisite dielectric strength shall be provided for use by the electricians. 68. Special regulations for touring Cinema Vehicle (1) In case of touring cinema Vans, films shall be wound upon spools in such a manner that the wound film shall not nay time reach or project beyond

Special regulations for touring Cinema Vehicle (1) In case of touring cinema Vans, films shall be wound upon spools in such a manner that the wound film shall not nay time reach or project beyond the edge of the flanges of the spool. The rewinding of films shall not be carried out in the Van in which the projector is installed while an exhibition is in progress. (2) An efficient double pole switch shall be fitted in the cinematograph lamp circuit within easy access of the operator. (3) The voltage of electric supply inside the reserved space shall not exceed 125 volts. (4) The heat of the illuminant and its position in relation to the optical system shall be such that it is impossible for the rays of the light to invite a stationery film. (5) The part light of the van shall be kept burning during the exhibition of films. (6) If a van is fitted with 16mm projector and hermetically sealed bulbs, a clear space of 1200mm shall be left around the apparatus and one person other that the cinema staff shall be allowed to be within a radius of 1200 mm of the apparatus. The frame of the projector shall be efficiently earthed. 69. Miscellaneous (1) All main switches, switch boards and like fittings which are the properties of Electric Supply Company shall e distinguished by Red Colour and every apparatus which is to be operated by authorized persons only shall be made completely inaccessible to the public. (2) Electric heaters or radiators shall not be used in any part of the building to which the public are admitted except with the consent of the licensing authority and subject to such conditions as may specified. 70. Except as otherwise specially provided in these regulation the electric installations shall be in accordance with the provisions of the Electricity Rules, 2005 as well as Indian Electricity Rules, 1956 which shall also continue to be in force till the regulation under Section 53 of the Electricity Act, 2003 are made and such other specifications as may, from time to time, be prescribed by the Lt. Governor by notification in the official Gazette. document_title:
Standing Order No. 337 : Public as "Eyes and
                        Ears" of the Police.
text: STANDING ORDER NO. Ops. - 55 (Previous Standing OrderNo. 337/2010) PUBLIC AS 'EYES AND EARS' OF THE POLICE Action against terrorists in particular and against criminals in general, is undoubtedly the first and foremost responsibility ofthe police. Allpossible steps need to be taken to ensure that such elements do not succeed in their nefarious designs. If an incident does take place, it is an equally onerous responsibility to ensure that the accused are apprehended at the earliest. Such action by itself is a major deterrent. Development ofcriminal intelligence is one of the basic tools available with the police to prevent commission of offences or to detect those which have been committed. Criminal intelligence can be collected by various means including development ofsources, eliciting information from criminals and informers, interrogation of criminals/ other accused, keeping track on jail releases, studying modus operandi, surveillance, patrolling etc. etc. These measures are being taken by the police from time to time. There is, however, one major source of criminal/terrorist related information/intelligence which is not being addressed in an institutionalized manner by the police. This includes individuals such as rehrij'patriwalaa/ vendors, chokidars /security guards, car-parking attendants, three- wheelers/TSR drivers parked in markets/colonies, porters, etc. These individuals should be briefed and their cooperation sought regarding information about movement ofcriminals/terrorists. They should be treated as the 'eyes and ears' ofthe police. Such individuals sitting on side-walks/ pavements, roads, railway platforms etc. see people moving up and down throughout the day. Over a period of time, they are able to gather a lot of information which never reaches the operational levels of the police or reaches in a limited manner. They get to hear about individuals indulging in crimes and their modus operandi. They are in a good position to see suspicious activities and movements of individuals particularly if an individual leaves behind a bag or any unidentified object in a suspicious manner. Beat Constables/Division Officers should be in contact with such individuals on a day-to-day basis. Atleast one fortnightly meeting must be organized with rehri Zpatriwalas, chokidars, security guards/ chokidars, three-whee1ers/TSR drivers, taxi stands, parking lotattendants (authorized/ unauthorized), porters etc. by the Beat Constables/Division Officers. The SHO must hold a meeting with such individuals ofeach area atleast once a month. The ACP should also hold such meetings in each area once in 2 months and the DCP should also hold such meetings at least once in three months. This aside, a detailed record should be maintained regarding each of the meetings held, number of persons from each occupation who attended etc. etc. The Beat Constable should have the names and categories of each of such individuals operating in his area clearly recorded in his beat book. If they have mobile phones, these should be available in the beat book. The Beat Constable/Division Officer must encourage such 233 elements to contact them even if the information is sketchy or not very reliable. When fortnightly meetings are held at the Beat/Division level or monthly meeting at the SHO, names

text: occupation who attended etc. etc. The Beat Constable should have the names and categories of each of such individuals operating in his area clearly recorded in his beat book. If they have mobile phones, these should be available in the beat book. The Beat Constable/Division Officer must encourage such 233 elements to contact them even if the information is sketchy or not very reliable. When fortnightly meetings are held at the Beat/Division level or monthly meeting at the SHO, names ofthose who attended and the category to which they belong should be recorded so that the meetings become meaningful. Video recordings of such meetings, at least, that taken by the SHO, should also be made for scrutiny by superior officers. Besides the above mentioned individuals, there are several other categories of citizens who can be motivated to act as "eyes and ears" ofthe police such as: 1. Residents of colonies through the residents welfare associations. 2. Traders through the market associations. 3. Nagrik Surkksha Samitis. 4. Persons working at STD/ISD booths. 5. Cyber cafes. 6. Washermen, barbers, cobblers, plumbers, key lock repairers, etc. 7. Students. 8. Petrol pump workers. 9. Doctors' clinic and even doctors in slum/small areas. 10. Domestic help providers/domestic help. 11. TV/fridge/computer mechanics. 12. Mother-dairy booth operators. 13. Security and other staff of hotels/ guest houses/eating houses particularly Dhabas. Focus should be on the dhabas at borders where normally truck drivers take rest, eat food and repair their vehicles. 14. Staff of cinema halls, places of entertainments, auditoriums. 15. Security guards deployed in vital installations, government/private office buildings. 16. Property dealers/Kabaries. 17. Bank guards. 18. Mobile phone and card dealers. 19. Bus drivers/conductors. This list is illustrative and not exhaustive and could include any other member of the community. Terrorism and crime prevention are major priority areas for us and it is imperative that all possible stake holders are associated in our attempts to keep surveillance overactivities ofa suspicious nature. Unless wemotivate various sections of the community, as above mentioned, in a positive manner, we will not be able to provide quality policing and safety/security to the citizens of the capital. A special helpline number 1090 has been started which should be conveyed to each and every stake holder above mentioned. They should be motivated to give information directly to the local police officers or to the helpline. They may be assured that details of the callers to the helpline would be kept confidential. Ifthey do not want to givetheir names, addresses, 234 etc. they would not be compelled to do so. Advertisements should also be taken out in this regard in the newspapers by the PRO. The District DCsP,ACsP/Sub Divisions and SHOmust make concerted efforts to develop the 'eyes and ears' of the Delhi Police. Their success in their assignments to a great extent will be measured by their success in implementing the scheme. Action taken should be reflected in the fortnightly law and order meeting by the Crime Branch based on statistics and information provided

document_title:
Standing Order No. 337 : Public as "Eyes and
                        Ears" of the Police.
text: be compelled to do so. Advertisements should also be taken out in this regard in the newspapers by the PRO. The District DCsP,ACsP/Sub Divisions and SHOmust make concerted efforts to develop the 'eyes and ears' of the Delhi Police. Their success in their assignments to a great extent will be measured by their success in implementing the scheme. Action taken should be reflected in the fortnightly law and order meeting by the Crime Branch based on statistics and information provided to them by the districts. DCP/PCR shall ensure that helpline 1090 is manned 24x7 and all messages recorded. Information received should be passed on by telephone to the concerned SHO/DCP. A confidential record be maintained. The caller has the option to disclose his identity or not. The helpline operator should try to make the caller feel as comfortable as possible and re-ensure him about the confidentiality of his identity. On the other hand, if the caller wants to disclose his identity contact address/telephone number then it should be recorded. The I/C Command Room and the DCP/PCR shall be responsible to ensure proper functioning of the helpline / sanction ofrewards in appropriate cases. The District/Unit DCsP should also ensure that informants are directly rewarded for any useful information provided if they have given their names/contact address/numbers and are willing to accept rewards. Much of the success Israel has experienced in thwarting terrorist bombings is being attributed to public awareness. The majority ofexplosive devices placed in public sites, such as bus stands, super markets or shopping centres have been discovered by community members who were able to alert the police before the bombs went off.We need to emulate this success. The performance of district officers, particularly of the SHOs and the police station staff, would be measured on how successful they are in mobilizing public support and creating not only awareness amongst the stake holders but also the desire to step forward and contribute. For this, the police station staff would themselves have to raise their performance bar and create confidence amongst all sections of the community. text: STANDINGORDER NO. 318/2010 Procedure for enquiry/investigation related to matters involving SC/STs etc. Thereisa need foreffectivesupervision overmatters involvingmembers of SC/ST Community. Reaching to logical conclusion in a time framed manner in every such enquiry/investigation is ofparamount importance. The Govt.has alsopaid special attention towards this aspect and had enacted special law such as Protection of CivilRights Act 1955, the SCs and STs(POA)Act, 1989and the SCs and STs(POA)Rules, 1995framed for carrying the provision ofthe SCs and STs (POA)Act, 1989. The police Headquarters, in the past had issued various instructions .videCircular No-·,35/97 and 3/2000 issued vide this Hdqrs. endorsement No. 30136-258/C&T (AC-VII)/PHQdated 22.9.1997 and 1651-700/C&T (AC·VIJ')PHQdated 20.1.2000 respectively. Out of 50% of direct recruitment quota of Sub-Inspector (Exe.)-Male, 10% of the post shall be filled by the departmental candidates amongst Constables, Head Constables and Asstt. Sub-Inspectors with minimum three years service, who shall not be more than 30 years (33 years of OBC & 35 years for SC/ST) of age. Similarly, 10% Q,f~tJ}~v.§.canciesshall be reserved for.Ex- Servicemen. Out ofthe 10%quot~~m~an<.'~foErx-Servicemen, half, i.e. 50% t~t· of such quota, will be reserved (ql\~~ng categories of Ex-Serviceman candidates:- . a) Having servedin the Special forces/NSG (Spl.Action Group) Or b) Having received a QI 'Qualified Instructors' grading in the commando course Or c) Officers from the Navy/Air Force who have worked m the specializedcommando type units. text: STANDING ORDER No. Rec. - 12 (Previous Standing Order No. 324/2009) RECRUITMENT OF·HEAD CONSTABLE[MINISTERIAL] IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY [i] This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Head Constable (Min.) in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 10 of Delhi Police(Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. Recruitment willbe carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 ofthe Delhi Police[Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. Candidates from all parts ofthe country willbe eligible to apply. Intimation regarding number ofvacancies and details ofrecruitment process shall be communicated to the Central Employment Exchange and Sub-Employment Exchanges in Delhi. In addition, the vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base of recruitment and make Delhi Police a metropolitan force. A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi Police website. Resident Commissioners of all the states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states. In the advertisements, fullparticulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfillthe eligibility requirements apply on the prescribed application form alongwith Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque of Rs. 100/-. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board of the Delhi Police located at New Police Lines, Kingsway Camp, Delhi. The candidates belonging to SC/ST category and ex-servicemen category are not required to send Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque alongwith the application form. [ii] The DCP/Establishment, Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise, i.e. Un-reserved, -SC, ST, OBe and Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi in the month of January and July each year. CP, Delhiwilltake a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies. The decision regarding recruitment willbe communicated by DCP/Establishment, Delhi to DCP/ Recruitment Cell, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitmen t. 2. MODE OF RECRUITMENT Vacancies in the rank of Head Constable (Ministerial) shall be filled through direct recruitment by holding various prescribed competitive examinations. 149 3. ESSENTIALQUALIFICATION (i) Age: 18to 25 years. The upper age limit as prescribed above will be relaxable only in the followingcases: (a) Up to a maximum of five years if a candidate belongs to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe category. (b) Up to a maximum of 3 years if a candidate belongs to an OBe category. This relaxation is admissible for those castes notified in the Central List and the List issued by the Govt. of NeT of Delhi. (c) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible up to 35 years (38 years for OBC, 40 years for SCs/STs) for widows/divorced women and women judicially separated from their husbands and who are not re-married. (d) Up to a maximum of 5 years for sportsmen/sportswomen of distinction who have represented a state at the national level and the country at the international levelin sports. The discipline of

text: STANDING ORDER NO. 260/09 PROCEDURE FOR ESTABLISHING THE IDENTITY OF A PERSON BROUGHT TO A HOSPITAL IN AN UNCONSCIOUS CONDITIONS. Establishing the identity of a person brought to a hospital in an unconscious conditioneither due to involvementin an accident or otherwise is extremely important. The process can be facilitated through proper coordination and a systematic approach by the staff of concerned Police Station, District MissingPerson Unit, MissingPersons Squad, PoliceControl Room, Police staff posted at the hospitals and the State Crime Records Bureau, Delhi. Wheneveran unidentified/unconscious person isbrought toa Hospital, the followingaction is required to be taken immediately:- ACTION BY THE DUTY CONSTABLE AT THE HOSPITAL 1. Hewillinform the concerned police station about the admission ofan .un-identified person after elicitingdetailedinformationfromthe person who brought him to the hospital or from doctor/hospital records. 2. Take possession ofthe personal search immediately fromthe hospital staff to see ifthere is any identity prooflikevisiting card or any other documents /articlesbeingcarried bythe person toestablish his identity. ) 3. Make ru:;t inventory in the presence of the hospital staff of all the recovered articles and hand -overthe same tothe inquiry Officerunder a proper receipt. 4. .MakeD.D. entry and inform the Duty OfficerofPoliceStation. WORD OF CAUTION It is also impressed that under no circumstances shall the person who . , has transported/brought the injured to the hospital be unnecessarily detainedyharassed. He should be relieved at the earliest after necessary particulars/details relating to incident/accident have been elicited from him. Giving"his identity should not be a compulsive exercise. He should onlybedetained ifthere are credible grounds forsuspecting that he caused the injuries/accident. ACTION BY THE LOCAL POLICE 1. Lodginga report in the DailyDiary at once. 2. Acopyofthe D.D.entry shall be givento the emergency officer immediately and the SHObe informed. 61 3. The 1.0.shall reach the hospital and try to ascertain the identity ofthe unconscious person from the identity card, debit/ credit card, visiting card orother documents, tailormarks, tattoo etc.to establish the identity. 4. Effortsto identifythrough mobilephone connection or IMEI(ifpossible} shall also be made, if found. 5. Obtain detailed particulars viz. age, sex, description religion, tattoo marks and clothes worn by the person. 6. Givedetailed information tothe P.C.R.forinforming the MissingPersons Squad and District Missing Persons Unit. 7. Contact the Transport authority to find out the ownership details in case the unidentified person concerned was riding a vehicle. Engine/ chasis No.should also be mentioned at the time ofquerry or "24 hours enquiry facility of Computer Section, R&D,Delhi Traffic Police, Teen. Murti Lines, NewDelhi (telephone No.23794652}". 8. ' .Make arrmangements to getthe individual photographed. Clarity and quality of the photograph should be ensured. 9. Send a detailed report with the photograph to,the DMPUand C.R.O:· for updating the ZIPNETand publication in the daily police bulletin and Gazette respectively. 10. Issue Hue and Cry notices, iffelt necessary. o 11. Cross-check with the information on ZIPNETand DailyPolice Bulletin, which gives information about persons reported missing in Delhi. 12. Issue a W.T.Message to all SPs in India. 13. Get photographs ofthe individual to broadcast on Television. 14. When an unidentified/unconscious

The Photographs and description of the Un-Identified Person found shall be uploaded on ZIPNET.The DMPUshall further.- 1. Checkthe database-ofMissing-Persons an-din case the descriptive rolltallieswithany ofthose reported missing, the concerned police station shall be informed 'at-once. 2. Photographs and details ofunidentified persons shall be shown to the public visiting the DMPUfor making enquiries about their ( ) missing relatives. 3. As and when the identity of the Un-Identified Person found is established, DMPUwillupdate the ZIPNET. b) The Missingpersons Squad(MPS)shall monitor the uploading ofdata regarding Un-Identified person found on the ZIPNETand willattempt to match the details ofUn-Identified Person found to persons reported missing. MPSshall also maintain close links with DPMUand ensure that uploading ofdata and matching ofUn-Identified Persons found/ Un-Identified DeadBodywith persons reported missing is carried out effectively. The information and photograph received from the local police in this regard shall be published in the Delhi Police Bulletin for circulation amongst the PoliceStations in Delhi. 2. Information about fixing of identity should also be published in the Delhi PoliceBulletin. ACTION BY THE P.R.O Whenever information regarding admission of an unidentified/ unconscious person in a hospital is received fromthe localpolice,the P.R.O. should ensure prompt and wide publicity through press release. Allconcerned i.e. SHOs, l/C DPMU,l/C Missing Persons Squad, l/C Control Room, SCRBand the Duty Constable at the Hospital shall ensure that the above instructions are implemented meticulously so that there is minimum delayin establishing the identity ofan unidentified Zunconscious persons. document_title: Standing Order No. 267 : Duties and responsibilities of police staff posted at various hospitals.
text: STANDINGORDER NO. 267/2009 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF POLICE STAFF POSTED AT VARIOUS HOSPITALS Introduction 1. Police personnel are posted to various hospitals in Delhi for their round the clock presence to attend to the medico legal cases (MLCs) and to maintain liaison with hospital authorities, which is required from time to time. This Standing Order contains instructions applicable to allpolicepersonnel posted at policeposts established in various hospitals. Aims and Objectives .2. The aims and objectives of establishing PPs at various hospitals and posting police personnel there are as under: '. (i) Toreceive, collateand disseminate promptly allinformation regarding accidents; un-natural injuries/deaths, such as burn .cases, deaths/ injuries due to bombexplosions, extremist action, 'crimes,i.e.murder, dacoity, robbery, rape, hurt, etc; deaths due to drowning, poisoning and natural calamities, i.e earthquakes, floods, etc. deaths/injuries due tolaw and orderproblems, death, etc. and to maintain a complete record thereof. ) (ii) To inform the concerned police stations in NCT, Delhi and the adjoining districts ofother States through PCR. (iii) Toassist the victims/relatives ofvictims for ensuring timelyhelp and providing relevant information to them. (iv). Tokeep aproper recordofMLCsjPostMortem(PM)cases and topursue -w, iththe concerned doctors for their expeditious opinion/ report. (v) Toinform the concerned police station immediately regarding receipt ofresults ofMl.Cs Zpostmortem Cases. Rotation of Duties ·3.· Thestaffshallperformduties inthree shifts and accordingtoavailability , ofstaff. Anupper subordinate l/C P.P. shall supervise the working of , ,the staff under the over all supervision of the ACP/SDPO and SHO concerned in whosejurisdiction the hospital is situated. Accommodation 4. Sufficient accommodation shall be got arranged by the Distt. DCsP for the staff, records and visitors concerned with the help ofhospital authorities. Asfar as practicable, the P.P. should be accommodated ,"Jina roomnear the EmergencyUnitofthe hospital and shall beprovided .furniture/ equipment tomake it a reasonably comfortableworkplace. 75 Communication Facilities 5. The P.P. at the hospital shall be provided with telephones from the hospital exchange and a direct telephone/extension of EPABX.In addition, hotline facilitywithPCRwould also be providedin important hospitals. Maintenance of Phones and Calls Record 6. It shall be the personal responsibility ofthe l/C PPwhowillbe either an SI or ASIto ensure that these telephones are kept in order and not misused. Proper record ofallcalls received/made indicating date, time, brief ofcalls, from whomreceived or to whom made and action taken, time etc. relating to all MLCsshall be kept by one ofthe police personnel to be called 'telephone clerk' in a register to be maintained by him as per Annexure-1.The register shall be checked daily by the I/C P.P.and it shall be his duty to ensure that the register is properly maintained. The I/C P.P. shall append his signatures with date at the close of the entries in the said register each day: SHas/ ACsP shall check this fact personally during their visits to hospital' and record their observations. Duties of the staff 7.(i) The staff deployed at the P.P. will ensure that the doctors attending the injured/casualties and preparing the MLCsare duly assisted by the policeinformingthem about the policestationin whosejurisdiction the incident has occurred and obtain other

text: register is properly maintained. The I/C P.P. shall append his signatures with date at the close of the entries in the said register each day: SHas/ ACsP shall check this fact personally during their visits to hospital' and record their observations. Duties of the staff 7.(i) The staff deployed at the P.P. will ensure that the doctors attending the injured/casualties and preparing the MLCsare duly assisted by the policeinformingthem about the policestationin whosejurisdiction the incident has occurred and obtain other such details from the victim and persons accompanying him. (ii) Information regarding the incident shall be conveyedtothe concerned police-stationin Delhi/neighbouring districts bythe quickest possible means and nearby places through PCR. (iii) The staff-on duty shall keep in their custody all articles pertaining to the victim and the case. The same shall be handed over to the 1.0. immediately under proper receipt. They shall make a record of such articles in a register as per Annexure-II. (iv] The staff shall take into custody allexhibits, duly sealed bythe doctor in heinous' offencessuch as murder, dacoity, robbery, rape etc. They shall hand overthe same to the Ia. They shall keep a record ofsuch documents/material in a register as per Annexure-II. (v) In serious cases where there is some delay in arrival of the 1.a the I/e PP on duty should talk to the victim and try to elicit as much, informationas he can about the incident. Heshould alsotake initiative in getting the dying decla.rationrecorded in the presence ofa doctor on duty, in cases, where the condition of the victim is extremely 76 precarious and chances ofhis/her survivalare bleak, beforethe arrival of local police and the Magistrate. He should have full information about the location and ward etc. where the victim is admitted. vi) On being informed by the CMOabout the discharge or death ofthe victimforwhom an MLChas been prepared, the l/C PolicePost, shall informthe policestation concerned and the nearest kin ofthe deceased by the quickest means. vii) Policepersonnel onduty must acquaint themselveswiththe topography and other relevant information relating to the hospital, and the various wards/ departments. viii) In case ofserious offenceslike riots, terrorist attacks, bomb blasts or natural calamities like earthquakes, fire and floods, etc., the police a officer(s)on duty shall keep ready record of the injured persons admitted to the hospital with their names, age, addresses, etc. ix) . The l/CP.P ..shall ensure that an upto date list oftelephone Nos. of Police Dept., hospitals and Magistrates who are required to be summoned for recording a dying declaration/inquest, etcvis maintained at the policepost. x) In case ofunconscioua/ unidentified person brought to the hospital, action willbe taken as per SO No.260 relevant to the subject. xi) Incase ofmajor incidents resulting in inflowoflargenumber ofvictims, i '. their relatives / well-wishers, etc. and WIP movements, the l/C P.P. at hospital shall request for suitable law and order and security arrangements through his district DCP.. xii) In case ofbomb blast victims arriving at hospitals, the concerned l/C .P.P. must request for a thorough anti-sabotage check to be

text: x) In case ofunconscioua/ unidentified person brought to the hospital, action willbe taken as per SO No.260 relevant to the subject. xi) Incase ofmajor incidents resulting in inflowoflargenumber ofvictims, i '. their relatives / well-wishers, etc. and WIP movements, the l/C P.P. at hospital shall request for suitable law and order and security arrangements through his district DCP.. xii) In case ofbomb blast victims arriving at hospitals, the concerned l/C .P.P. must request for a thorough anti-sabotage check to be organized to prevent secondary blasts. The hospital premises be got cleaned of allparked vehiclesexcept those identified as belongingto the Hospital staff which also should be got checked. 8. Experience has shown that a number ofD.D. entries/cases registered .in police stations do not get finalized early for want of MLCs/ postmartem reports etc. The staff posted in the hospitals do not maintain a systematic record regarding Ml.Cs/postmortem cases or do not keep track of these cases and sometimes fail to inform the concerned 10 though reports/results are ready since long. In order to cut such delays, l/C P.P.in the hospitals is required to keep proper record ofall Ml.Ca/Postmartem cases and pursue the matter with the concerned doctors togettheir opinion expeditiously. Forthat purpose, the followingsystem shall be adopted.- (i) Whenever an injured person is taken to/admitted in a hospital, the . 10 concerned would visit the hospital. In case of death the dead body would be shifted to the mortuary. 77 (ii) Each PolicePost at a hospital would have sufficient number ofpolice personnel posted in the casualty. text: STANDINGORDER NO. 269 /2016 'POLICEMITRA' 1. Introduction Policingas an institution has emerged today as averyimportant service delivery stake holder in the society. Various dimensions on day-to-day policing revolvearound critical needs ofcitizens. Citizens are veryimportant stake holder. In order to make the ground levelpolicing more effective,the assistance and cooperation ofcitizens is very necessary. 'PoliceMitra' is an initiative to involve members of civil society in prevention of crime, maintenance oflaw and order and for better communication with citizens as a whole. Section 17 ofDelhi PoliceAct, interalia, provides that.- (i) The Commissioner of Police, may, at any-time, by a written order, signed byhimselfand sealed with his own seal, appoint any able bodied male person <notless than 18years ofage, whom he considers fitto be a -Speclal.-PdliceOfficerto assist the-DelhiPoliceon .anyoccasion, when he/she has reason to apprehend the occurrence of any riot or grave disturbance of peace in any area and he is of the opinion that the ordinary policeforce is not sufficient for the protection ofpersons <residing and for the security ofproperty within such area. ) (ii) The Commissioner of Police shall publish the names of Special Police Officers appointed under this section in such manner as may be prescribed. 2. Eligibility Conditions for Police Mitra In exercise ofpowers conferred by section 8(2)ofDelhi Police Act, the Commissioner of Police has authorized all the District DCsP. Addl. DCsP and DCsr Crime, Railwaysand IGIAirportto appoint Special PoliceOfficers who will now be called 'Police Mitra' from amongst able bodied persons of the neighbourhood not below 18years ofage and having goodreputation to assist police in prevention of crime and maintaining law and order in the Capital as' per provisions contained in section 17 of Delhi Police Act read with Rule 31 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980 No. and order .l246-81/Spl.CelljPHQ dated 10.9.85. Copy enclosed at Annexure-I. 3. Procedure for appointment of Police Mitra It is emphasized upon all District DCsP that while appointing 'Police Mitra' special care should be taken to ensure that they do not have any criminal record/background and have not come to adverse notice for any anti-social or communal activity. To ensure this, all persons who offer< themselves forappointment as 'PoliceMitra' should first be asked to fillthe -......--I 91 proformaenclosed at Annexure-IIwith requisite verificationreport obtained, approvalofACPsought and the listofaspirants forthis assignment prepared. The verification shall not be got done directly from the applicant, but the same shall be got done by the persons living in/around the residence/ working address provided bythe applicant. Adiscreet enquiry shall also be got done from the Special Branch after initial verification ofthe applicant by the local police. 4. Method of appointment In continuation ofCircular Order No.6893-7100/XXIX/39 /Spl./C&T, AC-Vdated 30.01.89 and No.17283-483/C&T, AC-Idated 14.03.89, each district should make efforts to enroll "PoliceMitra" as SPOs from amongst the members ofthe public as possible. Every'PoliceMitra' so appointed shall, on appointment.- (i) Receive'a certificate ofappointment in such from as may be specified by the Administrator in this behalf. (ii) Have the same powers, privileges and immunities and perform the same duties as

Method of appointment In continuation ofCircular Order No.6893-7100/XXIX/39 /Spl./C&T, AC-Vdated 30.01.89 and No.17283-483/C&T, AC-Idated 14.03.89, each district should make efforts to enroll "PoliceMitra" as SPOs from amongst the members ofthe public as possible. Every'PoliceMitra' so appointed shall, on appointment.- (i) Receive'a certificate ofappointment in such from as may be specified by the Administrator in this behalf. (ii) Have the same powers, privileges and immunities and perform the same duties as envisaged in section 43 of Cr.P.C. (iii) Receivean identity card issued from ClMS(P&L),Delhi Police. () It should be kept in mind while considering cases of appointment of 'Police Mitra' that those persons residing in the area where such appointments are made should be givenpreference, as mentioned in section 17 ofDelhi PoliceAct, 1978. The duration of appointment of 'PoliceMitra' should be forthree years. Onethird ofthe 'PoliceMitra' should be replaced everyyear and none shall be repeated after three years. Itmay also be kept in mind whileenrolling 'PoliceMitra'that people with any vested or political interest do not get appointed. 5. Role and Functions of Police Mitra The role and functions ofeach 'PoliceMitra' willbe as per Annexure- III.Theservicesof'PoliceMitra'havebeen found veryuseful inthe prevention and detection of.crime, in juvenile aid, self defence camps for girls, night patrolling, promoting communal harmony etc. They have also made significant contributions in maintaining peace in their respective areas and building bridges between the police and the citizens. Their assistance to the police in raids and in organizing de-addiction camps is very useful in saving human lives and maintaining law and order. As such, services of 'PoliceMitra' should be welcomed in any area ofDelhi. \ 'J 92 Some ofthe 'PoliceMitra' would have a high sense ofmotivation and involvement. Such 'PoliceMitra' should be utilized to a greater degree in prevention of crime and those who perform well in a year should be adequately recognized and given awards. For this all 'PoliceMitra' should be asked to submit a monthly report to the concerned SHOs/SDPOs on the proforma. These reports should be examined after everythree months in a calendar year vizJanuary, April,July and October. Meetings with 'Police Mitra'may be held regularly and in an institutionalized manner rather than calling them only on special occasions. 6. Procedure for sorting out Objections: Any person objecting to the appointment of any person as a 'Police Mitra' may send his/her reasons for such objection to the Commissioner of Policewithin fifteendays ofsuch appointment and the Commissioner / Spl. CP-L&O/Joint CP-Range may accept such objection and cancel the appointment ofsuch officerafter giving the applicant an opportunity to be heard. 7. Asand when a heinous offenceoccurs in an area, it willbe the duty of the SHOto nominate a 'PoliceMitra' residing in the vicinityto interact with the victim or the family of the victim. It will be the duty of the 99 'PoliceMitra' to visit the victim's house as frequently as possible, after the occurrence of crime. As the victim/family of the victim are in a state ofutter shock during the first 15-20days period, the 'PoliceMitra' should be told to handle them with a great deal ofsympathy, kindness and consideration. He should not only console them but help them to the extent possible in regard to their problems and also conveyto the police any information orviewsthat they might have in respect ofthe case. The SHO and 1.0. should accompany the 'PoliceMitra' at least once in order to reassure the victims that effective police action is being taken and to also render any help that is possible. In fact, in highly sensational cases like dacoity, robbery with murder etc. even the ACPshould visit the victimsin order to reassure and console them. document_title: Standing Order No. 303 : Guidelines for police response and investigation in cases of Sexual Offences.
text: DEL H I POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. 303 OF 2019 GUIDELINES FOR POLICE RESPONSE AND INVESTIGATION IN CASES OF SEXUAL OFFENCE (I) .INTRODUCTION ' .'In the past few years, there have been various amendments in offences relating to sexual assault, including enactment of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Amendments have also "been made in the procedural law i.e. Code of Criminal Procedure and Indian Evidence Act. Moreover,the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi have also passed guidelines for the investigation of sexual assault cases. In addition to the statutes and directions of.the.Hon'ble Courts, certain other important directions have been incorporated -in this Standing Order which are to be followedwhile responding to and investigating sexual assault cases. (II) OBJECTIVES (i) To respond promptly and appropriately to 'calls' or information pertaining to sexual offences. (ii) To initiate immediate legal action on all such complaints as and when the same is received. (iii) To issue comprehensive instructions regarding investigation of rape or sexual assault cases so as to improve the quality of investigation and also to secure maximum conviction. (iv) To emphasize the criticai importance of the manner in which investigation is carried outin rape cases so that all available evidence is collected and the victim does not suffer any miscarriage ofjustice. (v) To provide immediate relief and assurance to the victim through counseling and provision of legal assistance, and investigate the case fairly in a time-bound manner so as to ensure that the guilty are promptly apprehended and subjected to trial. (vi) Toensure that the investigating officers are adequately trained and made aware of the legal perspectives, statutes and directions. They must also be closely supervised and all necessary scientific and logistical support should be made available to them. (III) RECEIPT OF INFORMATION AND RESPONSE (a) Call Received in PCR When a call or information of rape or sexual assault is received in the Central Police Control Room (CPCR),the Operator handling the call will try to record each and every relevant information being shared by the caller, including name, address, profession of the caller; name, address & age of the victim; exact place of occurrence; name, address and age of accused persons (if known) etc. The operator will immediately bring it to the notice of the ACPjCPCR, besides informing the concerned PCR Van, District Control Room etc., but he or she will not disclose the information to anyone else who is not connected with the matter. In-charge of PCR Van, unless it is operationally expedient to do so in the interest of the victim, should take care to avoid passing on the 'HaZat Report' on wireless and he may convey this through telephone to the concerned officersor CPCR. - (b) Response of Local Police SHO and other responsible staff of Delhi Police should immediately respond to a call or complaint involving offences against women or children and treat the entire city as his jurisdiction to begin with. The process of recording a complaint or

text: expedient to do so in the interest of the victim, should take care to avoid passing on the 'HaZat Report' on wireless and he may convey this through telephone to the concerned officersor CPCR. - (b) Response of Local Police SHO and other responsible staff of Delhi Police should immediately respond to a call or complaint involving offences against women or children and treat the entire city as his jurisdiction to begin with. The process of recording a complaint or statement, inspection of spot, getting medical help, identifying the accused and his apprehension (if sufficient evidence) etc. should commence immediately and jurisdiction decided later. All supervisory formations will ensure that constant briefing of police officersis ensured so that a call or complaint is responded to promptly without getting deterred byjurisdictional issue. If a complainant is not duly attended to or prompt police response is not provided on grounds of jurisdiction, strict disciplinary action should be taken. (c) Action on Receipt of Information (1) If an information or a 'call' regarding sexual assault is received through Wireless message or telephone in the police station, the same shall be recorded accurately in the Daily Diary by the Duty Officer.Asfar as possible, the name, address and telephone number of the informant or 'Caller' shall be mentioned in the Daily Diary. 2 (2) The Duty Officershall also intimate the Rape Crisis Cell (RCe) or the Rape Crisis Intervention Centre (RCIC)of the Delhi Commission for Women (DCW)on its 24-hour helpline number 23370557 and make an entry in the Daily Diary to this effect. If the victim is a foreigner, intimation should also be sent to the concerned Embassy/High Commission by the SHOof concerned Police Station at the earliest and a copy ofthe same be also forwarded to DCP/District. - (3) The Duty Officer shall invariably mark the 'call' preferably to a Woman Officer i.e. Inspector or Sub-Inspector posted or attached to the police station. The Duty Officer shall also immediately convey the information to the SHO' and Inspector (Investigation) in person or through telephone. (4) In case a Woman Inspector or SI is not available in the police station, ACP/SDPO will assign a Woman Inspector or SI from any other police station of the Sub-Division. (5) Subsequent to the filing of-the complaint/lodging of the FIR, only a woman officer of the rank of Inspector or Sub-Inspector shall be detailed as Investigating Officer (10) to conduct the spot enquiry and further investigation. (6) The Duty Officershall prepare a copy of the Daily Diary entry duly attested by him and hand it over to the Investigating Officer.The Officer, who has been assigned the DD entry; shall proceed to the spot (where the victim is reported to be present) along with sufficient staff. (7) SHO and/ or Inspector (Investigation) shall also proceed to the spot without fail once the information is prima facie confirmed. (8) In case the victim approaches the police,station herself or with her parents/ guardian, the Duty Officer will call the woman Investigating Officer to

text: by him and hand it over to the Investigating Officer.The Officer, who has been assigned the DD entry; shall proceed to the spot (where the victim is reported to be present) along with sufficient staff. (7) SHO and/ or Inspector (Investigation) shall also proceed to the spot without fail once the information is prima facie confirmed. (8) In case the victim approaches the police,station herself or with her parents/ guardian, the Duty Officer will call the woman Investigating Officer to deal with her. The Duty Officer will also inform the SHO and Inspector (Investigation) about the same. (9) The staff deployed at the Public Facilitation Desk shall handle the complainant/victim with due empathy and care so as to make her feel comfortable before she is further attended to. (10) It should be' kept in mind that incase a call or information of sexual assault is received through telephone, which is subsequently found 'switched-off, and the victim or the place of occurrence are also not traceable, the call should not be 'filed' in a routine manner unless proper verification from the caller or owner ofthe phone is done. (IV) RECORDING OF STATEMENT & REGISTRATION OF FIR Recording the statement ofthe victim of sexual assault is one of the most significant steps towards successful prosecution of the accused, since it is the basis on which the FIR is lodged and various penal sections of law are applied as per facts disclosed in the statement. The contents of the statement and the manner in which it has been recorded will be crucial. Therefore, the Investigating Officer (IO) should use her knowledge and experience to elicit each and every relevant information or details of incident from the victim in a congenial and empathetic manner. The 10 should not mechanically record the statement, but she should first assess the psychological state ofthe victim, as victim may be traumatized, particularly when the victim is a child. In view of provisions of POCSO Act, vide section 19 and 26 of the Act, while recording the statement of victim, wherever necessary, the assistance of translator or an interpreter or special educator having such qualification, experience may be taken by the 10. (1) The Investigating Officer shall record the statement of the victim promptly and accurately as narrated by the victim. (2) If the victim is a child i.e. less than 18 years of age, her parents or guardians or any other person in whom the child reposes trust and confidence shall be allowed to be present at the time of recording her statement, unless the allegations point to the involvement ofthe parents. (3) Ordinarily, the statement of the child victim shall be recorded at the residence of the victim or at any other place where the victim can make a statement freelywithout fear. (4) The Investigating Officer will ensure that at no point should the child victim come in contact with the accused. (5) Thevictim shall not be kept in the police station overnight on any pretext whatsoever

(3) Ordinarily, the statement of the child victim shall be recorded at the residence of the victim or at any other place where the victim can make a statement freelywithout fear. (4) The Investigating Officer will ensure that at no point should the child victim come in contact with the accused. (5) Thevictim shall not be kept in the police station overnight on any pretext whatsoever including medical examination, and in case the victim has no place of stay or family, she should be sent to safe places like Nan . Niketan, Short Observation Home etc. (6) The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi pronounced the following directions in Crl. Ref.No.02/16 - "Court on its own motion Vs State":- (i) A statement under the POCSO Act can be made only to a police officeror a magistrate, and; (ii) Provisions of the POCSO Act or the J.J. Act do not contemplate any report to be made by a counselor. It further makes it explicitly clear that counseling report/ notes of the counselor (as well as any person or expert recognized under the POCSO Act and Rules of 2012 and the JJ Act) are confidential in nature and the same cannot be made a part of the charge sheet or otherwise on the trial court record. As such, the IO/SHO while preparing the charge-sheet/Final Report of Rape/POCSO Act cases shall ensure that neither the Counselor is cited as PW nor the Counseling Report is included in the list of documents to be forwarded to the Court. (b) Registration of FIR (1) After the statement has been recorded, the 10 will make an endorsement and get an First Information Report (FIR)registered without any delay. (2) If there is delay in registration of FIR, due to victim reporting the matter late under certain circumstances, the same should amply be explained in the endorsement of the 10 and explained during the subsequent investigation ofthe case. (3) The FIRs relating to sexual offences shall not be uploaded on the official website of the Delhi Police as is being done in other FIRs, categorized as "Sensitive". (4) In view of the order dated 12.09.2017 of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in CWPNo. 8183/2017 titled 'Court on its Own Motion Vs. Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors.', a copy ofFIR in all cases of 'sexual violence' shall be sent to the Delhi State Legal Services Authority (DSLSA) on their dedicated e-mail sampark.dsZsa @gov.in immediately after registration of such FIR and in no case later than 24 hours of registration. (5) The 10 shall ensure that the identity of the child/victim is protected from publicity. Nodetails revealing identity ofvictim or accused (ifjuvenile) be shared by any staff, as it is also an offence ix] s 228 A of the IPCand .74ofthe JJ Act. (6) In terms of the directions of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, issued in Criminal Reference No. 2/2016 in the

(V) ACTION AT THE SCENE OF CRIME (1) Whoever first reaches the spot of sexual assault, whether it is PCR Van staff or patrolling police staff or the Investigating Officer, he or she will preserve the scene of crime till the District Crime Team or the FSL/CFSLteam visits and inspects the crime scene. (2) If the scene of crime is in the open i.e. park or jungle etc., then the entire scene of crime is to be cordoned offby using crime scene tapes. (3) The scene of crime shall be professionally photographed and video- graphed at the first instance, and only thereafter the exhibits shall be lifted and seized through Seizure Memo(s) by the 10 or the FSL/ CFSL team. All precautions shall be taken while lifting and packing the exhibits so that the same is not contaminated or putrefied. (4) Site plan of the scene of crime and route taken by the accused, if victim has been taken from one spot to another, be got prepared intelligently by the 10. Services of Draughtsman of Delhi Police may also be utilized in preparation of such site plans. (VI) MEDICAL EXAMINATION (1) After making preliminary enquiry or investigation, the 10 along with other lady police officer will escort the victim for medical examination. (2) The 10 shall ensure that the child victim is medically examined at the earliest preferably within twenty-four hours (in accordance with Section 164-A Cr.P.C.) at the nearest government hospital .or hospital recognized by the government. I (3) In case of a girl child victim, the medical examination shall be conducted preferably by a female doctor. (4) The 10 or the accompanying lady police officer shall try to make the victim comfortable so as to enable the victim to narrate the history to be recorded in the MLC performa by the doctor. All necessary efforts shall be made to ensure that the victim is medically examined ..

(4) The 10 or the accompanying lady police officer shall try to make the victim comfortable so as to enable the victim to narrate the history to be recorded in the MLC performa by the doctor. All necessary efforts shall be made to ensure that the victim is medically examined .. (5) In so far as it may be practical, the help of a Psychologist should be made available to the child victim before medical examination at the hospital itself. (6) The parents or guardian or person in whom child has trust should be allowed to be present during the medical examination. (7) In case the victim has teeth marks on the body, proper examination/ measurement be done and same be got photographed for comparison of the same with the denture of the accused (on his/their arrest) from a forensic Odontologist. (8) The medical examination report should be collected expeditiously by the 10. A copy of such Medical examination report be handed over alongwith IOs request to the magistrate who records the statement of the victim is] s 164 Cr.PC. In the event the results of examination are likely to be delayed, the same should be clearly mentioned therein. (9) Cases in which the victim is below 12 years of age, the consent of parents for medical examination or otherwise shall also be got recorded in the MLCunder their signatures or thumb impressions and the same be got countersigned and stamped by the examining expert or the Gynaecologist. In case the victim is over 12 years of age and refuses for medical examination, the same be got recorded in the MLC from the doctor and efforts shall also be made to get a signature or thumb impression of the victim as well as of the person bringing the victim to the hospital. (10) Investigating Officeras well as supervisory officers should ensure that the medical examination of the accused includes examination of any Sexually Transmitted Disease or Sexually Transmitted Infection, with which the accused might be suffering, so that the accused can be charged with appropriate sections of law and also to provide necessary treatment to the victim at the earliest, against any sexually transmitted disease or sexually infectious disease. (11) As per the recommendations of Justice Usha Mehra Committee, the Health Department of GNCTDhas set up 'ONE STOP CENTRE' as a pilot project in selected hospitals for victims of sexual abuse. The centre has the provisions of medical, legal and rehabilitative services for the victim under one roof, and the 1.0. should avail of the same wherever such a Centre is provided. Magistrate recording statement ofvictim U/ s 164 Cr.P.C. (2) In the event of the victim being admitted in the hospital, the concerned Magistrate shall be requested to record the statement of the victim in the hospital. (3) The child victim shall not be separated from his or her parents or guardian nor taken out from his or her environment on the ground of "ascertaining voluntary nature of statement" unless the parent or guardian is reported to be abusive or the Magistrate thinks it appropriate in the interest ofjustice. (4) Wherever possible, the 10 shall ensure that the statement of the victim is also video recorded as per Section 26 (4)of POCSOAct. (5) The Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP(Crl.) No. 5073/2011 titled 'State of Kamataka by Nonavinakere Police Vs. Shivnna @ Tarkari Shivanna'vide its order dated 25.4.2014 held that "...the Investigating .Officer shall not disclose the contents of the statement of the victim under section 164 Cr.P.C. until a charge sheet is filed to anybody other than those connected with the investigation of the case either in the capacity of supervisory officer orthe Prosecutor." (6) The Investigation Officer shall as far as possible take the victim to the nearest lady Metropolitan 1preferably Lady Judicial Magistrate. If there is any delay exceeding 24 hours in taking the victim to Magistrate, the Investigation Officermust record the reasons for the same in the case diary and hand over a copy ofthe same to the magistrate. (7) The section 164-ACr.P.C. imposes an obligation on the part of the 10 to get the victim of rape medically examined within 24 hours. A copy ofthe report of such medical examination should be immediately handed over to the Magistrate who recorded the statement of victim ix] s 164Cr.P.C. The check-list will also act as a guide to various steps of investigation specially required for investigation into rape cases. The check-list will also act as a guide to various steps of investigation specially required for investigation into rape cases. Since 'Death Penalty' has been provided in a rape case vide sections 376ABand 376DB of the IPC, the investigation into a rape case now assumes greater significance, and should be conducted with meticulous care and diligence. Rape cases are treated as 'Special Report Cases' in terms of SO No. 88/2010. Cases registered under POCSO Act shall also be treated as such. Initial Special Report (ISR)should be issued within 24 hours of the registration ofthe case by the ACPwithout fail and it must reach the DCP officethe same evenmg. Thereafter, Continued Special Reports (CSRs) shall be issued every Q fortnight and directions issued by the supervisory officers on ISR and CSRs must becomplied with meticulously by 10 and SHO, Following points, inter alia, should be kept in mind while investigating sexual assault cases:- (a) Collection of Evidence (1) Based upon allegations in the FIR, alleged history given in the MLC, injuries on the body of victim, if any, the medical report and version uj s 164 Cr.P.C., further investigation be carried out in a professional and scientific manner to collect evidences. (2) Each allegation be properly understood and linking evidences be brought on record. If the accused and victim are known to each other and offence is committed elsewhere, relevant mode of transport, place of stay, payments, use of phones, CDR for location, spot identification and inspection, etc. be carried out. (3) Due care be ensured while preparing various Memos (Furd) as there may be cases when the victim is minor or under trauma. Efforts be made to associate independent witnesses and videography be done of such places and articles. (4) Statements of the witnesses uj s 161 Cr.P.C. be recorded with due diligence to muster evidence in consonance with the chain of events and there should not be any contradiction. (5) In case the offence is committed in a moving vehicle, information of the vehicle be shared with adjoining districts of Delhi as well for early tracing of vehicle. Minute inspection of the vehicle by FSL team be ensured even ifthe vehicle is washed. (6) The Investigating Officer shall promptly refer for forensic examination the clothing and other articles to be examined for evidence. The Forensic Science Laboratory should also be requested to deal with such cases on priority basis and to make its report available at the earliest. Importantly, in cases where more than one accused are alleged to be involved, due care, application of mind be ensured while sending the exhibits. The queries on the FSL forms should be specific and have to be evidence-oriented so that adequate 'scientific evidence, FSL reports, DNA examination

text: and other articles to be examined for evidence. The Forensic Science Laboratory should also be requested to deal with such cases on priority basis and to make its report available at the earliest. Importantly, in cases where more than one accused are alleged to be involved, due care, application of mind be ensured while sending the exhibits. The queries on the FSL forms should be specific and have to be evidence-oriented so that adequate 'scientific evidence, FSL reports, DNA examination report etc. are brought on record for the concerned Courts to assess and reach a conclusion. (7) As per requirement, DNA fingerprinting of biological exhibits should also be got done. (8) Police records and charge-sheet must specify the continuity and sanctity of custody ofthe exhibits. (9)' . Queries in the FSL Form be drafted with due diligence so that the exhibits could be linked with the victim and the accused without any plausible doubt. (10) Due care should be exercised to ensure that the exhibits are duly preserved in cold storage to avoid putrefaction. (11) It is mandatory for police to take the bond vx] s 170(2) Cr.P.C. of the prosecutrix as wellas witnesses. (12) In case during investigation of the case, it comes to the knowledge of the 10 that the victim is a member of SC or ST, appropriate section(s) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (POA)Act, 1989 should be invoked and investigation of such cases be transferred to an officer of the rank of ACPfor further investigation. Needless to mention here that the authority issuing such certificate should be cited as PW with relevant record. (b) Preservation of MobilePhone or Other Electronic Evidences (1) In cases where phones or any other electronic device is allegedly used for taking pictures or making video etc., 10'should seize the same . with complete details of phones, hard discs, operating systems etc. as per the instructions contained in SO No.448/2017. (2) If CCTVfootage is taken on record for evidence purpose, the hard disc, its compatibility etc., should be mentioned in the Seizure Memo so that the same can be procured and played during trial. The CCTVfootage is to be procured as per the instructions contained in SO No.442/2016. (3) Ownership details of SIM connections, IMEINo., make, colour etc. of the phones being used by victim as well as accused be brought on record. (4) A letter must immediately be written to the concerned telecom service provider (TSP)for preserving the relevant CDRs in their system till conclusion of trial and for not destroying any of those without taking NOCfrom police. (5) Whenever any computer or electronic record is seized, the certificate u/ s 65-B Indian Evidence Act, 1872 should be obtained from the person under whom such system was working or from the persons authorized under the I.T. Act, 2000. (6) Special care must be taken in respect of naming the Cellular Companies as the witnesses. Each and every document provided by them i.e., Consumer Application Form (CAF), ID proof of

text: not destroying any of those without taking NOCfrom police. (5) Whenever any computer or electronic record is seized, the certificate u/ s 65-B Indian Evidence Act, 1872 should be obtained from the person under whom such system was working or from the persons authorized under the I.T. Act, 2000. (6) Special care must be taken in respect of naming the Cellular Companies as the witnesses. Each and every document provided by them i.e., Consumer Application Form (CAF), ID proof of customer, CDRs, 1() Certificate u/s 65 B Indian Evidence Act is to be proved by the Nodal Officer of the service provider and they must be mentioned in the list of witnesses. The CDRis to be collected as per the instructions contained in SO No.451/2017. (7) In order to get linking evidence from such devices, same should be forwarded to the FSL with supportive equipment, operating devices etc. for analysis under proper seal and brief summary of the case. (8) Wherever the data available in the Hard Disk, CCTV, Mobile Phones etc. is required for investigation, a mirror image of the same be got prepared under proper record. (c) Arrestand Interrogation of Accused (1) If the accused is unidentified, sincere efforts are required to be made for identification and arrest of the accused person(s). This task should not be left to the woman 10 alone and SHO should form special team(s) for identification and apprehension of the accused person(s). ACP and DCP shall monitor this at their personal level. (2) In a 'gang-rape' case, more than one team cari be formed at the Sub-Division or District level depending upon the nature and sensitivity ofthe case. -: (3) Once the accused person is apprehended, he should be examined at length to establish and connect whole sequence of events. Careful evaluation of the information gathered during interrogation is always helpful in connecting the accused with the crime he has committed. (4) The accused so arrested be immediately subjected to medical examination as per provisions ofsection 53-Aof the Cr.P.C. (d) Preserving the exhibits taken fromaccused (1) Exhibits seized or handed over by the doctors taken from the victim!accused need to be preserved and sent for examination by the FSL experts at the earliest. The 10 must use the investigative tools/kits provided in the PS for collection/preservation of evidence, and precautions should be taken to avoid putrefaction of exhibits while .sending the same to the ESL. The refrigerators provided to the. police stations for the purpose shall be used for preservation of exhibits only and not for any other purpose. (2) Investigating Officers shall deposit all the relevant exhibits/ documents for examination with the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) as early as possible, preferably within 07 days from the date of its collection. Further, in case of biological samples such as blood, semen, 11 etc. which putrefy or degenerate at a rapid rate; should be sent on the same day or the next day ofcollection. (e) Information and Attendance of Victim During Hearing of Bail and lawyers of the Delhi Commission for Women All the Investigating Officers shall inform the complainant or victim of sexual offences through any possible means of communication regarding the listing of bail application in order to facilitate them to put their version before the court, if they so desire. Each and every bail matter should be attended by the 10 and/ or Inspector (Investigation) with a detailed brief for the Court and the Public Prosecutor. Copy of bail application, replies thereto and order of the Court should be part of the Police File. The Investigating Officer should also keep in mind the mandate of Section 40 of the POCSO Act as well as Rule 4 of POCSO Rules for necessary implementation. (IX) PINK FUND When a child victim comes in contact with the Police Officer, generally he/ she may not feel comfortable as the Police Officer is not known to him/her. In order to provide a child-friendly environment as also to make the child victim feel at home, Investigating Officer may have to offer some food item or toy etc. In some instances, the clothes Zundergarment of the child victims may have to be seized for some crucial evidences, and some alternative clothes/undergarment willhave to be procured for the victim. For this purpose, a Fund will be maintained in the DCP office for disbursal to the Investigating officer through concerned ACP. The ACP concerned shall maintain a complete record of fund to be released including FIR details, amount, purpose, date of release and acknowledgement. A utilisation certificate will also be provided by 10 duly verified by SHOo 12 The Fund will be maintained/ designated as the Pink Fund and shall be recouped regularly post utilisation from the Head, 'Imprest Money', allocated to the districts. (a) Special Provisions forFiling Charge Sheet .Expeditious completion of investigation in rape and sexual offence cases is of paramount importance. Investigation in such cases shall be closely monitored by the concerned DCP. (1) The Investigation of offences under sections 376, 376A, 376AB, 376B, 376C, 376D, 376DA, 376DB or section 376E of the IPC and sexual assault cases under POCSO Act shall be completed within 60 days from the date of filing of FIR in view of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018.. (2) It should be ensured that pseudonyms are used in place of the name of the victim while recording the statement u/s 161 Cr.P.C. so as to protect the identity of the victim. This provision willbe also followedif the person alleged against is a juvenile (JCl.]. (b) DraftChargeSheet (1) In view of the above provisions, a draft charge-sheet in the sexual assault cases mentioned in para (a)(i)above be prepared within 45 days without fail. (2) Inspector (Investigation), SHO and ACP shall personally monitor such cases and ensure that the draft charge sheet is prepared and put 1':1 up to them by the 10 within the stipulated period. Needless to mention that the investigation of these cases should be supervised by the SHO/ACP right from its inception very closely and the 1.0. should be appropriately guided. (3) They shall also ensure that the 10 put up the draft charge sheet to the Public Prosecutor concerned on the next working day and 10 doesn't keep the charge sheet-with herself. Further investigation, if required, shall continue, including arrest of the co-accused, PO proceedings, deposit of exhibits, age-estimation, etc. and the same shall be mentioned in the last paragraph of Column No. 16 (Brief Facts ofthe Case) of the Final Report. (4) In cases where, despite best efforts all the points have not been covered in the main charge-sheet, the 10 should clearly specify the same and mention in the charge-sheet that further report i.e. supplementary charge-sheet(s) as per provisions of section 173(8) CLP.C. shall be filed in due course. Another Final Report in the form of a Supplementary Charge Sheet shall be filed as soon as possible after completion of investigation in all respects. Even a second or subsequent Supplementary Charge Sheet(s) can be filed in due course depending upon circumstances and requirement of the case. (5) Action required to be taken after filing main charge-sheet or Final Report like arrest of co-accused, filing of any FSL report or any other relevant document, etc. should be mentioned in the 'Follow Up Action/ Supplementary Charge Sheet Register' so that follow-up action can be ensured even if the 10 and/ or SHO is transferred lL1 subsequently. In respect of all such cases, where supplementary charge sheet is to be filed or any follow-up action is to be taken, an entry to this effect shall be made in Red-ink in the Index of the relevant FIR Book by the MHC(R), at the time of issuing Road Certificate, and shall be duly attested by SHO or Inspector (Investigation).
