text: STANDING ORDER NO. 258/2010 RECRUITMENT OF CONSTABLES [SANDMEN] MALE IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY: - [i] There are two bands in Delhi Police viz. Brass Band and Pipe Band. In addition, a number of buglers are also required for police parades and other functions at Provisioning & Logistics, New Police Line, PoliceTraining Collegeand Police Training School. This necessitates recruitment' of trained personnel periodically so that we may have required number of bandmen and buglers. Deputy Commissioner of Police, Ist Bn., DAP will be incharge of the Brass Band while Principal/PTC willbe in-charge ofthe Pipe Band. fiil This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of constables (Bandsmen) male in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 20 and 9 of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 [ii] of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. Intimation regarding number of vacancies and details of recruitment process shall be communicated to the Central Erriployment Exchange and Sub-Employment Exchanges in Delhi. In addition, the vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in the Employment.News inviting applications from all over . t:" the country in order to w1'Ei~tfthebase of recruitment and make Delhi Police a metropolitan force.'A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi Policewebsite. Resident Commissioners of all the states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states /Distt. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility requirements apply on the prescribed application form alongwith Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque of Rs. 100/-. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board ofthe Delhi Policelocated at NewPolice Lines, KingswayCamp,Delhi. The candidates belonging to SC/ST category and Ex-servicemen category are not required to send Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque alongwith the application form-. [iii] The DCP/Establishment, Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. un-reserved, SC, ST, OBC and Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi in the month of January and July each year. C.P. Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies and availability of training infrastructure. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/Establishment, Delhi to DCP/Recruitment, Delhi who will initiate the process ofrecruitment. 2. CONSTITUTION OF RECRUITMENT BOARD. A Special Commissioner or a Joint Commissioner of Police shall be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi to exercise overall supervision over the entire recruitment process. One or more Joint Commissioner or/and Joint Commissioner of Police/ Recruitment Cellmay be similarly nominated to assist him. One or more Recruitment Board shall also be nominated by the Commissioner of Police. While the constitution of the board shall be decided by the Commissioner of Police, normally the Recruitment Board shall, besides a DCP, include

text: Delhi Police Standing Order No.183/2010 Subject: - Procedure regarding lodging of reports for loss of Registration Certificate/Driving Licenses etc. I. Introduction This Standing Order aims at laying down instructions and procedure regarding reporting of loss of Registration Certificate/Driving Licenseetc. of motor vehicles to the Police to minimize inconvenience to genuine losersof suchdocuments. II. Legal Provision A. The procedure for issue of Duplicate Licenses/Badgesin view of lossetc. has been specified under the provisions of Rule-S of the Delhi Motor VehiclesRules,1993,which statesthat: - (3) If at any time a licence or a badge is lost by the holder thereof or is destroyed, the holder shall forthwith intimate the facts in writing in Form LLD in case of driving licence badge and in Form L.CON.A in case of conductor's licencebadgeasthe casemay be,to the licensingauthority. (4) Uponthe receipt of intimation as aforesaid the licensing authority shall, if he is not the authority by whom the licence was issued, apply to that authority for particulars of the licenceand of any endorsements thereon, and after making such enquiries as he thinks fit shall if he is satisfied that a duplicate may properly be issued,issuea duplicate license/badge: Provided that in case of MMV or HMV "No Challan Pending" certificate shall have to be obtained from Delhi Traffic Police before the issue of duplicate licence B. The provision for issue of Duplicate Certificate of Registration/Fitness in view of loss etc. has been specified under the provisions of Rule-32 of Delhi MotorVehiclesRules,1993,which statesthat:- (1) ForTransport Vehicle- (a) If at any time of certificate of registration/fitness of a transport vehicle is lost, destroyed or mutilated, the owner shallforthwith intimate the facts in writing to the registering authority by whom the certificate of registration was issuedor by whom the registration mark of the vehicle was assigned under sub-section (6) of Section41 of the Act and shall apply in the Form 26 to the said authority for the issue of a duplicate certificate of registration. In casecertificate of registration has been lost, a copy of the First Information Report lodged with the police shall also be furnished by the owner along with his application. (b) Upon receipt of an application in Form 26 alongwith a proof of his present residence together with a prescribed fee the registering authority may, after making such enquiries as appear necessary and obtaining a "No Challan Certificate" from the Delhi Traffic Police and the Enforcement Branch of Transport Department and obtaining particulars of the original certificate of fitness from Chief Motor Vehicle Inspector, "No due certificate" from the Recovery Branch of the Transport Department etc., issue on Form 23 a duplicate certificate of registration a certificate of fitness in Form38 clearly stamped"DUPLICATE"in red ink; III. Procedure to be followed (i) All PoliceStations shall, therefore, record without any delay, reports, as lodged by concerned persons in daily diary registers the loss of the aforesaid documents. A copy of the relevant entry of the daily diary shall be handed over to the informant, who shall be advised to submit

text: DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. 202/2019 ; GUIDELINES FOR ISSUANCE OF LICENSE FOR SALE OF POISON/ACID 1. INTRODUCTION The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India ih the matter of 'Laxmi Vs Union of India and 'Others' [2013(9) scale 291] directed on 18.07.2013 that the States/Union territories shall regulate sale of acid and other corrosive substances. The Hon'ble Lieutenant Governor of NCTof Delhi has thereafter notified the Rules, in exercise ofthe powers' conferred by Section 2. & 8 of the .Poisons Act, 1919 vide notification N.F8/Misc.j2012/HP-II/6985-;i,(;.dated '25.08:2017 which ~e called 'The Delhi Poisons Possession and Sale Rules, 2015", which shall extend to the whole ofthe Nati~iral Capital Territory of Deihi. ~~~.: . .•~}...-1)-' 2. OBJECTIVE In order to giveeffect.to the order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and the Delhi Poisons Possession and Sale Rules, 2015, this Standing Order is being issued setting out the guidelines for issuance of license fOT sale of poisons, acid and other corrosive substances in Delhi. 3. PROCEDURE FOR OBTAINING LICENSE FOR POSSESSION OR SALE OF POISONS As per Rule 2(c) of the Delhi Poisons Possession and Sale Rules- 2015, 'Licensing Authority' means the Commissioner of Police or any other officer authorized under sub-section (1) of Section 7 of the Poisons Act-1919 to grant a license. In Delhi, the Deputy Commissioner ofPolice, Licensing Branch, Delhi is authorized to grant a license.. -'"1;0. 1 No person, unless exempted under the provisions of the Act, shall sell or possess for sale any poison specified in the Schedule except under a license in 'Form-A' as per Annexure-I granted or renewed in that behalf by the Licensing Authority. Subject to provisions of Rules 8 and 9, a license granted or renewed under these Rules shall remain in force for fiveyears from the date ofissue. 4. APPLICATION FOR GRANT OR RENEWAL OF LICENSE (1) The procedure for filing application for grant/renewal of license shall be as under: (a) Every person desiring for the grant of license or renewal of a license shall make 'a written application to the licensing authority in 'Form-B' as per Annexure-II and such application shall bear a fee ofRs. 500/- (Rs. FiveHundred only) as renewal fee per year for fiveyears, which is.further subject to a decision taken in this regard by the GNCT of Delhi (provided that the application for renewal of license is made more than three months prior to the date ofexpiry oflicense). (b) As per rule 6(lO)(a),' in case the application, with accompaniments reqp.ired under' Rple(l),}s not received within .the time specified above i.e. more than three months prior to the date ofthe expiry, but is received before the expiry, license shall be renewed only on payment of a fee amounting to twice the fee ordinarily payable i.e. Rs. 1000/- (Rupees one Thousand only)(per year). (c) In case an application with accompaniments is received by the Licensing Authority after the date of expiry, but not later than 30 days from the date of expiry, the license may, without prejudice to any other action that

(c) In case an application with accompaniments is received by the Licensing Authority after the date of expiry, but not later than 30 days from the date of expiry, the license may, without prejudice to any other action that may be taken in this regard, be renewed on payment of thrice the fee ordinarily payable i.e. Rs. 1500/-(Rs. (2) Application(s) for duplicate license, when the original is lost or destroyed. shall be made in writing and shall bear a court fee stamp ofRs. FiveHundred only. (3) In the case ofany change in the place ofbusiness ofthe licensee, a fresh application for license shall be made to the licensing Branch 2 and such application shall bear a court stamp of Rs. Five Hundred. (4) The licensee shall prominently display the license in the place of business. 5. LICENSE TO WHOM GRANTED (1) The applicant/licensee shall comply with the provisions of 'The Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989'. (2) Alicense shall be granted only to a person not below the age of 21 years and not of unsound mind, and who in the opinion of the Licensing Authority is competent to conduct business in poisons. The licensing authority, besides other things, will consider:- . a) Conviction in any offence involving violence or moral turpitude .and sentenced for a term ofmore than six months at any time during a period of last fiveyears; b) Execution ofa bond under-Chapter-Vlll of the Code-of Criminal "Procedure, 1973 for keepip:~peace or for good behavior during last fiveyears; ,-~'. .,.r;'. c) Cancellation of an earlier license of the applicant, under this Act any time during last fIve'years and d) Report of local police regarding character/antecedents of the applicant. Note:- As laid vide Rule 12(1) of Delhi Poisons, Possessions and Sale rules, 2015, the licensee has to be imparted training to conduct business in poisons. As such, till receipt of further clarification from the GNCT of Delhi as to who will impart the training, the Licensing Authority, shall, while granting license, check and ascerta:in about the training skills acquired by the licensee and maintain a record thereof. (3) The license issued to a firm or company shall always be in the name of the Proprietor or Proprietors of the company or a responsible person to be nominated by such proprietor or proprietors for the purpose, or in the case of a public company, in the name ofits manager. text: DELHI POILICE STANDING ORDER NO. 208/2019 DIRECT RECRUITMENT OF CONSTABLE (DRIVER)-MAlLE IN DELHI POLICE. 1. INTRODUCTORY This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Constable (Driver)/Dispatch Rider in. Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 17A(XX)of the Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitm.ent) Rules, 1980 and amendments issued from time to time. ' " . . }~. . . 1~ :, '.~.:- -e . . IJ ~_ ••. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCPjEstablishment to DCP/Recruitment who will initiate the process of recruitment. Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. The vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base of recruitment' and make Delhi Police a Cosmopolitarr Police Force. A copy of the advertisement will also be uploaded on the Delhi Police website. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility criteria can apply onlinealorigwith a fee of Rs. 100/ -only. The recruitment will be done by the Recruitment Board of the Delhi Police. Fee is exempted for all candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Ex-Servicemen eligible for reservation after, uploading- the Caste Certificates/Discharge Book or NOC, as per existing Government orders. 1 2. The constitution of the Board(s) shall be decided by the Commissioner of Police. The Recruitment Board shall comprise of a DCP/ Addl.DCP and two officers of the rank of ACP to be nominated by the Commissioner of Police, Delhi. If necessary, a panel of DCsP/Addl. DCsP/ACsP may be nominated to work on different dates, especially during large scale recruitments. text: .~IANLJINli ORDE~ NO. 221 Subjects> Kidnapping and maiming of children for the purpose of, begging •.. I. Introductory: In the conference of IGsP held in 1965, the subject. of .kidnapping and m.aiming of· children for purposes of begging was discussed. It was suggested that: whenever .instances of begging by maimed children, come t.o: the notice of the local police, enquiries should invariably be -rnade fa find out. how such children had become maimed. The circumstances. under ::.. : which some children from orphanages were reportedly taken out on 'daily basis' for the purpose of beqqlnq- were also to be subjected to . indepth enquiries. It was decided in the conference that annual drives should be launched, simultaneously - in all the States/U'Is Wi" the ebove objectives inview. 2. Every year," one.. week is fixed for· .. the above purpose and surprise raids for rounding up begging children, followed· by . enquiries ·about the ir antecedents etc. are to be condu- cted. The : ultimate objective of such drives : is to locate the :persons/gangs behind kidnapping/ maiming of children. for begging and. .for taking drastic action against such persons/gangs.· In addition efforts should be made for the rehabi- litation of juvenile beggars with the assistance of the approprl!'lteStates/Volunt;:lry agencies. t •• • '. 3. It has been intimated. by the· CBI that despite this decision, nil results of such drives · were often beinq ."sent. Ttiis gives the impression ·that eurpr ise'<raide are not. being conducted with the seriousness they -deserve, It has, therefore, beeifdecided vide this Hdqrs.No.27329- 40/C&: T.AC.I;' dt.6.1D.88 that the Special. Staff and Vi,gihirice Cells of each. District should .be ·entrusted with the job of organising raids, with the help·.bf the. staff .of .Police. Stations . in selected areas for a period of .. one week each year and also to ensure that : · more crucial follow-up enquiries are conducted by such staffs about the persons/qanqs behind ~ such .atrocltles against the .children, so that theY·are dealt with severely. DCP/Crime & DCP/Vigilance were also requested to have si.milar drives conducted, :II. Leqal Position: 4. . Section 363CiS.) of t.he· Indian Panel Code, which came into force with effect· from . the ,15th January, 1960 reads as follows:- . J63(A)"(1) Whoever kldnaps any minor or, not being t.he.lawful .guardian, of a minor, obt.ains 'the custody .of the rnlnor in order that. such .rnlnor may be .employed -or .used for the purposes cifbegging, -shall be .pLinishable with imprisonment of either description. for a term, which may. extend to ten years and shall also be liable ·to fine •.. (2) Whoever· maims· ~ny· minor in 'arder · that such minor may be employed or used for the: purp6sesof begging shall be punishable • with imprisonment for life, and shall also be -.liable to fine. q) Where any person_, not being the lawful quardian at a miner, employs or uses sucn minor. for the purposes of begging, it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is· proved, that he kidnapped or

(4) In this Sectioru- (a) Begging means ::- (i) SoliCiting or receiving alms in a public, place whether under the pretence of sing1r:'g, dancing, fortune-telling, perfor-::' ming tricks or selling articles or other- wise. (ii) Entering any private/premises for the' purposes of soliciting or receiving alms. (Hi), Exposing or exhibiting,' with the object of obtaining or' extorting alms, any ,.; sore, '~wound, injury, deformity or disease whether on himself, or any o~ther persons or of an animal. (iv) Using a, minor as an exhibit for the purpose of soliciting or receiving alms. (b) Minor means :- (i) in t.he case of a male, a person under sixteen years of age; and , ' (ll) in the':'ca~'e' of a female,' a person under eighteen years of age. ' III. .Responsibility to of Local Police 5. In additlon the annual drives mentJoned in paras 2 ,& 3 above all 'SHOs and I/C Police Posts should, keep a look out for such cases in their respective jurisdictions. It has to be , realised t.hat. the victimized children. will seldom be able to put, up their cases or appear as complainants before the police •. It is, therefore, necessary on' the part Of the local police to secure public assistance in this ,respect 'by giving wide publicity' to the provisions of law and bringing culprits to book. 6. The Police Officers should take full advantage of the presumption in sub-section, 3 of section 363.,.A-IPC, in pursuing suspicious oases. Whenever any children, maimed or ot~er-' wise, are found begging, alqngwith the adults, vigorous enquiries should immediately be taken up by the police to, ascertain if they have been kidnapped for ,that purpose. There may. be cases' where minors, are found begging; but the persons, or persons" in whose custody, they may be staying, are not easily traceable. Suitable watch should be' maintained on such children to locate their guardians. .If persons; who run houses, where such children take shelter or food are found, they should be dealt with under this section after registration of cases. The offences described in sub-sections 1 & 2 of Sect.ion 363-A IPC are cognizable and non- bailable, IV. Centralised 7. document_title: Standing Order No. 104 : Disposal of complaints / other references.
text: STANDING ORDER No. 104 OF 2010 DISPOSAL OF COMPLAINTS/OTHER REFERENCES This Standing Order aims at providing a coordinated, effective and prompt mechanism to dealwith references/complaints. The Standing Order consists of two parts i.e. Part-I deals with the methodology in respect of important references /general references received from various offices in PHQwhereas Part-Il deals with procedure in respect of complaints - their receipts, classification, examination, disposal and compilation ofstatistics for effectiveand closer supervision. PART-I 1. Instructions have been issued time totime fromvarious Head ofOffices, regarding the imperative necessity ofeffectiveand prompt disposal of all references, particularly references received from the MHA, Lt. Governor or his Secretariat, PM's Sectt., President's Sectt., CMOffice, Hon'ble Courts, Hon'ble MPs/MLAs and other important Govt. offices including various commissions. Action, as explained in this S.O.must be taken to ensure expeditious and proper disposal ofall references. 2. Allreferences pertaining to complaints/grievances received from the office of the Hon'ble Union Home Minister, received through Joint Secretary (UT), shall be dealt with by the concerned Joint Commissioners ofPolice(Ranges)and they shall ensure that the prompt action is taken and afactual reply is sent bythem within a reasonable time. A copy of such report shall also be sent to the Vigilance Unit (PHQ)for record. 3. Sq far as the PHQ is concerned, It shall be the responsibility of the Inspector /Incharge of the Branch to see that every case including Timed, Immediate and Urgent references, is dealtwith with utmost priority. Interim replies should be sent promptly only in those cases in which final replies cannot be sent immediately and material/ information has to be collected from units /districts. Dispatch offinal reply should be ensured within the stipulated time-frame. Reasonable margin for collecting information shall be given to the districts/units as far as possible. The DCsP of districts/units shall ensure that the time limit as prescribed in the reference is meticulously followedand replies complete in all respect, are sent in the first instance itself. All districts/units DCsP must ensure that. references from offices as mentioned in para-I are attended to with utmost precaution and promptness. The software to monitor various timed-references will generate automatic reminders well before the due date. All such references willbeuploaded on day-to-day basis on the computer which will not only process the existing data to match with any similar reference but also indicate the pendency on daily basis to monitor references in an organized and systematic way. 221 4. In order to ensure expeditious disposal arid to avoid infructuous exchange ofpaper work, the followingprocedure shall be followed: a) The addressee office, initially making a reference, shall invariably specify a definite time limit within which a reply is expected from the officeaddressed, in consonance with the requirements ofthe case. If this is not possible ab initio due to any reason, it shall be done at the stage of the first reminder, which shall normally be issued after a fortnight in respect ofreferences from officesas mentioned in para-I and one month for other references from the date ofissue of initial reference. If

If the target has exceeded, the forwarding office should explain the position and indicate the further time required. b) The recipient on receipt of such reference shall examine whether he could comply with the request within the prescribed time limit or shall seek more time for the purpose. In the latter event (or on receipt of the first reminder, in all other cases) he can send interim reply explaining the expected time required for final reply. c) Aseparate register for 'TIMED and 'IMPORTANT' references should be maintained in the prescribed proforma (Annexure-I) and all possible efforts be made to send the reply within the specific time frame. d) The Diary Register maintained for the important references should be kept up-to-date and it should indicate the date of final disposal as well, as the gist ofreply. e) A daily check ofTimed/Important references should be undertaken at supervisory levelto ensure that these are promptly attended. f) Once a correspondence is treated as 'TIMED' and 'IMPORTANT', it should be dealt with utmost care and urgency as is done in case of a Parliament Question. g) The diarist should mark such references personally and deliver such references to the concerned dealing assistant without any delay after making entry in his register containing the gist ofreference. h) The senior officers concerned should be kept informed of all such references. It would be better if the references are put up to them before they are sent to the concerned branch/ dealing hand. i) The cases of such districts/units/branches, which are regular defaulters, should be brought to the notice of senior officers which shall be processed by them through personal efforts. j) Cases of exceptional delay, should be scrutinized to pin-point responsibility against the defaulter and action should be initiated in all such cases. 222 k) For a vigorous follows-up action on all proposals, references sent to the officesas mentioned in para-I, letter reminders (notexceeding two in number ofthe initial reference) shall be issued under the signatures ofAsstt. Commissioners ofPoliceconcerned. Thereafter, the case shall be brought to the notice ofDeputy Commissioner ofPoliceconcerned and the matter be taken up demi-officiallywith senior officials of the concerned offices at their level. Alist ofpending proposals with GNCT,Delhi/Government ofIndia over a quarter shall be sent to Secretary (Home),DelhiAdministration once everyquarter fordisposal. m) For expediting decisions and disposal of pending references expeditiously and in order to ensure that no reference is pending in any officeformore than aweekin any case, a WeeklyArrear Statement' shall be prepared byallbranches and sent to the ACP/DCP concerned on every; Monday. The information should be sent as given in Annexure-It .. n) All communications from Members of Parliament, Legislative Assemblies, recognized Associations and public bodies shall be acknowledged. 0) Languageused inthe replies should be courteous and as far as possible should be speaking to indicate reasons in case of rejections and the gist ofreply ofeach reference shall be recorded in relevant register. p) In case ofmissent matters, same shall be re-directed to the concerned department under intimation to the person/party concerned immediately. PART-II 5. COMPLAINTS,THEIR RECEIPT. CLASSIFICATION, DISTRIBUTION. EXAMINATION AND DISPOSAL PROCEDURE FOLLOWED BY VIGILANCE BRANCH /lPHQ. 1) CLASSIFICATION OF COMPLAINTS. (i) The Delhi Police Bhawan (Vigilance Branch) receives complaints for enquiries /verification fromvarious sources, which include complaints from individuals, PMOffice, MHA,L.G House, GNCT,NHRC, CVC, 223 PGC, CM, SC/ST Commission, NCW/DCW, Minority Commission, Hon'ble Courts, DOV, RWA and others. For convenience it may be divided in four broad categories:- (a) Complaints requiring enquiries by Vigilance Branch; (b) Complaints intended for districts/units for calling a report after enquiry by the districts/units concerned; (c) Complaints intended for district/units for necessary action and direct disposal at their end; (d) Complaints not concerning police department and intended for other agencies / department. 2) RECEIPT/CLASIFICATION AND DISPOSALS OF COMPLAINTS. (i) Allcomplaints received in Delhi Police Bhawan (Vigilance Branch) from whichever quarters they come, either by post, E-mail, fax or by hand shall be delivered in the Personal Section ofDCP/Vigilance at 1 st floor, Delhi Police Bhawan, Asaf Ali Road, Delhi. text: ;. DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO.l09 OF 2019 PROCEDURE FOR ISSUANCE OF NOTICE/ORDER BY POLICE OFFICERS U/S 41A, 91, 160 & 175 Cr.P.C. I. INTRODUCTION It has been noticed that some investigating officers do not comply with the ·legal requirements of Sections 41A, 91, 160 and 175 Cr.P.C. with regard to summoning of witnesses or· suspects iri the course of an investigation or in connection with. an inquest held ujs 174 Cr.P.C. Sections of the Criminal Procedure Code empower investigating officers to examine orally any person who is believed to be acquainted with the facts and the circumstances of the case( s). / Section 41A Cr.P.C. stipulates issuance of notice for appearance before a Police Officer in all cases where the arrest of person ·rs not required. The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in its Judgement titled Amandeep Singh Johar Vs State of NCT of Delhi dated 7th February 2018 has categorically explained about the procedure to be mandatorily followed by Police Officers as has been mentioned in Section 41A Cr.P.C. also .. A Model format for notice under section 41A Cr.P.C. and directions of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi are enumerated in this S.O. and also enclosed as Annexure ...:. A. Section 91 Cr.P.C . . stipulates issuance of summons to ·produce document or other things before a Police Officer and as per directions of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, a model format for notice under this section is enclosed as Annexure -:-B. According to Sections 160 and 175 Cr.P.C., an officer making an investigation/ enquiry shall invariably issue an order in writing to any person summoned to attend such investigation/ enquiry and shall endorse on the copy of the order retained by the person so summoned, · the date and time of his arrival and the date and time of his departure from the place where he is summoned. The Model Forms regarding the instant sections, as per the directions of Hon 'ble Delhi High Court, are also enclosed with this Standing Order at Annexure C & D respectively. 1 .;'. II. RELEVANT STATUTORY PROVISIONS . Prior to examining the Judgement in case titled Amandeep Singh Johar Vs Gout. of NCT of Delhi & Ors. passed ·by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it would be useful to set out the statutory provisions which relates to requirement of appearance before a Police Officer of any person. For ready reference, the extract of provisions of Sections 41A, 91, 160 and 175 of Cr.P.C. is reproduced as below:- "Section 41A Cr.PC". Notice of appearance before police officer; - (1 ) The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 41, issue a notice directing the person against whom a re.asonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed a cognizable offence, to appear before him or at such other place a1:; may be specified in the

text: of appearance before police officer; - (1 ) The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 41, issue a notice directing the person against whom a re.asonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed a cognizable offence, to appear before him or at such other place a1:; may be specified in the notice. (2) Where such a notice is issued to any person, it shall be the duty of that person to comply with the terms of the notice. (3) Where such person complies and continues to comply with the notice,. he shall not be arrested in respect of the offence referred to in the notice unless, for reasons to be recorded, the police officer is of the opinion that he ought to be arrested. (4) Where such person, at any time, fails· to comply with the terms of the notice or is unwilling to identify himself, the police· officer may, subject to such orders as may have been passed by a competent Court in this behalf, arrest him for the offence mentioned ·in the notice." "Section 91 Cr.PC". Summons to produce document or other thing. (1) Whenever any Court or any officer in charge of a police station considers that the production of any document or other thing is necessary or desirable for the purposes of any investigation, inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Code by or before such Court or officer, such Court may issue a summon, or such officer a written order, to the person in whose possession or power such document or thing is believed to be, requiring him to attend and produce it, or to produce it, at the time and place stated in the summons or order. (2) . Any person required under this section merely to produce a . document or other thing shall be deemed. to have complied with the 2 requisition if he causes such document or thing to be produced instead of attending personally to produce the same. (3) Nothing in this section shall be deemed- (a) to affect sections 123 and 124 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (1 of 1872 ), or the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 (13 of 1891)or (b) to apply to a letter, postcard, telegram or other document or any parcel or thing in the custody of the postal or telegraph authority. "Section 160 Cr.PC". Police officer's power to require attendance of witnesses. (1) Any police officer, makihg an investigation under this Chapter may, by order in writing, require the attendance before himself of any · person being within the limits of his own or any adjoining station who, from the· information given or otherWise, appears to be . acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case; and such person. shall attend as so required: Provided that no male person under the age of

text: Police officer's power to require attendance of witnesses. (1) Any police officer, makihg an investigation under this Chapter may, by order in writing, require the attendance before himself of any · person being within the limits of his own or any adjoining station who, from the· information given or otherWise, appears to be . acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case; and such person. shall attend as so required: Provided that no male person under the age of fifteen years or woman shall be required to attend at any place other than the place in which such male person or woman resides. · (2) The State Government may, by rules made in this behalf, provide for the payment by the police officer of the reasonable expenses of every person, attending under sub- section (1 ) at any place other than his residence. "Section 175 Cr .PC". Power to summon persons. (1) A police officer. proceeding under section 174, may, by order in writing, summon two or more persons as aforesaid for the purpose of the said investigation, and any other person who appears to be acquainted with the facts of the case and every person so summoned shall be bound to attend and to answer truly all questions other than questions the answers to which would have a tendency to expose him to a criminal charge or to a penalty or forfeiture. (2) If the facts do not disclose a cognizable offence to which section 170 applies, such persons shall not be required by the police officer to attend a Magistrate's Court." 3 ··~ l III. PROCEDURE FOR ISSUANCE OF NOTICES/ORDERS Upon consideration of the Judgement in case titled Amandeep Singh Johar Vs Govt. of NCT of Delhi passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, it is directed that as far ·as working of Section 41A is concerned, the following procedure shall be strictly followed by the police in Delhi: - Procedure for issuance of notices/order by police officers ujs 41A. (i) Police officers should be mandatorily required to issue notices under Section 41A Cr.PC (in the prescribed format) formally to be served in the manner and in accordance with the terms of the provisions contained iri Chapter VI of the Code. Model form of notice under Section 41A Cr.PC & its acknowledgement is enclosed herewith as Annexure-A. {ii) The concerned suspect/ accused person will necessarily need to comply with the terms of the notice under section 41 A and make himself available at the requisite time and place. (iii) Should the accused be unable to present himself at the given time for any valid and justifiable reason,. the accused should in writing immedi.ately, intimate the investigating officer arid seek an alternative time within a reasonable period, which should ideally not exceed a period of four working days, from the d'ate on which he were required to attend, unless he is unable to show justifiable cause for such non-attendance. · · (iv) Unless it is detrimental to the

Should the investigating officer believe that .. such extension is being sought to cause delay to the investigation or the suspect/accused person ·is being evasive by seeking time, (subject to intimation to the SHO/SP of the concerned Police Station), deny such request and mandatorily require the said person to attend. {v) A · suspect/ accused on formally receiving a notice under section 41A Cr.PC and appearing before the concerned officer for investigation/interrogation at the police station, may request the concerned 10 for an acknowledgement. (vi) In the event the suspect/ accused is directed to appear at a place other than the police station {as envisaged under Section 41A(l) Cr.PC, the suspect will be at liberty to get the acknowledgement receipt attested by an independent witness if available at the spot in addition to getting the same attested by the concerm!d investigating officer himself. 4 ~ ' . {vii) A duly indexed booklet containing serially numbered notices in triplicate carbon copy format should be issued by the SHO of the Police Station to the Investigating Officer. The Notice should necessarily contain the following details: {a) Serial Number (b) Case Number (c) Date and time of appearance {d) Consequences in the event of failure to comply (e) Acknowledgment slip (viii) The Investigating Officer shall follow the following procedure: {a) The original is served on the Accused/Suspect; {b) A carbon copy (on white paper) is retained by the IO in hisjher . case diary, which can be shown to the concerned Magistrate as · and when required; (c) Used booklets are to be deposited by the IO with the SHO of the Police Station who shall retain the same till the completion of the ·investigation and submission· of the final report under section 173 (2) of the Cr.P.C. (d) The Police department shall frame apprppriate rules for the preservation and destruction of such booklets. IV. DIRECTIONS OF THE HON'BLE HIGH COURT OF DELHI (a) The ·. Hon'ble Delhi High Court further directed that the above procedure ·shall apply also to the working of Sections 91, 160 and 175 of the Cr.PC as well. AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY (i) While issuing such notices, the concerned Investigating Officer must ensure his/her presence on the given date and time and if due to any unforeseen circumstances/ officiai exigencies, the Investigating Officer is required to be away, the Inspector 5 (Investigation) or SHO will take the needful action in respect of the noticee. However, in a rare situation of serious exigency of an operational nature where none of the above officers is present, while recording the presence of the noticee, the Duty Officer will issue the necessary acknowledgement and also record a DD entry to this effect. The. Duty Officer will also collect a copy of self-attested ID proof from the noticee and inform the SHO accordingly. A copy of DD entry and ID proof shall be handed over to the Investigating Officer upon hisjher arrival. (ii) Procedure booklets (containing serially numbered notices in triplicate) in format identical to the above prescription in guideline (vii) & (viii) with modifications having regard to the statutory provisions in the forms for notices and acknowledgment shall be maintained. (DCP/IT Centre, Hindi Section/PHQ). text: D E L H I :p 0 L I C E STANDING ORDER N0.109 OF 2020 PROCEDURE FOR ISSUANCE OF NOTICES OR ORDERS BY POLICE OFFICERS I. INTRODUCTION It has been noticed that some investigating officers do not comply·with the legal requirements of Sections 41A, 91, 160 and 175 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) with regard to summoning of witnesses or suspects in the course of an investigation or in connection with an inquest held u/s 174 Cr.P.C. These sections of the Criminal Procedure Code empower investigating officers to examine orally any person who is believed to be acquainted with the facts and the circumstances of the case(s). Section 41A Cr.P.C. stipulates issuance of notice for appearance before a Police Officer in all cases where the arrest of person is not required. The Hon 'ble High Court of Delhi in its judgement titled 'Amandeep Singh Johar Vs. State of NCT of Delhi' dated 07.02.2018, has categorically explained about the procedure to be mandatorily followed by Police Officers as has been mentioned in Section 41A Cr.P.C. also. A Model format for notice under section 41A Cr.P.C. and directions of Hon'ble High Court of. Delhi are enumerated in this S.O. and also enclosed as Annexure - A. Section 91 Cr.P.C. stipulates issuance of summons to produce document or other things before a Police Officer and as per directions of Hon 'ble High Court of Delhi, a model format for notice under this section is enclosed as Annexure - B. According to Sections 160 and 175 Cr.P.C., an officer making an ·, . . . , . ~ ' investigation or enquiry shall invariably issue an order in writing to any person ~ •. .... ;..i • ' !. summoned to attend such investigation or enquiry and shall endorse on the .copy of the order retained by the person so summoned, the date and time of his !illcl . arrival and the elate time of. his depar~~e from the place where he is summoned. The Model Forms regardirig . the instant sections, as per the 1 directions of Hon 'ble Delhi High Court, are also enclosed with this Standing Order at Annexure C & D respectively. II. RELEVANT STATUTORY PROVISIONS Prior to examining the judgement in case titled 'Amandeep Singh Johar Vs Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors.' passed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it would be useful to set out the statutory provisions which relates to requirement of appearance before a Police Officer of any person. For ready reference, the extracts of provisions of Sections 41A, 91, 160 and 175 of CrPC are reproduced as below:- Section 41A Cr.P.C. (Notice of appearance before police officer) (1) The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under the provisions of sub-section ( 1) of section 41, issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a reasonable suspicion exists that

(Notice of appearance before police officer) (1) The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under the provisions of sub-section ( 1) of section 41, issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed a cognizable offence, to appear before him or at such other place as may be. specified in the notice. (2) Where such a notice is issued to any person, it shall be the duty of that person to comply with the terms of the notice. (3) Where such person complies and continue_s to comply with the notice, he shall not be arrested in respect of the offence refe rred to in the notice unless, for reasons to be recorded, the police officer is of the opinion that . he ought to be arrested . . I I I (4) Where such person, at any time, fails to comply with the terms of the notice or is unwilling to identify himself, the police officer may, subject to such orders as may· have been passed by a competent Court in this behalf, arrest him for the offence mentioned .in the notice." Section 91 Cr.P.C._( Summons to produce document or other thing) (1) Whenever any Court o.r any officer in charge of a police station considers that· the production of any document or other thing is necessary or desirable for the purposes of arty investigation, inquiry, trial or other proceetling under tliis Code by or before. suc~h Court or officer,. such Court may _issue a summon, or such officer a written order, fo the person in whose possession or power such document or thing is believed to be, requiring him to attend and produce it, or to produce it, at the time and place stated in the summons or_o rder. (2) Any person required under this section merely to produce a document or other thing shall be deemed to have complied with the requisition if he 2 causes such document or thing to be produced instead of attending personally to produce the same. (3) Nothing in this section shall be deemed- (a) to affect sections 123 and 124 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (1 of 1872 ), or the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 (13 of 1891) or (b) to apply to a letter, postcard, telegram or other document or any parcel or thing in the custody of the postal or telegraph authority. to Section 160 CrPC (Police officer's power require attendance of Witnesses) (1) Any police officer, making an investigation under this Chapter may, by order in writing, require the attendance before himself of any person being within the limits. of his own or any adjoining station who, from the information given or otherwise, appears to be acquainted

(2) The State Government may, by rules made in this behalf, provide for the payment by the police officer of the reasonable expenses of every person, attending under sub- section (1) at any place other than his residence. Section 175 Cr.P.C. (Power to summon persons) (1) A police officer proceeding under section 174, may, by order in writing, summon two or more persons as aforesaid ·for the purpose of the said investigation, and any other person who appears to be acquainted with the . facts of the case and every person so summoned shall be bound to attend and to answer truly all questions other than questions the answers to which would have a tendency to expose him to a criminal charge or to a penalty or forfeiture. (2) If the facts do not disclose a cognizable offence to which section 170 Cr.P.C. applies, such persons shall not be required by the police officer to attend a Magistrate's Court." -~ III. PROCEDURE FOR ISSUANCE OF NOTICES/ORDERS Upon consideration of the Judgement in case titled 'Amandeep Singh Johar Vs Govt. of NCT of Delhi' passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, it is directed 3 that as far as working of Section 4 lA is concerned, the following procedure shall be strictly followed by the police in Delhi: - (i) Police officers should be mandatorily required to issue notices under Section 4 lA Cr.P.C. (in the prescribed format) formally to be served in the manner and in accordance with the terms of the provisions contained in Chapter-VI of the Criminal Procedure Code. Model form of notice under Section 41A Cr.P.C. and its acknowledgement is enclosed herewith as Annexure-A. (ii) The concerned suspect or accused person will necessarily need to comply with the terms of the notice under section 41A Cr.P.C. and make himself available at the requisite time and place. (iii) Should the accused be unable to present himself at the given time for any valid and justifiable reason, the accused should in writing immediately, intimate the investigating officer and seek an alternative time within a reasonable period, which should ideally not exceed a period of fol,lr working

(iii) Should the accused be unable to present himself at the given time for any valid and justifiable reason, the accused should in writing immediately, intimate the investigating officer and seek an alternative time within a reasonable period, which should ideally not exceed a period of fol,lr working days, from the date on which he were required to attend, unless ·, ·-··. . · he is unable to show justifiable cause for such'h'bri-attendartce. (iv) Unless it is detrimental to the investigation, the police officer may permit such rescheduling, however only for justifiable causes to be recorded in the Case Diary. Should the IO believe that such extension is being sought to cause ·delay to the inv~stigation or the suspect or accused person is being evasive by seeking time, (subject to intimation to the SHO /DCP of the concerned Police Station), deny such request and mandatorily require the said person to attend. (v) A suspect or accused on formally rece1vmg a notice under section 4 lA Cr.P.C. and appearing before the concerned officer for investigation or interrogation at the police station, may request the concerned IO for an acknowledgement. (vi) In the event the suspect or accused is. directed to appear at a place· other than the police station (as envisaged under Section 41A(l) Cr.P.C.), the suspect will be at liberty to get the acknowledgement receipt attested by an independent witness if available at the spot in add_ition to getting the same attested by the concerned investigating officer himself. (vii) A duly indexed booklet containing serially numbered notices in triplicate carbon copy format should be issued by the SHO of the Police Station to the Investigating Officer. The Notice should necessarily contain the following details: (a) Serial Number (b) Case Number (c) Date and time of appearance 4 (d) Consequences in the event of failure to comply (e) Acknowledgment slip (viii) The Investigating Officer shall follow the following procedure:- · (a) The original is served on the accused or suspect; (b) A carbon copy (on. white paper) is retained by the IO in his or her case diary, which can be showri to the concerned Magistrate as and when required; (c) Used booklets are to be deposited by the IO with the SHO of the Police Station who shall retain the same till the completion of the investigation and submission of the final report under section 173 (2) of the Cr.P.C. (d) The Police department shall frame appropriate rules for the p:r;-eservation and destruction of such booklets. IV. DIRECTIONS OF THE HON'BLE HIGH COURT OF DELHI (a) The Hon'ble Delhi. AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY 1. While issuing such notices, the concerned Investigating Officer must ensure his ·or her presence on the given date and time and if due to any unforeseen circumstances or official exigencies,. the he is required to be away, Inspector (Investigation) or SHO will take the needful action in respect of the noticee. However, in a rare situation of serious exigency of an operational nature, where none of the above officers is present, while recording the presence of the noticee, the Duty Officer will issue the necessary acknowledgement and also record a DD entry to this effect. The Duty Officer will also collect a copy of self-attested ID proof from the noticee· and inform the IO or SHO accordingly. At:copy of DD entry and Ib proof shall be handed over to the Investigating Officer upon his or her arrival. 5 2. The Investigating Officers are responsible for exerc1smg full care and precautions with regard to the personal safety of·p ersons summoned by them. They should guard against the possibility of such witness or suspect attempting to commit suicide or causing any bodily harm to himself. The task of IO should as far as possible be carried out in Sankraman Kaksha or ori the ground floor of the Police Stations. 3. · When a woman has to be questioned or interrogated and a notice under section 160 .of Cr.P.C. needs to be served, the IO must keep in mind that a woman cannot ·be summoned to the police station. However, the notice can mention the details and time where the women will be questioned, which should ordinary be where the women resides, preferably in the presence of other family .mem,bers or women police personnel. · 4. As per section 160 Cr.P.C., no male person under the age of fifteen years or above the age of sixty-five years or woman or a mentally or physically disabled person, is required to attend at any place other than the place in which such male person resides. Procedure booklets (contai.ning serially numbered notices in triplicate) in format identical to the above prescription in guidelines (vii) & (viii) with modifications having regard to the statutory provisions in the forms for notic:es and acknowledgment shall be maintained. 6. Wide. publicity should ·be given for educating the public at large through various modes of Public Advocacy. 8. INTRODUCTORY [i] This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Head Constable (Store Clerk)in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 17-B(XVIII) of Delhi Police(Appointment & RecruitmentHAmendment) Rules, 2010. Acopy of the advertisement willalso be put on the Delhi Police website. Resident Commissioners of all the states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states. In the advertisements, full particulars of the essential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility requirements apply on the prescribed application form alongwith Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque of Rs. 100/-. Out of the 10 marks for the formatting features, a candidate should secure at least 6 marks to qualify. There is no bar to candidates correcting the mistakes by use of editing tools while typing the passage. v) PRACTICAL TEST Successful candidates (depending upon the number of vacancies) shall also be called to appear before the Selection Board for a practical test( in accounting and indenting Radio Spare parts) on a date fixed by the Chairman of the Board. The practical test will be of 10 marks and will also be of a qualificatory nature. Candidates who secure 35% marks in practical test will be declared qualified. 15. The final result will be prepared on the basis of marks obtained in the written test (100 marks), typing test on computer '(20 marks) and Practical Test (10 marks) . . In large. recruitments, whenever felt desirable and necessary, at the end of the .recruitment process, a list of candidates will be announced which will- be .strictly 'according to merit and will include names of candidates upto 10% of the vacancies advertised. They will be put through medical examination and police verification. This will be done so' that if some candidates higher up in the merit list (category-wise) do not make it through the medical examination or police verification, or are unable to join the training due to personal reasons, or other exigencies, candidates lower in the merit list as announced above can be appointed strictly based on merit. This exercise will be undertaken so that vacancies do not go unfilled and would be relevant for that recruitment only. It is reiterated that number of selected candidates shall not exceed the number of vacancies advertised. Being called for medical examination or being subjected to police verification will

police verification, or are unable to join the training due to personal reasons, or other exigencies, candidates lower in the merit list as announced above can be appointed strictly based on merit. This exercise will be undertaken so that vacancies do not go unfilled and would be relevant for that recruitment only. It is reiterated that number of selected candidates shall not exceed the number of vacancies advertised. Being called for medical examination or being subjected to police verification will in no way give any legal claim or right to any candidate being finally appointed. Such candidates shall not be considered against any future /other vacancies. 16. MEDICAL EXAMINATION The candidates so selected shall be medically examined by doctors in selected government hospitals in Delhi as per the prescribed standards. 17. VERIFICATION OF CHARACTER & ANTECEDENTS The verification of character & antecedents of the candidates as above willbe done through concerned authorities expeditiously. Ifneed be, special teams shall be sent to liaise with district authorities to expedite the police verification. 18. FINAL LIST OF SUCCESSSFUL CANDIDATES The final list of successful candidates [as per the number of vacancies advertised (category-wise)] strictly as per merit shall be declared after completion of police verification and medical examination. Where equal marks have been obtained by candidates their merit will be fixedas per date of birth. The older candidate willbe given preference and in case the date of birth is also the same, marks in the written test would decide the merit. Cases of selected candidates against whom any criminal case is registered/ pending investigation/ pending trial in the court, will be kept pending till the finalization of the same and' their cases will be decided on merit after finalization of cases. As regards the cases of departmental selected candidates against whom any DE/PE/Crl.Case/Vigilance Enquiry etc. is pending will also be kept pending till the finalization ofthe same and their cases willbe decided on merits after finalization ofcases. 19. DISPLAY OF F-I-N-A-_L .. R _._. .E-S-U-L-T The declaration or the result will be by displaying the lists of successful candidates for a week in the various Distt./Unit Hdqrs. on 4/5 notice boards, according to roll numbers, to avoidrush at the notice board. The list shall also be put on Internet/Delhi Police website and Intra DP. date etc. fixedfor the purpose shall also be indicated on the result sheet itself and website. Acopy ofthe result sheet willbe sent to PHQon the date the result is declared. (iv) Ordinarily, the services of those recruit Head Constable (Store Clerk) who fail to qualify in the final examination will be terminated under Rule 5 of Central CivilServices Temporary Services Rules, 1965 by the Principal/PTC. However, a maximum of one additional chance will be given to the failed trainees and if heIshe does not pass in all the papers even after availing the additional chance, his/her services will be terminated by the Principal/PTC. (e) If any information submitted by the trainee in his/her job application is found to be false, fabricated or manipulated to gain employment. (f) Any other ground which adversely reflects his/her behavior and the officeris otherwise found unsuitable forPoliceservices. (vi) A trainee shall not be allowed to take final examination, until he/ she has successfully undergone a stipulated period of training at Police Training School/ College. 90% attendance in indoor/outdoor periods is compulsory, relaxable by 5% in exceptional circumstances 60 by Principal/DCP in-charge Training, failing which he/ she will be debarred from appearing for the final examination. STANDING ORDER NO. 156/2013 RECRUITMENT OF WORKSHOP HAND (CONSTABLE) IN DELHI POLICE 1. INTRODUCTORY [i] This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Workshop Hand (Constable)in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 17-B (XV)of Delhi Police (Appointment & Recruitment) (Amendment) Rules, 2013. [ii] Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. Candidates from all parts of the country willbe eligibleto apply. Intimation regarding number ofvacancies and details of recruitment process shall be communicated to the Central Employment Exchange and Sub-Employment Exchanges in Delhi. The vacancies shall be advertised in Employment News and leading newspapers (inEnglish & Hindi) ofDelhi and their editions in all other States. A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi Police website. Resident Commissioners of all the states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states. In the e-, advertisements, full particulars of~the''''tssential requirements will be given so that only those candidates who fulfill the eligibility requirements apply on the prescribed application form alongwith Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque of Rs. 100/-. The recruitment willbe done by the Recruitment Cellofthe Delhi Police located at New Police Lines, Kingsway Camp, Delhi. The candidates belonging to SC/ STcategory and Ex-servicemen category are not required to send Demand/Bank Draft/Bankers Cheque alongwith the application form. [iii] The DCP/Establishment, Delhi will put up the vacancy position category-wise i.e. Un-reserved, SC, ST, OBC and Ex-servicemen candidates to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi in the month of January and July each year. C.P. Delhi will take a decision regarding recruitment depending on the number of vacancies. The decision regarding recruitment will be communicated by DCP/Establishment, Delhi to DCP/Recruitment Cell, Delhi who will initiate the process of recruitment. 2. MODE OF RECRUITMENT Allvacancies ofWorkshop Hand (Constable) in Delhi Police shall be filled 100% by direct recruitment viz. (i)90% vacancies shall be filled from the open competition and (ii) 10% vacancies shall be filled from the Delhi PoliceConstables by giving them age relaxation as per GOI's instructions. Entrance Test for outside candidates and departmental candidates shall be same. 63 3. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATION AND OTHER STANDARDS (i) Age: 18 to 27 years. The upper age limit as prescribed above will be re1axableonly in the followingcases:- (a) Upto a maximum of fiveyears if a candidate belongs to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe category (b) Upto a maximum of 3 years if a candidate belongs to an OBC category. This relaxation is admissible for those castes notified in the Central List and the Listissued by the Govt. ofNCTofDelhi. (c) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible upto 35 years (38 years for OBC, 40 years for SCs/STs) for widows/divorced women and womenjudicially separated from their husbands and who are not re-married. (d) Upto a maximum of 5 years for sportsmen/ sportswomen of distinction who have represented a state at the national leveland the country at the international level in sports. castes notified in the Central List and the Listissued by the Govt. ofNCTofDelhi. (c) Relaxation in the upper age limit is admissible upto 35 years (38 years for OBC, 40 years for SCs/STs) for widows/divorced women and womenjudicially separated from their husbands and who are not re-married. (d) Upto a maximum of 5 years for sportsmen/ sportswomen of distinction who have represented a state at the national leveland the country at the international level in sports. The discipline of sports for which relaxation is available is mentioned in the Annexure - 'A'. If a candidate belongs 'to SC/ST category a.nd fulfills the above criteria, he/ she is eligible for 5 years relaxation in upper age limit over and above the relaxation prescribed at Clause 3 (i)(a). In effect, he/ she qualifies for relaxation in the upper age limit to a maximum of 10 years. This concession will be available only to those sportspersons who satisfy all other eligibility conditions relating to educational qualifications, etc., and furnish a certificate issued by the followingauthorities.- (i) Secretary of the National Federation of the sport concerned in cases ofInternational Competition. (ii)SecretaryoftheNationalFederationor Secretaryofthe StateAssociation ofthe sportconcernedin cases ofNationalCompetition. (e) Ageconcession to Ex-Servicemen will be allowed in accordance with the orders issued by the Government of India from time to time. They will be permitted to deduct the period served in the armed forces from their actual age and the resultant age, so derived, should not exceed the prescribed age limit by more than three years. It is further clarified that an "Ex-Serviceman" means a person, who has served in any rank, whether as a combatant or non-combatant in the Army, the Navy or the Air Force of the Indian Union and who retired from such service after earning his pension. 64 (f) Relaxation In the upper age limit is admissible to those serving Constables enlisted in Delhi Police with a minimum of 3 years continuous service who shall not be more than 30 years ( 33 years for OBe and 35 years for SC/ST 'candidates) of age on the first day ofJanuary of the year, if the examination is held in the first half of the year and on the firstday of August ofthat year, if the examination is held in the later half of the year. Introduction ,A case has come to notice in which a Member of Parliament was formally arrest.ed and 'released on bail on 9.2.88 but intimation regarding the arrest./release of the Hon'ble M.P. was sent to Speaker, Lok Sabha on 14.9.88, i,e, after a lapse of over seven months. The Govt.. of India' have taken a' serious view of this lapse on' the part of the police officer concerned. II. Intimation 2. Such intimations if sent by Police to the Speaker of Lok Sabha/ Chairman. of Rajya Sabha/Speaker of State Legislative' Assembly/Council .should be sent .by a Police Officer not below the rank of Dy. INTRODUCTORY [i] This Standing Order deals with the direct recruitment of Assistant Sub-Inspector(Radio Technician) in Delhi Police in accordance with Rule 17-B(vii)ofDelhiPolice (Appointment & Recruitment) Rules, 1980. Recruitment will be carried out by a Recruitment Board, as prescribed in Rule 8 of the Delhi Police [Appointment and Recruitment] Rules, 1980. Candidates from all parts of the country will be eligible to apply. Intimation regarding number of vacancies and details of recruitment process shall be communicated to the Central Employment Exchange and Sub-Employment Exchanges in Delhi. In addition, the vacancies shall be advertised in leading newspapers (in English & Hindi) of Delhi and their editions in all other States. Vacancies shall also be published in Employment News inviting applications from all over the country in order to widen the base ofrecruitment and make Delhi Police a metropolitan force.A copy of the advertisement will also be put on the Delhi Police website. Resident Commissioners of all the states will also be requested to publicise the recruitment in their respective states. text: Standing Order No. Issue Date Issued By Issuing Unit Issuing Branch 99/94 29/11/1994 DCP/HQ(II) Police Head Quarters C&T Subject: FUNCTIONING OF DISTRICT WOMEN CELLS Contents STANDINGORDERNO. 99 FUNCTIONINGOF DISTRICT WOMENCELLS There will be nine District women cells (DWC)functioning in the nine police districts of Delhi. Each cell will be headed by an ACP. The cells will be under the control of DCP/Districts. DCP/CAWCwill coordinate the working of the cells and provide general guidelines on professional matters but the day-to-day functioning of the cell will be looked after by the District DCsP. Duties: (a) The DWCwill investigate all cases of murder for dowry and death of women where dowry is the motive behind the crime. This would include offences u/s 304B and 306 IPC. (b) The DWCwill investigate the cases of rape of women. (c) The DWCmay investigate other cases of crimes against women and when they are marked to them by DCP/Districts or DCP/CAWCor Addl.CP Ranges or Add1.CP/Crime. (d) The OWCwill enquire into complaints received by it and submit it to the DCP of the concerned Distt. for registration and investigation of cases which may arise out of such enquiries. However, the OWCshall not enquire into complaints which have already been dealt with by CAWCell of the Crime Branch or any of the other OWCunless specifically directed to do so. This is necessary to stop the practice of complainants going from cell to cell when the enquiry in a particular cell does not favour them. (e) The DWCwill look into every case of unnatural deaths of married women in their districts and submit a report on the prescribed proforma (Annexure A) to Distt. DCPwith a copy to DCP/CAWCwithin 48 hours. (f) OWCs will conduct anti-eve-teasing drives in their 'respective districts. (g) OWCwill also organize training in un-armed combat for school/college girls. Procedure for transfer of cases All cases of dowry deaths and rape will automatically be transferred to the DWCas soon as a case falling in the above categories is reported in any Police Station. The Duty officer of the P.S. shall immediately inform the ACP/OWCon telephone and wireless and record a DO entry to that effect. The ACP/OWC will immediately assign the case/s to an 1.0 . who shall visit the police station, discuss the cases with SHO/I.O. of the police station who had done the initial enquiry and take up the case immediately. In case there is some delay due to unavoidable reason the case shall be transferred to the DWC's after the first case diary. Records to be maintained by District CAWCs (a) Crime Register Each 1.0. will maintain a Crime Register on the prescribed proforma as is being done by the SHOs of Police Station. ACP/District Women Cell will maintain a separate Crime Register. (b) Special Report Files: All files investigated by District Women Cell would be treated as Special Report Cases. A special report file will be maintained in respect of every case. Special Reports will be sent by ACP in the same manner as

text: be maintained by District CAWCs (a) Crime Register Each 1.0. will maintain a Crime Register on the prescribed proforma as is being done by the SHOs of Police Station. ACP/District Women Cell will maintain a separate Crime Register. (b) Special Report Files: All files investigated by District Women Cell would be treated as Special Report Cases. A special report file will be maintained in respect of every case. Special Reports will be sent by ACP in the same manner as is being done in S.R. Cases by ACP I/C/ Sub. Division. Copies of the ISRs and CSRs shall be sent to DCP/CAWC as well as District DCsP by the ACP/DWCs. The ISRs and CSRs will incorporate the information as per proforma at Annexure '8'. (c) Diary Despatch Register: As per Rules. (a) Pairvi Register: A separate register for monitoring the 'Pairvi' of cases under trial would be maintained. The District Women Cells will maintain the record and conduct \Pairvi' in accordance with the Standing Order on the subject. Training: All officers on posting to the DWC will undergo_ a basic Orientation Course for 3 days to be organized by DCP/CAWC in Nanakpura. Thereafter, they shall attend course periodically as and when organized by DCP/CAWC. They will also attend other professional courses as and when -conducted by or nominated by the District DCsP. However, the specialized courses conducted by DCP/CAWC will have precedence in case the timing of both coincide. Close supervision by supervisory officers ACP DWC will discuss the case with the 10 at the first opportunity and guide him in chalking out the plan of investigation. Similarly, after the investigation has been completed but before the challan is prepared another meeting will be held between the 10 and the ACP DWC wherein the ACP will evaluate the evidence on record and give further directions wherever necessary. Specific mention about both these discussions will be made in the Crime Registers of the 10 and the ACP. DCP/CAWC will hold meetings with all the officers of District women cells every month. The progress of enquiry into the complaints and investigation of cases will be reviewed in this meeting. DCP/CAWC will forward his/her observation to Distt. DCP who will take suitable action. The over all supervision of DWC will that of Distt. DCP. Special Intimation the Complainant ACP DWC will send an intimation to the complainant on Annexure C about the investigation having been taken over by the cell. During the course of investigation the 10 must maintain contact with the complainant and keep her informed about the important developments in the case. After the finalization of the case, the result of investigation will be intimated to the complainant on Annexure D. Reports to be send by the District CAWCs to DCP/CAWC. 1. text: STANDINGORDER No. Ops.-lS (Previous Standing Ord.er No. 102/2009) FUNCTIONING OF THE PUBLIC GRIEVANCES CELL 1. GENERAL In order to prevent violation of human rights, enquire into the allegations of its violations and keeping check on corrupt practices, gross misconduct and to look into other complaints by a Delhi ! Policeman a Public Grievances Cell, henceforth to be called as PG Cell, headed by an ACP,has been set up in each Delhi Police Distt .. P.G. Cellwillalso impart training to sensitize the forceto honor human rights and adopt good practices in their day-to-day working, This Cell shall especially deal with the complaints filed by the public with the DCP or to the Cell and pay special attention to the allegations of corruption; gross misconduct and custodial crimeofevery description. 2. LOCATION Asfar as possiblethe ACP,Public Grievances Cellshan be accommodated in the office complex of the District DCP. A prominent board may be put up outside the officeto inform the public about it. 3. STAFFING District, DCsP will ensure sufficient staff for PG Cell and provide all essential facility for its smooth functioning. The selection of staff for PG Cell should be done after careful perusal of their service record. The ACP IJC Cell shall also supervise the functions of Complaints Branch, PunishmentBranch and the Accident Victims Compensation Cellofthe District, DCPofficeshall also function under his supervision. 4. FUNCTIONS Following shall be the important duties of the ACP/PG Cell: (i) To monitor all the complainants coming to the office ofthe DCP or to the Cell with their grievances. (ii) Toconduct enquiries into complaints whereprimafacie evidence of corruption, violation of human rights and gross misconduct on the part of the subordinate officers causing harassment to public are found and submit a report to the DCP. (iii) To monitor the follow-up action on these enquiry reports. (iv) Toconduct traps and sting operations and trap corrupt officers. (v) To also monitor the complaints received in the police stations. (vi) T()ensure timelyreplies/reports upon complaints in which reports are called for by the PHQ and Vigilance Branch. (vii) To monitor the progress of all enquiries in which departmental action is recommended by them. 147 (viii)To monitor the compliance of all Standing Orders/Circular Orders issued on the subjects relating to dealing with public such as Human Rights, making ofarrests, treatment ofarrested persons, summoning .of women to police stations, arrest of women, and to the family of accident victims, etc. and other facilities given to the persons in police custody. . DELHI POLICE STANDING ORDER NO. 10/2018 GUIDELINES FOR ORGANIZING PROTESTS OR DEMONSTRATIONS AT OR NEAR CENTRAL VISTA, INCLUDING JANTAR MANTAR AND BOAT CLUB 1. BACKGROUND The permanent residents of Jantar Mantar Road, New Delhi had filed an O.A. No. 63/2016 seeking relief from the Hon'ble National Green Tribunal and for passing appropriate orders, as Jantar Mantar had become a ground for organizing protests by various categories of groups both political and non-political. It was also averred that the manner .of demonstrations and the occupations of the area are causing noise and air pollution resulting in insurmountable and untold miseries to the residents and adversely affecting the health of the residents and their children. The Hon'ble NGT, after hearing the matter in the Original Application, directed the respandents:- I. To immediately stop all the activities of dhama, protests, agitations, assembling of people, public speeches, using laud speakers, etc. at Jantar Mantar Road, II. To remove all makeshift/temporary structures, loud speakers and public address system from the said stretch of Jantar Mantar Road, III. To remove the garbage/waste lying an the stretch of Jantar Mantar Road and clear the entire area, IV. To shift the protestors, agitators and the people holding dharnas to the alternative site at Ram Leela Maidan, Ajmeri Gate, forthwith, 1 · - I The order of the Hon'ble NGT was subsequently challenged vide Civil Appeal No. 862, 863 & 864 of 2018, on the ground that these directions violate the fundamental right ofthe appellants. While disposing of W.P. (C) No. 1153 of 2017 and the other connected Civil Appeals No. 862, 863 and 864 of 2018, the Hon'ble -- -·--Su-PTerri.~e==-eou-r~vide-i-ts--:order~date-d" -'-23:07-:2018';- ·directed---the-:······ Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, to frame detailed guidelines in consultation with other concerned agencies, and to devise. a proper mechanism for limited use of the area for such purposes but to ensure that demonstrations, etc. are regulated in such a manner that these do not cause any disturbance to the residents of Jantar Mantar Road or the' . offices situated there. The Hori'ble Supreme Court further clarified that a provision can be made for taking requisite prior permission from the Police for holding such demonstrations by a particular group and while examining such proposals, the parameters can be laid down which shall be looked into in order to decide whether the permission is to be granted or not. Accordingly, all concerned agencies including Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India, NDMC, Resident Welfare Associations Jantar Mantar Road were consulted before framing the guidelines as per the directions of the Hon'ble Apex Court. The guidelines, as enumerated hereafter, are being issued in conformity with the letter and spirit of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court ofIndia. 2. PERMISSION FROM COMPETENT AUTHORITY The order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court directs that such public meetings, demonstrations etc. at Jantar Mantar would not be allowed without the written permission from Police. In compliance thereof, the following shall be ensured:- Application addressed to DCP/New Delhi District (NDD)for grant of 1. permission for all protests must be submitted at least 7 days in advance, excluding the day of the event, at the HAX Branch of DCP/NDD Office. Application submitted less than 07 days before the event may also be considered depending on the availability of the space at Jantar Mantar and subject to the condition that sufficient time available for necessary law and order 1S arrange ments. Permission will be granted on 'first-come-first-serve' basis and will 11. be subject to assessment by Special Branch, Traffic Police and New Delhi District Police. DCP/ New Delhi District shall examine the request and take a 111. decision as to whether the proposed demonstration, dhama, public meeting etc. shall be allowed or not, keeping in viewits likely effect viz. whether it would cause any obstruction to traffic or danger to human safety or disturbance to public tranquility etc. The request will be considered and then allowed or rejected keeping in view the aforesaid considerations. DCP/New Delhi District will have the authority to revoke the IV. permission in case of unforeseen and sudden developments such as VIP security requirements or any other intelligence input, and the reasons for revocation shall be duly recorded and conveyed to the organizer(s). v. GUIDELINES FOR ORGANIZING PROGRAMMES AT BOAT CLUB The Hon'ble Supreme Court in its judgement directed that "the Commissioner of Police, New Delhi, and other official respondents can frame proper 'guidelines laying .down the parameters under which permission can be granted in the Boat Club area. It can be a very restrictive and limited use, because of the sensitivities pointed out by the respondents and also keeping in mind that Ramila Maidan is available and Jantar Mantar Road in a regulated manner shall be available as well. Thus, the proposed guidelines may include the. provisions for regulating the numbers of persons intending to participate in such demonstrations, prescribing the minimum distance from the Parliament House, North and South Blocks, Supreme Court, residences of dignitaries etc. within which no such demonstrations would be allowed, imposing restrictions on certain routes where normally the Prime Minister, Central Ministers, Judges etc. pass through; not permitting any demonstrations when foreign dignitaries are visiting a particular place or pass through the particular route; not allowing firearms, lathis, spears, swords, etc. to be carried by demonstrators; not allowing them to bring animals or pitch tents or stay overnight; prescribing time limits for such demonstrations; and placing restrictions on such demonstrations, etc. during peak traffic hours."
